Coplanar transmission line embedded with 48 × 48 um<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> graphene flakes is manufactured through standard microfabrication process and utilized to measure the sheet resistance variation of graphene under external bias voltage. The tuning behavior agrees well with the theoretical model by rigorously solving the Maxwell's equations with the Kubo formula and is of great help for the design of graphene-incorporated switchable devices.

articleTitle: Plasmonic nano-antenna arrays for high-sensitivity and broadband terahertz detection
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a high-performance terahertz detector based on a two-dimensional plasmonic photoconductive nano-antenna array. The nano-antenna array is designed to offer a strong interaction between the incident terahertz radiation and an optical pump beam. This offers significantly higher detection sensitivities compared with non-plasmonic photoconductive antennas. The nano-antennas are also designed to offer broad detection bandwidths. We experimentally demonstrate record-high signal-to-noise ratios as high as 107 dB over 0.1-5 THz frequency range.

articleTitle: Influence of amplitude and phase errors on near-field to far-field transformation
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Due to the influence of environment and multipath effect, the calibration data of spherical near-field antenna measurement are not accurate, which will result in amplitude and phase errors in the near-field to far-field transformation. In order to obtain more accurate antenna radiation pattern, the influence of amplitude and phase errors on the near-field to far-field transformation results are simulated. According to the analysis results, the amplitude and phase errors can be controlled within the tolerable range when the system is designed.

articleTitle: Wideband circularly polarized cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wideband circularly polarized (CP) cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is presented. The DRA is excited in its fundamental HEM11δ mode. A U-shaped slot and a fork-like feed line are used to obtain circularly polarized fields. For demonstration, a prototype operating at 2.4-GHz WLAN band was studied. The reflection coefficient, axial ratio (AR), radiation patterns, antenna gain, and radiation efficiency are simulated and measured, and good agreement between them is observed.

articleTitle: Waveguide-based monopulse wideband travelling-wave array
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel, travelling-wave, waveguide antenna structure with monopulse capability in the two principal planes is proposed with increased frequency bandwidth. The array consists of two interleaved waveguide arrays which provide appropriate excitations to the antenna elements above the waveguide to generate proper sum and difference patterns. With the use of printed antennas and the elimination of the narrow frequency characteristics of the slots on the waveguides, the bandwidth of the array is greatly improved.

articleTitle: Efficient computation of the reflectarray far fields in adaptive grids for speed improvement
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A technique for the efficient computation of the radiation patterns of reflectarray antennas in an adaptive grid for speed improvement is presented. It relies on the use of the Non-Uniform Fast Fourier Transform (NUFFT) to efficiently compute the spectrum functions. This new application of the NUFFT improves computing times and memory usage, with regard to the use of the FFT, for very directive reflectarrays in which a high resolution in the UV grid is needed to correctly characterize the main beam and adjacent secondary lobes.

articleTitle: An updated version of the Dyson Conical Quad-Spiral Array (DYQSA) feed system for VGOS applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of an updated version of the dual polarized ultra wideband feed system for covering the new VGOS (VLBI Global Observation System). This feed system is based on an array version of four elements of the self-complementary conical log spiral antennas. The feed system achieves the VGOS's requirements with operating with high efficiency (> 50%) in a wide bandwidth from 2 GHz to 14 GHz. It provides two attractive characteristics: dual circular polarization compared to dual linear ones in the state of the art solutions and also a real and constant input impedance in the whole operation band.

articleTitle: Austin benchmark suite for computational bioelectromagnetics: AIM performance data
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The adaptive integral method (AIM) is used to solve the basic, moderate, and hard classes of problems in the Austin Benchmark Suite for Computational Bioelectromagnetics. Performance data, including computational costs and errors, are shown for both fast and efficient simulations run on a supercomputer cluster.

articleTitle: 12.6 GHz off-set fed multilayer reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work describes the design of an offset-fed printed microstrip reflectarray with patches of variable sizes. The single element characterization will be provided, which is designed in a multilayer fashion to improve the bandwidth of the manufactured antenna as well as to smooth the phase variation with the patches' size. Taking into account the type of feed available, a 4×4 conventional array, a theoretical analysis for the best feed position is used. Simulation and measured results for a prototyped reflectarray operating at 12.6 GHz is presented.

articleTitle: Experimental validation of a design criterion for UHF ungrounded wearable antennas for RFID applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An antenna design criterion based on the simulated distribution of electric and magnetic energy densities has been proposed to improve the robustness of wearable antennas. A flexible tag characterization and performance evaluation platform is here used to assess the effectiveness of this theoretical approach. Specifically, the analysis has been carried out by considering a single layer UHF RFID tag operating at the ETSI band (865-868 MHz).

articleTitle: Verification of feed spillover reduction using FF-MARS in a CATR using computational electromagnetic simulation
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The Mathematical Absorber Reflection Suppression (MARS) technique is used ordinarily to identify and then suppress effects of spurious scattering within an antenna range measurement. This paper, for the first time, demonstrates by means of computational electromagnetic simulation that MARS can also be used to attenuate feed spillover in an offset parabolic reflector compact antenna test range. Preliminary results are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: A high gain dual-polarised differential rectenna for RF energy harvesting
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A rectenna for radio frequency (RF) energy harvesting is presented in this paper. We introduce a novel technique for RF rectification that is based on differential field sampling and a Greinacher voltage doubler rectifier. The proposed rectification antenna is a dual polarized patch with 4 ports that operates for the WiFi frequency band of 2.4–2.5 GHz and has a gain of 6.75 dB at each port. The proposed novel topology doubles the amount of input power accepted for each polarization and then quadruples the overall output power. In addition we have a differential output voltage source that is typically required for the electronics connected to the harvesting system.

articleTitle: A three-port reconfigurable network for muti-polarization antenna applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A three-port reconfigurable network for muti-polarization antenna applications is presented. Five power routing states (1:0), (0:1), (1:1), (1: j) & (1:-j) is provided with 9 PIN diodes. The high frequency parasitic effect of the PIN diodes involved in impedance matching is accurately considered. Good matching and isolation performance is verified at the design frequency 5.2 GHz by using the co-simulation method of HFSS and ADS.

articleTitle: The importance of antenna near-field losses in intra-body UHF communication applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The gain of the intra-body propagation channel between tissue implanted antennas is largely dependent on the lossy tissue structures on the direct path between the nodes. Nonetheless, intra-body link performance may be improved through careful antenna design to minimize the near-field losses which are doubly important in this application. In an initial study we consider the effect of insulation on an implanted dipole antenna at the MedRadio band (2.36-2.40 GHz) and placed within a muscle tissue phantom. Simulated electric field and radiation efficiency results are discussed for the single antenna case.

articleTitle: User association-based interference management in ultra-dense networks
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: To handle the severe interference in the Ultra-Dense Network scenario, an user association-based interference management scheme is proposed in this paper. By setting up proper regulations and standards, each user equipment (UE) can choose to affiliate with one specific Small Cell Access Point (SAP) among its alternative BS set, with the goal for maximizing the network throughput. Simulation experiments had been carried to evaluate the new scheme's performance by comparing with some classic ones. According to the results, it is believed that the BS's on/off strategy is necessary for the densely deployed network scenarios.

articleTitle: Design of A RFID patch antenna integrated with mercury switches for wireless tilt sensing
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a passive RFID patch antenna for wireless tilt sensing. The shorted patch antenna has a compact structure and low profile, with an overall size of 40 mm × 61.4 mm × 1.57 mm. Loaded with four mercury switches, it can detect five tilt states from two axes according to the resonant frequency of the sensor.

articleTitle: Miniaturized UHF three-element sequential rotation array antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a miniaturized UHF antenna with three sequentially rotated elements operating at 433MHz for Satcom applications. The main body of the antenna is formed by three sequentially rotationally arranged bent Planar Inverted-F Antenna (PIFA) elements, which helps dramatically reduce the size of the antenna. To drive the main body, a new compact feeding network based on spiral shaped Wilkinson power divider is also developed, achieving three-way power splitting and 120° phase shifting. In this way, a sequential rotation array antenna with compact size (Ø0.216λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>), low cost, easy fabrication, and good performance is realized.

articleTitle: Theoretrical derivation of mutual coupling and radiation properties of loop antenna arrays valid from rf to optical
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Circular loop antenna arrays are extremely useful for a wide variety of applications, including geophysical sensing and communications. In the optical regime, these structures are especially useful for solar energy harvesting. One of the most difficult to achieve enabling technologies for these applications is superdirectivity. Rapid design and analysis of these devices requires accurate and efficient calculations for the mutual coupling and radiation properties. Due to the complexity of the integrals involved in the calculations, numerical full-wave solvers are often employed. Unfortunately, these are often time-consuming and memory-intensive. Closed-form analytical solutions would allow the designer to rapidly analyze the radiation characteristics of an array and lead to extremely efficient optimizations. This paper presents straightforward analytical expressions for computing the radiation properties of arrays including the effects of mutual coupling. The theory is general enough to take into account dispersion and loss of materials at optical frequencies. It will be shown that full-wave simulations for a simple 2×1 array of nanoloops can take up to six hours, while the analytical implementations take less than a minute. As an illustrative example, a broadband highly directive array will be optimized and the resulting design will be validated with full-wave simulations.

articleTitle: Bandwidth performance of an antenna array with tapped delay-line and compressive sensing
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper examines the effects of broadband interference on an adaptive antenna array when receiving compressively transmitted data. Transmission of compressive data (at the source) may be desired to reduce data rate, but the interference (broadband or not) and additive noise may not be necessarily compressive measurements. This study examines how an antenna array with tapped-delay line suppresses the interference.

articleTitle: Design of a periodic substrate-integrated-waveguide leaky-wave antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a periodic SIW leaky wave antenna. The design employs transverse slots along the length of the structure. The resulting SIW leaky wave antenna has a 8.9° narrow beam with side lobe level of -11.9dB down. The antenna is fabricated on Roger 5880, measured using the network analyzer, and simulated using CST microwave studio. Experimental measurements are in good agreements with simulation results.

articleTitle: Accurate and efficient simulation of bioelectromagnetic models
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Simulation of bioelectromagnetic problems can be complex, necessitating analysis and benchmarking of the various simulation solutions. Use of different numerical approaches to solve the same problems allows verification of the simulation results.

articleTitle: Markov modeling of spatial variations in multipath
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Multipath effects over small-scale movements are characterized using a finite-state Markov model. Performance of the model is evaluated by comparing statistical behavior of synthesized data with those were taken at 60 GHz inside a reverberation chamber. The proposed method allows multipath behavior prediction for new environments or frequencies in line-of-sight and non-line-of-sight situations.

articleTitle: UHF RFID antenna impedance matching techniques
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The modified T-match network uses planar inductive strips for conjugate matching Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) Integrated Circuits (RFICs). Narrow and broadband matching techniques and electromagnetic simulations are applied in [1] for specific designs. This paper extends these efforts through antenna element parameterization and design trade-off analysis. Narrow and broadband designs are fabricated; antenna input impedance and tag range tests confirm predictions.

articleTitle: Low cross-polarization ultrawideband planar antenna array
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An ultra-wideband planar tightly coupled phased arrays (TCPAs) with extremely low cross polarization is proposed in this paper. Different from previously reported TCPAs, the adjacent elements of the proposed array are not only tightly coupled in current excited direction, but also connected in the orthogonal direction. The infinite array achieves a 5.4:1 bandwidth for VSWR<;3.1: 1 while scanning from -45° to 45° in all planes, with the cross polarization level <; -65 dB along E plane scanning and <; -30 dB along H plane scanning. A prototype for a 10 × 10 planar array was fabricated and measured, and reasonable agreement with the simulation results is obtained.

articleTitle: Computations of electromagnetic wave scattering using FEM-BEM-DDM with H-matrices
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The nonconformal domain decomposition method (DDM) of the hybrid finite element-boundary element(BEM) with FETI (finite element tearing and interconnecting) like algrithm and multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) are presented for computing large electromagnetic scattering problems in this paper. Due to the Robin-type transmission conditions, it is possible to employ nonconformal interface discretizations of the targets. We speed up the solution process by reducing the unkowns by adopting the thought of FETI, leading to sevaral dense FEM inverse matrices. H-Matrices is introduced into this method to reduce memory consumption, when faced with plenty of sub-domains. Furthermore, MLFMA is applied to improve the efficiency of computing technique. Accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method are demonstrated through several numerical experiments.

articleTitle: Broadband circularly polarized square slot antenna with a G-shaped feedline
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of a compact circularly polarized square slot antenna fed by a G-shaped strip feedline. The 3-dB axial ratio (AR) band can be achieved by simply extending the feedline with a G-shaped monopole. To extend the AR bandwidth achieved by the G-patch, perturbations in the form of a U-strip and an L-shaped slot are introduced in the wide slot and ground plane respectively. Measured results showed a wide 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 37.1% (4.5-6.55 GHz) and an impedance bandwidth of 70.1% (3.32-6.95 GHz). The proposed antenna is suitable for wideband circular polarization applications in the IEEE C-band.

articleTitle: Analytical study of the TE-waveguide modes in time domain
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The problem of propagation is solved for circular waveguide TE-modal waveforms within the framework of the evolutionary approach to electrodynamics (EAE). Physical dimensions of the electric and magnetic intensity vectors, volt per meter and ampere per meter, ingressed in Maxwell's equations are factorized in SI units. Then a system of evolutionary equations for the modal amplitudes dependent on axial coordinate and time are obtained from the Maxwell's equations supplemented with the boundary conditions for perfect electric conductor surfaces. Solutions for the waveguide modal fields and for the energetic field characteristics are presented graphically.

articleTitle: Compact implantable MIMO antenna with electromagnetic band gaps
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact four-unit MIMO antenna operating in the 2.45-GHz ISM band for implantable applications is proposed. Two radiators are integrated on the same antenna, and each radiator is shared by two antenna elements, greatly reducing the overall size of the implantable MIMO system. High isolation between two antenna elements is achieved by etching a “+”-shaped slot in the radiator, extending a stub on the ground and embedding two electromagnetic band gaps (EBG) between the radiator and the ground. The proposed MIMO antenna has a dimension of 18.5 × 18.5 × 1.27 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The simulated impedance bandwidths are 18.64% (2.14–2.58 GHz). The simulated maximum mutual coupling is below −15.99 dB at ISM band. The envelope correlation coefficient has been researched and the results indicate the independence between the antenna elements.

articleTitle: Back radiation suppression through a semi-transparent round ground plane for a mm-Wave monopole antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Omnidirectional radiation pattern with minimum backward radiation is highly desirable for millimeter-wave telecommunication antennas. In this work, we propose a round, semitransparent ground plane of radius 0.8λ with uniform impedance distribution that can reduce the back radiation of a monopole antenna by 8.8 dB as compared with a similar sized metallic ground plane. The value of uniform impedance is obtained through analytical optimization by using asymptotic expressions in the Kirchhoff approximation of the radiation pattern of a toroidal wave scattered by a round semitransparent ground plane. The semitransparent ground plane has been realized using a low-cost carbon paste on a Kapton film. Experimental results match closely with those of simulations and validate the overall concept.

articleTitle: Magnetic-thermal co-simulation of nonlinear magnetic materials at high frequencies
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A coupled magnetic-thermal solver is developed for the modeling and simulation of nonlinear magnetic materials. By adopting a temperature-dependent dynamic hysteresis model, the magnetic loss is characterized and calculated from the solution of Maxwell's equations, which serves as the heat source in the thermal problem. By solving the thermal problem, the temperature shift is obtained and its effect on the magnetic material property can be quantified, which is then coupled back to Maxwell's equations. The resulting coupled magnetic-thermal system can be solved for both the electromagnetic fields and the temperature, and hence, account for both the electromagnetic and the thermal responses in a high-frequency operation.

articleTitle: HIBiscus, a broadband antenna with matching impedance and uniform radiation pattern
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Global 21-cm spectrum observations in the Very High Frequency (VHF) range require broadband antennas with frequency independent pattern and excellent match across an octave. The simulation package FEKO was used to create a new design with the characteristics needed, and the geometry was iteratively improved and verified by testing scale models in an anechoic chamber. The final design was constructed at full size and used with success on the experiment.

articleTitle: Invisible near-field probes at infrared frequencies based on impedance engineering at the nanoscale
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Near-field probes are becoming a fundamental tool in optical imaging, for applications spanning from biology and medical research to nanophotonics. The scattering from these probes, however, perturbs the electromagnetic fields under study, distorting the resulting images. A solution to this issue was proposed based on covering the probe with suitable plasmonic materials. However, since materials having specific properties are often not available at the required frequency, we propose here an alternative general technique to suppress the probe's scattering, without the need for plasmonic or metamaterial shells. In particular, we propose to control the response of an aperture-type probing tip working at infrared frequencies by directly carving suitable slits on its aluminum cover (feasible with current nanotechnology). The slits act as transmission lines for the incident field, and allow controlling the impedance of the nano-object. Our numerical results show that this method allows drastically suppressing the dipolar polarizability, and therefore the dipolar scattering, of the probe. As a relevant example, we show that the modified tip perturbs much less the resonant fields of a nanophotonic cavity, while still being able to measure the field distribution. These results may have important practical impact for optical imaging and nano-electromagnetics.

articleTitle: On the singular spectrum of the radiation operator in near reactive zone
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper the problem of studying the spectrum of the radiation operator in near reactive zone is addressed. This topic is of great importance because of its connection with the so-called Number of Degrees of Freedom concept which is a key parameter in inverse source problems. The case of a bounded rectilinear magnetic source with the radiated field observed over unbounded rectilinear domain parallel to the source is considered.

articleTitle: Innovative optimization-based design of UWB planar arrays for grating lobes reduction
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: UWB planar phased arrays with inter-element spacing greater than half-wavelength suffer from the presence of grating lobes in the radiation pattern. An innovative approach to mitigate this problem, based on the optimization of the array elements positions along the broadside direction (z-direction) is presented. The main innovation of the proposed new design methodology is related to the fact that the positions of the array elements are left unchanged in the xy-plane, thus not affecting the planar dimension of the array aperture. Selected numerical results are shown to validate the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Remote reconstruction of dielectric objects based on the extrapolation of limited observation data
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Conventional diffraction tomography (DT) can be used to reconstruct objects under a full view. However, solving inverse problem could be challenging when the full angle data is not available. In this article, a novel diffraction tomographic algorithm with extrapolation method is proposed to detect two-dimensional (2D) dielectric objects in the case that the observation stations are far away from the search domain and the observation angles are limited. Extrapolation is introduced to obtain more data in the frequency domain. Using this algorithm, all locations, shapes, and dielectric properties of targets can be reconstructed under 90° observation angle. Due to the use of fast Fourier transforms in the implementation, this algorithm is very fast although there are many iterations of extrapolation. Images can be reconstructed with nearly real time performance. Numerical examples are given to show the validity of the algorithm.

articleTitle: A novel wide-band MIMO antenna system for smart phones
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, a novel wide-band, planar, multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna system is proposed. The MIMO antenna system consists of 4 monopole antenna elements. It is covering different 4G wireless standard bands between 1900-3300 MHz and 3559-3822 MHz in addition to the WLAN 2450 MHz with a single continuous wide band of 1.4 GHz. The MIMO antenna system is fabricated on a commercially available RO4350 substrate with ϵ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> equal to 3.5. The dimensions of the board are equal to 115 × 65 × 0.76 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> which is a typical back plane size of a smart phone. The proposed design is efficient, compact and low profile. MIMO performance metrics such as envelope correlation coefficient and isolation are calculated and good agreement is observed between simulated and measured values.

articleTitle: An all textile H-plane SIW horn antenna with metameterial absorber for millimeter-wave WBAN applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An all textile H-plane SIW horn antenna for millimeter-wave WBAN applications is proposed. A coaxially fed SIW H-plane horn is designed for radiation toward the human body surface. In order to mitigate the degenerations caused by the interactions between the antenna and human body, a metamaterial absorber is attached in front of the aperture of horn. All components mentioned above are made of textile materials. The simulated 10-dB return loss bandwidth is 2980 MHz (26.44 GHz-29.42 GHz) which covers a potential candidate frequency band of 5G communication. The simulated results show that the proposed antenna has a directional radiation pattern toward body surface with a gain of 3.94 dBi and has the maximum gain of 9.19 dBi at 9 = 35° on the 28 GHz skin-equivalent phantom.

articleTitle: The shape optimisation of closely-spaced electrically-small antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A shape synthesis method for single electrically-small antennas that does not require specification of the feedpoint location prior to shaping is extended to the case of closely-spaced antennas that operate at different frequencies.

articleTitle: On the backscattering from RFID tags installed on vehicular glasses
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper discusses the application of power budget link in RFID systems with tags installed on vehicular windshield with polarized films. The performance of three tags on glasses with polarizing films and a circular polarized antenna is studied using full wave simulations and measurements. It is found that the mismatch effect due to the change impedance of the RFID antenna when the tag is placed on the windshield presents the main contribution in the budget losses and is the main responsible of the reading range reduction.

articleTitle: An overview of low profile miniaturized antennas for low frequency applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an overview of recent advancements in theory and design of low-profile miniaturized antennas that can radiate purely vertical polarization is presented. Low profile antennas are desired for mobile platforms to reduce visibility and air drag. Also for operation in near ground communication at low VHF and HF bands, vertical polarization is highly desirable considering much higher path-loss for horizontally polarized wave propagation. In this paper designs and principles of operations of three different low-profile antennas with vertical polarization are presented.

articleTitle: Rotationally tunable frequency selective surfaces for large areas via linkage mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In the past decades, frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) have been widely used for providing desired frequency responses in microwave and optical frequencies. Various tuning techniques have been investigated to switch or continuously tune the frequency responses based on the needs in certain circumstances. However, it's still challenging to alter each unit of the FSS synchronously which results in slight differences in terms of phase and magnitude of the frequency response of each unit. Therefore, the goal of this research is to develop a large-area mechanically tunable FSS by uniformly controlling the frequency response of each unit cell. In this research, we propose a rocker-linkage based rotational FSS and its frequency response can be tuned synchronously. Each unit cell is composed of a square loop and several of them are attached to a rotating cylindrical connecting link in a row. They are connected by rocker linkages forming the whole structure. By actuating the driving link via a linear actuator or motor, each unit cell rotates synchronously and changes its frequency response simultaneously. A prototype with a dimension of 14 by 14 unit cells was designed, fabricated, and examined with field tests. It was demonstrated that the resonant frequency of the stop-band shifted to the high frequency with a maximum value of 0.9 GHz (14% in terms of fractional bandwidth). Since the proposed linkage-based rotational FSSs do not require any electronic components, it has a higher microwave-power-handling capability compared to the commonly-used electronic tunable FSSs.

articleTitle: Substrate integrated waveguide slotted antenna array with amplitude weighting and integrated monopulse feed
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 20×12 substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) slotted antenna array is introduced that has amplitude weighting in both the horizontal and vertical dimensions and is equipped to make angle measurements in both azimuth and elevation directions. A SIW monopulse feed structure is embedded within the combiner substrate and feeds the four SIW antenna quadrants from the backside of the array. Amplitude weighting is achieved in the azimuth direction by varying the radiating slot offset from the centerline, while the elevation amplitude weighting is achieved through a series of SIW sidewall couplers integrated into the antenna face. The resulting design and measured results demonstrate a low profile, low-loss, passive antenna array capable of accurate angle measurement in target tracking applications.

articleTitle: An end-to-end optimization approach to drastically reduce cross-polarization in offset mmWave reflector antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: High cross-polarization is a well-known issue for offset reflectors, especially designs with low F/D ratios. In this paper, we explore the possibility in using spline-profiled horns to create a feed aperture distribution reducing reflector cross-polarization. We optimize two smooth-walled, spline-profiled horn designs to lower the reflector cross-polarization, where one design has a set of pins optimized to excite higher-order modes. The design with pins is able to dramatically reduce the cross-polarization to levels less than -45 dB. Furthermore, the design can be fabricated with a 2-axis CNC lathe and radial hole postprocessing.

articleTitle: A 2D FDFD eigenmode method with edge singularity correction and conformal technique
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 2D FDFD eigenmode method with edge singularity correction and conformal technique is presented. The presented method takes the conducting edge field singularity into account and it is combined with the conformal method to handle more complex conducting objects. The numerical experiments showed that the presented method is more accurate than the conventional method.

articleTitle: Extracting surface impedance method for an anisotropic polygon unit cell
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: One patterning technique, the point shifting method, has enabled generating smoothly varying, and highly anisotropic impedance surfaces with a wide range of patch sizes and shapes. Previously the surface impedances of each different shape of unit cell were assumed by the impedance of similar size rectangular cells. In this work, we studied an approach to calculate more accurate surface impedances for anisotropic polygon unit cells, based on the moment of inertia equations. The method is verified by simulations.

articleTitle: Quantum light rectification in nano-rectennas
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces the paradigm of quantum light rectification by nano-rectennas. The theory is based on the synthesis of the quantum-optical light description and the scattering-matrix approach to phase-coherent electron transport in rectifying diodes (Landauer-Buttiker concept). The dc-current operator is expressed in terms of the special functions of the normally ordered electronic and photonic creation-annihilation operators. The observable dc-current is calculated as an expectation value of the current operator with respect to both electronic and light components of the rectenna state. Potential applications of the developed theory to the solar power conversion into the dc-current are discussed.

articleTitle: A novel analytic beam steering approach for clustered phased array architectures
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The synthesis of the sub-array phases for multi-beams scanning applications is here addressed. A hybrid analog/digital architecture is considered in which analog element excitations are used to generate a reference beam, while a digital sub-arrayed beam-forming network (BFN) is used for steering a secondary beam within a limited scan cone. The digital phases are obtained through an innovative analytic method, jointly optimized with the sub-arrays configuration. A simple numerical assessment has been reported to validate the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Optimized dual-linear polarization frequency scanning microstrip array antenna for cylindrical polarimetric phased array radar (CPPAR)
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design and simulation results of an optimized dual linear polarization frequency scanning microstrip antenna for CPPAR are presented. The antenna radiation pattern has been optimized to have matched horizontal and vertical polarization pointing angles at 2.8 GHz. The simulation results show that the beam pointing angle mismatch in the optimized antenna is less than 0.18° from 2.75 GHz to 2.85 GHz and is approximately 0.04° at 2.8 GHz, which are acceptable for weather measurement applications.

articleTitle: Single-bit compressive imaging system for the mmW and THz bands
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present, a novel 64 × 64-pixel imaging system utilizing a low-cost single-bit comparator sensor and a compressive sensing algorithm for mmW and THz bands. To validate the proposed methodology, a photoexcited high-resistivity Silicon wafer is used as the spatial light modulator and a 2-port vector network analyzer is used as the source-receiver pair. Recording only the “sign” of the measured signal, the proposed approach can reconstruct 4K-pixel image of the scene using only 1,024 measurements at 690 GHz.

articleTitle: SIGW dual level H-plane horn antenna for millimeter waves
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The modified configuration of substrate integrated H-plane horn is presented which is very versatile that enables the horn to have a thin thickness of its planar feed line while having a thick radiating aperture at millimeter wave frequencies. This configuration is based on substrate integrated gap waveguide (SIGW) technology in which the propagating printed ridge is separated with the periodic structure. In this design, the level of the separated ridge has the same thickness of the thin microstrip feeding. The upper level is coupled with a transition to the lower level which is integrated with periodic structure.

articleTitle: A dual-band dual-polarization antenna using unequal crossed slots on metallic cavity
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a design for a dual-band slotted cavity antenna with its bands having orthogonal polarizations in a shared aperture. The design and its simulated performance is presented at X-band, which is typical of many satellite radar applications, such as MDA's pending RADARSAT synthetic aperture constellation. The presented antenna comprises a 2×2 array of crossed-slots which have unequal arm lengths, cut on a rectangular metallic cavity and fed by a crossed waveguide feed. This design demonstrates (by simulation) an impedance bandwidth close to 10% for both frequency bands with an overall isolation between the ports better than 30dB. A directivity of 12 dBi was obtained in both polarizations, which corresponds to aperture efficiencies of 73% and 46% for the lower and higher frequency bands respectively. This antenna can be considered as a sub-array for larger array realizations.

articleTitle: Windmill clutter mitigation using active meta-surfaces
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Windmill clutter mitigation using active meta-surfaces is introduced. The active meta-surfaces are smart metamaterial whose elements are loaded with tunable lumped elements. Using the Gaussian white noise as the control signal, the reflecting signal of the meta-surface would act like noise which makes the radar receiver very hard to detect. The concept and simple simulation are shown to show that the wind turbine clutter can be mitigated and bring no harm to air surveillance radar.

articleTitle: A miniaturized frequency selective surface by using vias to connect spiral lines and square patches
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a new miniaturized frequency selective surface (FSS) structure is proposed. Compared with previous FSSs, the proposed structure has promising miniaturization features. The array element is implemented by using vias to connect structures on two surface layers. The dimensions of the proposed array element are only 0.035λ×0.035λ. The top layer is constructed by four spiral-shaped structures; the bottom is made of four square-shaped patches. They are connected in series by vias. In so doing, the values of the resonant component values are increased; thus the resonant frequency is shifted downwards. The frequency response is insensitive to the oblique incidence angle. Also, the proposed design is symmetric rotationally on the xy (the surface) plane and can be applied for circular polarization applications.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave amplification based on dispersion engineered intraband photonic transitions
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Intraband electronic transitions are the fundamental quantum effect underpinning Drude conductivity in solid state materials. In electromagnetic or photonic structures, periodic space-time variation in the permitivity of the structure can be used to generate analogous transitions. In non-dispersive or weakly dispersive systems, this effect generates many undesirable harmonics. This paper introduces the idea of applying dispersion engineering to effectively control the process of intraband photonic transition. It is shown that this effect leads to electromagnetic wave amplification in a properly engineered dispersive system. Such structures may find applications in low-noise amplifier-mixers and magnetless nonreciprocal systems.

articleTitle: A compact broadband circularly polarized WSS antenna for future 5G communication systems
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a small broadband circularly polarized square slot antenna for future 5G communication systems. The proposed antenna has a compact size of 5.5×5.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and consists of a wide square slot (WSS) and a T-shaped stub in the ground plane. The WSS structure is fed through a microstrip transmission line designed on the other side of the substrate. Symmetric and asymmetric fractals are made with in the WSS structure to achieve wide CP bandwidth. The impedance and 3dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of the proposed antenna is 72.15% (21.6-41.8 GHz) and is 67.17% (25.69-44.5 GHz) respectively. The simulated peak gain of 4.85 dBic is achieved with in the AR band.

articleTitle: A simulation model of correlated shadow fading in ultra dense networks
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Correlated shadow fading model plays a key role in mobility management of mobile communication systems. For the 5th generation mobile communication systems (5G), due to the densely-deployed base stations, the accuracy and computational complexity of conventional shadow fading simulation model cannot meet the simulation requirements in 5G. A more accurate shadow fading model with a low computational complexity is proposed in this paper. The bilinear interpolation algorithm is used to enhance the accuracy of the proposed model. According to the characteristics of 5G ultra dense networks, only the necessary shadow fading map is stored to reduce the memory cost. The accuracy and efficiency of the proposed model is validated by extensive simulation results.

articleTitle: Topological approach to the design of terahertz circuits
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this contribution, we showed that cyclotron resonance of semiconductors can be utilized in Topological Insulator-based devices to break the time-reversal symmetry for one-way edge modes propagation in THz frequency range. To demonstrate the concept, we proposed a tunable power splitter based on Topological Insulator.

articleTitle: Integrated calibration noise coupler for room temperature SKA band 1 feed system
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents design of a novel coupler for the injection of calibration signal into the RF path of the SKA Band 1 quad-ridged flared horn, covering frequencies from 350-1050 MHz. The coupler is integrated in the feed horn and provides a coupling factor of -35 dB. The calibration signal is injected before the first amplification stage, without any degradation in the noise performance of the room temperature system.

articleTitle: Tiling optimization of orthogonal-polygon shaped aperture for phased array antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents an innovative tiling optimization strategy for arbitrary orthogonal-polygon shaped apertures. An exhaustive search approach, together with a multi-objective strategy, has been used in order to obtain optimal tiling configurations, jointly optimizing two different pattern features of interest. A simple example validating the proposed method has been finally reported.

articleTitle: An ellipse-shaped with slanted slot circularly polarized monopole antenna for UHF RFID readers
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An ellipse-shaped circularly polarized (CP) monopole antenna is proposed in this paper. A slanted slot is added into the antenna to enhance 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth. The antenna operates at ultrahigh frequency (UHF) band for radio-frequency identification (RFID) reader applications. The measured bandwidth of standing wave ratio (SWR) <; 2 is 535 MHz (553 MHz-1088 MHz) and the measured 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth 45MHz (900MHz-945MHz). The size of the radiating element is 137 mm × 122 mm.

articleTitle: Pedagogical construction of a green's function from physical consideration
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: By invoking an elementary problem in electrostatics, the Green's function for the Poisson's equation in one dimension is obtained from physical principles. Simple in mathematical form, the physical implications of the function can readily be drawn from its graphical appearance, while the consequence of the singular nature of the source that gives rise to the electric field and the corresponding potential function can readily be recognized. Relation of the Green's function for bounded domain to that in infinite space can be seen by receding the boundary to infinity. A series representation of the function can be obtained by augmenting it to form a periodic function, followed by series expansion of the latter. The discussion borne out by this development can provide an early exposure to the concept of the Green's function that brings forth physical insight. Knowledge of ordinary differential equation and Fourier series is sufficient to comprehend the discussion.

articleTitle: A depolarizing chipless RFID tag with quasi-loop resonators
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel depolarizing chipless RFID tag with quasi-loop resonators is presented. A set of resonators, similar to the concentric loops, are employed in the structure of the proposed chipless tag. Each resonator is composed of a pair of inverted L-shaped microstrips with short horizontal stubs at one end. Due to the layout of resonant elements, a compact dimension of 2.1 cm × 2.2 cm with four resonant peaks in the frequency band from 4 to 9.5 GHz is obtained. A reliable frequency shift encoding (FSE) is realized even though the coupling effect exists between the resonators. The frequency shift encoding enables each resonant element to represent 3.9-bit digital information. Furthermore, the designed chipless tag possesses depolarizing characteristic, increasing the reliability of detection in a harsh environment full of multi-path reflections.

articleTitle: Dielectric resonator antenna: A solution for its mount on metallic body
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In a Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA), conventionally glue or adhesive is used to fix the ceramic DRA block onto the antenna Ground Plane (GP) made of a metallic sheet. In this work a new compound ground plane has been conceived. This serves as a GP for the DRA as well as a holding structure. This technique replaces the adhesive or glue. The design has been made in such a way that no characteristics and radiation pattern of the antenna are disturbed. A full metallic configuration, suitable for practical purposes has been suggested in this work. The proposed configuration shows expected broadside radiation and ~ 6 dBi gain, with agreeable co-polar to cross-polar isolation. Finally, a prototype has been fabricated and experimentally studied. The measurement results corroborate the simulated data.

articleTitle: The calibration of Ray tracer based on indoor office measurement at 28 GHz
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the calibration procedure of Ray tracing simulator (RT) is introduced and channel characteristics are studied based on the measurement in the NYU indoor office scenario in the millimeter wave (mm-Wave) band. 3D scenario model of the office is constructed and the dielectric parameters of the indoor materials are calibrated iteratively. The error between RT simulation result and the measured data reduces from 5.49 dB to 0.98 dB. More simulations are realized by using the RT with the calibrated material parameters and the path loss exponent (PLE) of CI model is fitted. Compared with the PLE of measurement, the error is 0.1. Therefore, the calibration is validated and the RT can be used to analyze more channel characteristics and guide communication system design.

articleTitle: Electrically-small, low-profile, dual-linear and circularly polarized huygens dipole antennas with broadside radiation patterns
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Electrically-small, low-profile, broadside-radiating Huygens dipole antennas are reported that have high radiation efficiencies and are either dual-linear (LP) or circularly (CP) polarized. The Huygens behavior, i.e., a high front-to-back ratio, is realized by exciting two complementary electric and magnetic dipole radiators, simultaneously having the same amplitude and phase. To achieve this design, we modified the electrically-small near-field resonant parasitic (NFRP) Egyptian axe dipole (EAD) antenna to act as the electric radiator and the capacitively loaded loop (CLL) NFRP antenna to act as the magnetic radiator. By organically combining the crossed EAD and CLL NFRP elements together with proper excitations by a pair of driven dipole elements, the resulting electrically small antenna generates broadside Huygens radiation patterns with either dual-LP or CP characteristics. They have ka = 0.87; are low-profile, ~0.04λ exhibit good radiation performance with 4.54 dBi LP and 4.58 dBic CP peak realized gains; have > 20 dB front-to-back ratios; and have > 93.9% radiation efficiencies at their resonant frequencies. These antenna systems are quite suitable for narrow bandwidth applications including, e.g., wireless power transfer (WPT) to charge batteries in wireless sensors, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), and other compact portable devices.

articleTitle: Fabrication and measurements of a low-cost, dual-polarized advanced planar array with wide scanning coverage
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Specialized narrowband planar arrays are attractive for radar, narrowband communication and SATCOM due to the ease of integration of the radiators with electronics. However, the cost of phased array technology remains prohibitive for direct insertion in some applications when compared to traditional mechanically steered arrays. To address this issue, this paper describes the manufacturing and measurements of a low-cost, planar, and monolithic printed circuit board array operating in the S-Band (2.7-2.9GHz) with an active VSWR <; 2.2 up to scanning angles up of +/-50° from broadside. Scan loss is also kept very low (n <; 1.2). An 8×8 planar array was fabricated and its impedance and array patterns were measured.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave computational interferometric radiometer
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work is focused on the conception of a new kind of mm-wave radiometer based on a computational imaging technique. The aim is the design of a radiating aperture associated with a dispersive component able to passively multiplex the received signals, allowing for a massive simplification of the active part in comparison with conventional solutions. This approach also requires the implementation of fast algorithms for retrieving the coded signals and reconstruct images of the target, desirably at the speed of several frames per second.

articleTitle: Isogeometric analysis of EM scattering on multiply-connected subdivision surfaces
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Isogeometric analysis (IGA) has been implemented to solve the electric field integral equation (EFIE) on simply-connected subdivision surfaces (Li et al., J. Comput. Phys., 319, 145-162, 2016) using a Helmholtz decomposition. This paper will present a method of moments within the framework of IGA on more complicated (mainly multiply-connected) subdivision surfaces by developing div-conforming basis sets. Furthermore, we will examine h-refinement to study the super-convergence behavior of the numerical scheme used to discretize the the EFIE.

articleTitle: Design of 2 by 2 dual-polarized antenna array with high isolation, wideband and low cross polarization
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 2 ×2 dual-polarized aperture-coupled microstrip antenna array with high isolation, broadband and low cross polarization is proposed for X-band radar systems. Two orthogonal 4-way corporate (parallel) feed networks are placed on the opposite sides of ground, which not only has a multistage structure with broadband but also provides equal amplitude and reversed phase outputs. A perforated metal plate is employed to suppress the cross polarization by blocking the radiation from feed networks. The simulation results show that the dual-polarized array exhibits an impedance bandwidth of 19.8% for vertical port and 16.7% for horizontal port. The cross polarization level is better than −33dB in E plane and −32dB in H plane, and the isolation between ports is above 35dB.

articleTitle: Circuit analysis of the stability of a two-element non-foster impedance matching network
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We study a non-Foster impedance match network whose topology is a formal inverse of the reactance of a Chu TM10 mode impedance. The network has a two negative elements: a negative series capacitor facing the load and a negative shunt inductor facing a resistance-terminated port or source. By circuit analysis, we determine explicit conditions on the negative elements for the network to be stable. Importantly, we show that one condition cannot be satisfied. It is conjectured that non-Foster circuits having multiple negative elements have a severe restriction on their topologies in order to be stable: every negative lumped reactance must have an adjacent positive “swamping” element. If more general topologies without swamping elements are desired, the method of bandpass negative elements holds promise.

articleTitle: A novel circular patch antenna of generating vortex beams based on complex transformation optics
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Generation of vortex beam carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM) is a popular field of research in recent years. Based on the theory of complex transformation optics, a standing-wave current distribution along the circumference of a conventional circular patch is transformed into a uniform traveling current distribution instead, thus leading to the generation of vortex beams. Compared to the other designs of generating vortex beams, our design takes a patch antenna as a single radiator, thus, it has incomparable advantage in the compact structure.

articleTitle: A systematic software-based radar system simulation method
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: With the increasing complexity of modern radar system and the increasing number of devices used in the radar system, it would be highly desirable to model the complete radar system including hardware and software by a single tool. This paper presents a novel software-based simulation method for modern radar system which here is automotive radar application. Various functions of automotive radar, like target speed, distance and azimuth and elevation angle detection, are simulated in test case and the simulation results are compared with the measurement results.

articleTitle: 3D modeling of BAW-based multiferroic antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The thin-film multiferroic bulk-acoustic-wave (BAW) antennas consisting of piezoelectric and magneto-elastic materials are modeled. The effect of ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) on the radiation efficiency is demonstrated. As the applied in-plane magnetic DC field aligns the FMR frequency of the magneto-elastic layer with that of the BAW resonance of the structure, peaks in radiation efficiency are observed. Benchmark against the conventional dipole antenna and Chu's limit validates the advantage of the multiferroic antennas. This work represents the first three-dimensional investigation in magneto-elastic coupling based thin-film multiferroic antennas for potential applications in electrically small antennas.

articleTitle: Wideband high gain circularly polarized Fabry-Perot Resonator antenna with asymmetric superstrates
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A method of using multiple dielectric slabs with small-footprint to design wideband circularly polarized Fabry-Perot Resonator antenna is presented. This approach employed two thin truncated dielectric slabs as partially reflecting surface (PRS) with positive reflection phase gradient, which can significantly improve the 3-dB gain as well as axial ratio (AR) bandwidths of the antenna. The proposed design with the very compact size of 1.5 × 1.5 × 0.7 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> yielded impedance matching, and axial ratio bandwidths are approximately 63.3% and 48.1%, respectively. Additionally, the proposed antenna achieved a 3-dB gain bandwidth of 58.8% with a peak gain of 15 dBi.

articleTitle: Mixed quadratic model for peak spatial-average SAR of coherent multiple antenna devices
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) is a measure of the electromagnetic exposure of portable devices imposed by regulatory agencies. In this paper, we model peak spatial-average SAR of multiple-antenna portable devices using a simple mixed quadratic function of the transmitted vector signal. The model takes into account the movement of location on peak SAR as the transmitted signal varies in amplitude and relative phase between antennas, and can be applied to any number of antennas. Examples with two and four antennas are presented.

articleTitle: A multimode wideband dual-polarized antenna based on stub-loaded dipoles
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a multimode wideband dual-polarized antenna based on stub-loaded dipoles is proposed for 2G/3G bands. Its radiator consists of two pairs of dipoles loaded with stubs. By loading the stub to a straight dipole, a new adjustable resonant mode is formed and combines with the primal resonant mode of the dipole to obtain a wide impedance bandwidth. Two pairs of coplanar striplines (CPSs) are used to feed the radiators. Measurement shows that the antenna achieves an impedance bandwidth of 25.6% with SWR<;1.5 (1.7 to 2.2 GHz) and a high isolation of greater than 27 dB within the bandwidth. Also, a stable radiation pattern with half-power beamwidth of 65±4.2 degree at horizontal plane and a stable gain of 8.1±0.8 dBi are obtained over the operating frequency band.

articleTitle: Diplexer integration into a Ka-band high-gain gap waveguide corporate-fed slot array antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A multilayer integrated diplexer-antenna array module for Ka-band high capacity point-to-point backhaul links is presented. The proposed module is composed of three unconnected metal layers with a simple mechanical assembly and no electrical contact requirements between the distinct layers based on gap waveguide technology. A 7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order hybrid diplexer-splitter with a novel architecture is successfully integrated into a ridge gap waveguide corporate distribution network of a 16 × 16 slot array antenna. The measured input reflection coefficients for both Tx/Rx channels are below -13 dB with measured total efficiency better than 60% in the designed passband. The measured isolation of gain between the two channels is more than 55 dB.

articleTitle: A compact cavity-backed monopole antenna for UWB applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new directive ultra wideband (UWB) antenna using a cavity-backed monopole is presented. This compact, broadband, and high-gain antenna consists of a triangular-shaped monopole radiating element along with a tapered cavity. The proposed design uses two pairs of shorting lines to improve radiation pattern consistency at higher frequencies and a tapered cavity to enhance the gain and impedance bandwidth of the antenna. Electromagnetic simulations show an impedance bandwidth with voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) < 2 from 3.0 GHz to 14.5 GHz (133%) and a gain greater than 6 dBi from 3.0 GHz to 10.8 GHz (113%) with a peak of 10.8 dBi. The proposed antenna is relatively compact with overall dimensions of 0.65λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l</inf> × 0.32λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l</inf> × 0.18λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l</inf>, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l</inf> is the free-space wavelength of the lowest operating frequency.

articleTitle: Stacked shorted circular patch antenna in SIW technology for 60-GHz band arrays
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact high-gain stacked multi-layered antenna in SIW technology for array at 60GHz band is proposed. A single radiator composed by a shorted circular patch with a stacked element is studied in order to fulfil the desired performances. The simulated stacked antenna attains 9.1dBi of maximum gain and 10% of impedance bandwidth with a size of 3.75 × 3.75 × 2.94 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The proposed antenna is an excellent candidate for integrated low-cost millimetre-wave array systems.

articleTitle: Controllable angular scattering with a bianisotropic metasurface
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose the concept of a bianisotropic meta-surface with controllable angular scattering. We illustrate this concept with the synthesis and the analysis of a metasurface exhibting controllable absorption and transmission phase as function of the incidence angle.

articleTitle: Axial and circumferential modulation on cylindrical metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Sinusoidal impedance modulation is performed along the axis and the circumference of cylindrical leaky wave antennas (LWAs). The radiation characteristics of the axially modulated cylindrical metasurfaces are compared to those of the circumferentially modulated ones. The reduction in the peak gain and the increase in the half power beamwidth, of the radiated fan beam with respect to the curvature, are observed to be more significant for the case of circumferentially modulated cylindrical LWAs.

articleTitle: Offset fed planar inverted L antenna with built-in coplanar waveguide
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The offset fed planar inverted L antenna with built-in coplanar waveguide is proposed and numerically analyzed. The antenna characteristics of proposed antenna are almost same as those of the offset fed planer inverted L antenna. It is shown that the offset feed is easily realized by the built-in coplanar waveguide.

articleTitle: Planar endfire circularly polarized antenna with unidirectional radiation
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A single-layer single-fed endfire antenna with circular polarization and unidirectional radiation for X-band applications is proposed. The design is based upon two complementary Yagi-Uda arrays and the series feeding technique. Simulated results confirm a usable bandwidth (the common overlapped bandwidth limited by the 3-dB AR and -10-dB |S11|) of 1.0% can be achieved. At 10 GHz, the gain is 7.23 dBic and the front-to-back ratio is 14.45 dB. The overall antenna size is 1.05λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>×0.65λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> while the profile is only 0.026λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>.

articleTitle: Low-cost 60 GHz 3D printed lens fed by a planar source with WR15 transition integrated on FR4 PCB
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present in this paper a cost-effective, high-gain V-band lens antenna system. The lens is illuminated by a planar antenna integrated on standard FR4 PCB along with a built-in connector using a fin-line microstrip-to-waveguide transition (enabling WR15 waveguide connection). The lens has an elliptical dome-type design destined to be manufactured in ABS plastic using 3D printing. The proposed antenna solution achieves high gain (> 28 dBi) in V band (57-66 GHz) and targets low-cost backhaul links that will be required in 5G small cells.

articleTitle: Design and integration of high precision GPS/GNSS antennas for modern cars
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: To benefit from the modern Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) requires improved antennas with increased bandwidth, better gain, low cost and smaller dimensions. This paper discusses in general the design and integration of patch antennas, with the main focus on dual-feed stacked patch antennas for GNSS applications in modern vehicles.

articleTitle: On the use of radome materials for a high-power, wideband, millimeter wave antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A comprehensive study on radome materials for a wideband, high power millimeter wave horn antenna is undertaken in the thermal, mechanical and electromagnetic domains. The radome must thermally handle continuous high power, mechanically withstand pressurization, have low loss and minimize the impact on the antenna match and far-field. Studies using several materials in each domain are conducted to determine which is the most suitable. Practical considerations such as available thicknesses and durability are heavily weighted in the selection process for practical realization of the radome.

articleTitle: Far field approximation of half-space Green's function
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper derives far field approximation of half-space dyadic Green's function which relates the reflected field to a point source. Subsequently, it is casted into a convenient form for far field evaluation. The result is validated against numerical software such as FEKO. Excellent agreement is achieved.

articleTitle: RCS reduction and gain enhancement for slot antenna array
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, RCS reduction as well as gain enhancement for a slot antenna array is presented. The proposed antenna is a 2×2 slot array with a checkerboard surface located on the top of the antenna aperture. The checkerboard surface, combining an EBG structure and a metallic grounded slab, is adopted to realize a wideband RCS reduction. The experimental result reveals that the proposed antenna array possesses in-band and out-of-band RCS reduction from 5 GHz to more than 12 GHz for both co- and cross polarizations. Besides, the gain enhancement is about 2.1 dB compared with the original slot antenna array.

articleTitle: Detection of the cervical spondylotic myelopathy using noninvasive microwave imaging technique
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper represents a newly developed noninvasive diagnostic method for cervical myelopathy detection using the microwave imaging technology. In this technique, the neck will be illuminated by the electromagnetic waveform using a UWB antenna. Then the scattered field by the neck will be measured by the receiver UWB antennas at various locations around the neck. We have simulated a simple model of a neck for detecting cervical myelopathy using CST software. The computed results demonstrate the high feasibility of using microwave technique to diagnoses the cervical myelopathy.

articleTitle: Small-reflected substrate integrated waveguide termination with multi-step shape and absorbing material
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A planar wideband substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) termination with multi-step shape and absorbing material is reported. Early reported absorbing material based SIW terminations exhibit fractional bandwidth (FBW) less than 45%. To broaden bandwidth, the multi-section stepped-impedance transformation is introduced into the design of SIW termination based on the theory of small reflection. The multi-step shape such as trident is used to mold the absorbing material, so that the impedance matching between the substrate and absorbing material can be improved and achieve a wider bandwidth. Measurement of the fabricated prototype exhibits a FBW over 70% with return loss better than 17dB, as well as system integration capability and low structure complexity.

articleTitle: Joint DoA and bandwidth estimation of unknown signals through single snapshot data and MT-BCS approach
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel strategy for the estimation of the direction-of-arrivals (DoAs) and the bandwidth of multiple signals impinging on a linear array is introduced. Starting from the voltages measured at the output of the array elements at a single time instant, the retrieval of the DoAs is addressed by means of a customized strategy based on the Multi-Tasks Bayesian Compressive Sensing (MT-BCS) in order to correlate the solutions obtained over different frequency samples. The spectral correlation allows to improve the accuracy of the DoAs recovery, although the single instant data acquisition, and to have an estimation of the signals bandwidth. A preliminary numerical result is reported to shown the behavior of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A wearable and reconfigurable folded slot antenna for body-worn devices
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a wearable reconfigurable antenna based on the concept of folded slot antennas is reported. The antenna is designed over Artificial Magnetic Conductor (AMC) to reduce the impedance mismatch due to the presence of human body and also to minimize the Specific Absorption Rate (SAR). The antenna and AMC surface are designed on a flexible substrate so that the antenna structure can be curved and mounted on human body.
