articleTitle: 3D printed feed-chain and antenna components
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a set of additive manufactured (AM) monolithic waveguide-based feed-chain and antenna components, namely a Ku-band diplexer, a Ka-band dual-polarized directional antenna and W-band straight waveguides. These components provide representative examples of the current capabilities of AM technologies. Examples are provided over a large frequency spectrum and for diverse applications. Good performance and agreement between simulation and measurement results validate the presented designs and showcase the achievable performance of this new manufacturing technology.

articleTitle: A tunable SIW integrated filter/antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A tunable 3-D filter/antenna integration implementation is presented herein. The tunable integrated device consists of a tunable coaxial substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) resonator coupled to a tunable cavity-backed slot antenna. The filter/antenna synthesis presented in this work follows closely with traditional filter synthesis with the antenna coupling energy to free space used as the second external coupling port of the device. The filter/antenna is frequency tunable from 1.71-2.88 GHz (51%) with a fractional bandwidth range of 2.90-8.10%, gain of -3.14-2.61 dBi, overall efficiency between 26.3 and 82.6%, and cross polarization level better than 20 dB in all cases.

articleTitle: Bandwidth analysis of phase crossover and non-phase crossover frequency operations of HAIS
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Scalar Holographic Artificial Impedance Surface (HAIS) is a modulated slow leaky-wave antenna whose surface impedance profile is obtained using holographic principle. The surface impedance modulation functions aid in the formation of the desired radiation pattern, polarization, aperture efficiency and bandwidth of the radiating structure. This paper compares the bandwidth of phase crossover and non-phase crossover frequency operations of scalar HAIS. It is shown that the non-phase crossover frequency operation provides an additional degree of freedom of structural modification to achieve desired polarization along with larger operational bandwidth.

articleTitle: Time-domain design of a linear antenna array for wideband shaped beams
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This investigation reports a new design of a linear antenna array for wideband shaped patterns. The array consists of uniformly spaced antipodal Vivaldi elements. The proposed design process is based on the optimization of true-time delays by implementing a particle swarm algorithm. Simulation results show wideband shaped beam patterns of 15° and 30° degrees of coverage.

articleTitle: A novel seamless scanning leaky wave antenna in ridge gap waveguide technology
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel seamless scanning leaky wave antenna in ridge gap waveguide technology is presented. The impedance matching technique is employed to suppress the open-stopband (OSB) which produces a discontinuity for a seamless scanning leaky wave antenna. Ridge gap waveguide proposed recently is used as the feeding structure. The antenna radiates from longitudinal slots of which the leaky constant is designed small to ensure a high directivity. The simulation results of full-wave analysis show that the proposed antenna bandwidth is from 12GHz to 18GHz covering the whole Ku-band while seamless scanning is achieved from backward to forward directions including broadside radiation. The scanning range is from -20° to 14° with an average gain of 18dB.

articleTitle: All-dielectric bianisotropic metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The realization of bianisotropic responses with all-dielectric metasurfaces is investigated, and a systematic design approach is developed. It is shown that by cascading anisotropic dielectric layers (subwavelength gratings) one can achieve bianisotropic responses. The all-dielectric bianisotropic metasurfaces exhibit a significantly improved loss performance over their plasmonic counterparts. A design example is presented and the performance verified through full-wave simulation.

articleTitle: Suppression of sidelobe level and sideband of time-modulated linear antenna arrays by using NSDE
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Nondominated sorting differential evolution (NSDE) is applied to simultaneously suppress sidelobe level (SLL) and sideband level (SBL) in time-modulated linear antenna arrays. The SLL and SBL of a time-modulated linear array can be reduced by optimizing excitation amplitudes and the switch-on time intervals of each element. Numerical results confirm the effectiveness and flexibility of this method.

articleTitle: Terahertz metamaterial to demonstrate extremely wide range of effective refractive indices in the 0.3-THz band
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Research on terahertz technology has progressed to offer game changing industrial applications. However, high-performance optical elements that manipulate electromagnetic waves in the terahertz waveband remain unrealized. Metamaterials can provide unprecedented refractive indices and offer a possible solution to the lack of optical elements. Here, we demonstrate simple control of parameters for identical kinds of meta-atoms allowing simple design of an extremely wide range of refractive indices including the high refractive index of 12.3, a refractive index near zero of -0.37, and a negative refractive index of -5.4 in the 0.3-THz band.

articleTitle: Van Atta arrays for realizing angular and frequency wideband carpet cloaks
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this contribution, we propose a fully passive antennas-based carpet cloak inspired by Van Atta array configuration for retroreflectors. We consider an electrically large triangular bump over a ground plane, whose sides are covered by two arrays of conventional half-wavelength dipoles. When illuminated by a plane wave, the energy is captured by the first array and transmitted beyond the obstacle by the second one. The VanAtta-inspired connection ensures the restoration of the reflection angle as if the bump were not present, mimicking the ground reflection. The proposed solution is able to overcome the intrinsic narrow frequency and angular bandwidths of conventional carpet cloaks based on metasurfaces. The performances have been numerically evaluated, showing the ability of the proposed setup to mimic the reflection from a ground plane for different illumination angles.

articleTitle: Center-fed traveling-wave microstrip array antenna using elliptically-shaped radiating elements in quasi millimeter-wave band
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A center-feeding travelling-wave microstrip array antenna is designed to realize a high-gain and broadband two-dimensional array antenna in quasi millimeter-wave band. Microstrip antennas suffer from high feeding-loss in high frequency band. Therefore, center-feeding and travelling-wave operation are applied. To reduce manufacturing errors in etching process, we propose elliptically shaped radiating elements directly connected to the feeding line. The simulated performance of the designed two-dimensional microstrip planar array with 45-degree polarization in quasi millimeter-wave band is evaluated in this paper.

articleTitle: Circular polarization agile microstrip antenna with double balanced multiplier on ring slot
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a circular polarization agile microstrip antenna. The antenna is based on an integration technology of antennas and microwave circuits. A double balanced multiplier (DBM) is utilized as the microwave circuit to achieve a circular polarization excitation and its sense switching function.

articleTitle: A novel high-performance dms/dgs low-pass filter for radar applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces the design of low pass filter for radar applications. The main block of the proposed filter is the combination of defected microstrip structure (DMS), compensated microstrip capacitors, and two defected ground structures (DGS). The proposed filter has several desirable features such as low insertion loss of 0.3 dB within the pass band, a wide rejection band from 1.5 GHz to 8.3 GHz with more than 20 dB attenuation, as well as sharp cutoff. Moreover, the proposed design has a compact size of 5.8cm×3.5cm. Experimental measurements of the fabricated filter agree with simulation results, which confirm that the proposed DMS/DGS filter design is suitable for radar and microwave applications.

articleTitle: Ultrasensitive telemetric sensor based on adapted parity-time symmetry
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose and experimentally investigate a new parity-time (PT)-symmetric wireless sensor system, whose equivalent circuit topologically satisfies the time-reversal and spatial-inversion symmetry. We demonstrate that an adapted PT-symmetric wireless sensor can enable high quality-factor (Q-factor) and great sensitivity in detecting physiological and environmental variations, overcoming the long-standing challenge in optimizations of Q-factor and sensitivity of miniature wireless sensors. Our results may ever have an impact on many wireless sensing, imaging and monitoring systems, particularly benefiting the emerging micromachined sensors, bioimplants, wearable devices, and internet-of-things applications.

articleTitle: Inkjet printing of antennas on glass or solar cells
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper demonstrates an effective method to print antennas on glass using an inkjet printer. Such a prototyping method is much cost effective and accurate compared to screen printing or clean room fabrication, and can be easily extended to print on wafers, plastics, or foams. Sample designs, printing, and results are presented.

articleTitle: Analysis of the degree of practically achievable superdirectivity using poynting streamline method
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Streamlines of Poynting vector fields and antenna effective area shapes provide a unique way to understand the physics of a receiving superdirective antenna. Superdirectivity is implemented by expanding the effective area shape from the border of the antenna physical aperture. Considering using a resonant structure in font of an aperture antenna, under the same resonant element density, the expanded distance of the effective area shape keeps the same for different antenna aperture sizes and shapes. Based on this assumption, superdirectivity is practical for electrically small and middle size antennas and electrically large antennas with a large aspect ratio. A superdirective horn antenna with 115% aperture efficiency was experimentally demonstrated.

articleTitle: Dual band, dual polarized, rail mount MIMO stadium antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a dual band, dual polarized rail mount MIMO antenna designed to provide mobile wireless coverage in the stadium environment. The high band (1695-2690 MHz) antenna is a dual polarized vertical printed dipole array with dual slant linear polarization. The low band (698-960 MHz) elements are vertically and horizontally polarized omnidirectional sleeve monopole antennas.

articleTitle: Metamaterial loop body coil element for 10.5T MRI
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A metamaterial based microstrip loop element is proposed for the ultra-high magnetic field MRI body coils. The advantage of the leaky wave broadside radiation capability of the metamaterials is utilized. A 12 cm by 12 cm square loop simulated at 447 MHz for 10.5T demonstrates good penetration of magnetic field into the phantom with no change in the resonance condition or the Q-factor after loading. It also maintains the uniformity of the field inside the phantom over a large field of view. The proposed design verifies that a resonator coil element longer than half-wavelength can be designed without affecting magnetic field distribution using metamaterials.

articleTitle: Flexible RF coil array system utilizing electro-textiles for 3T MRI carotid artery imaging
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: RF coil array system for 3T MRI carotid artery imaging is systematically designed, fabricated and characterized. Highly conductive (linear conductivity of 3Ω/m) electro-textiles and the topology of conformal surface coil array are used that will improve the coil performance. The major challenge of accurate tuning is overcome by the tunable circuitry and the complete consideration of human body and different parameters. The coil array key parameter of low S12 is achieved. The measured S11 of the fabricated coil array achieves -18 dB at exactly 127.7MHz. The measured S12 of the fabricated coil array has a maximum of -16dB, which is within the reasonable range. The effect of deformation on S11 performance is not significant, with a maximum of 1.1MHz shift when conformal to a cylinder with radius of 30mm, representing a typical human neck.

articleTitle: Warpage-free antenna for smart contact lens applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An electrically small antenna is designed to facilitate Near-Field Communication (NFC) applications on smart contact lenses. It features a distributed multi-layer coil structure that eliminates the possibility of substrate warpage. Wireless power transfer and data communication via resonant inductive coupling is demonstrated between a smart contact lens prototype and a smartphone.

articleTitle: Near-field and far-field characterization of Active Electronically Scanned Antennas (AESA) using electro-optic field probes
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Electro-optic (EO) probes provide an ultra-wideband, high-resolution, non-invasive technique for polarimetric near-field scanning of antennas and phased arrays. Unlike conventional near field scanning systems which typically involve metallic components, EO probes are all-dielectric with an extremely small footprint. As a result, EO field probes can be used very effectively for simultaneous near-field and far-field characterization of radiating apertures. In this paper, we present and discuss measurement results for different active electronically scanned antennas (AESA) at S, C and X bands with both linear and circular polarizations.

articleTitle: Feasibility of efficient and accurate estimation of cranberry crop yield using microwave sensing
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present an experimental and computational study to investigate the feasibility of microwave radar for non-invasively and accurately estimating fruit yields in cranberry beds prior to harvesting and within agricultural research plots. Dielectric measurements of the fruit and leaves show a significant contrast in the 0.5-7.5 GHz range. Full-wave computational electromagnetics simulations of microwave scattering from random distributions of cranberries show a monotonic increase in cross-polarized backscatter signal strength as a function of fractional cranberry volume. The results provide evidence of the potential of microwave reflectometry for accurate and rapid estimation and spatial mapping of cranberry crop yields.

articleTitle: A novel single-layer reflectarray antenna using square spiral element
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel single-layer reflectarray using square spirals is presented in this paper. The square spiral element employs four square spiral arms. By changing the length of the arm, a 450° phase variation range is realized. Besides, the element indicates stable responses for different incidence angles and the reflection phase curve is almost linear. Based on the good phase performance, a square reflectarray with side length of 99 mm is designed and simulated. The simulation results show good radiation performances and 1-dB gain bandwidth is about 31.3% at the center frequency of 15 GHz.

articleTitle: A Ka-band (26 GHz) circularly polarized 2×2 microstrip patch sub-array with compact feed
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A Ka-Band (26 GHz) 2×2 sub-array with square-shaped microstrip patch antenna elements having two truncated corners for circular polarization (CP) is presented. In addition, the layout for a new compact microstrip feed network for the sub-array is also presented The compact feed network offers a footprint size reduction of near 60% over traditional sub-array at 26 GHz. Experimental data indicates that a truncation amount a = 0.741 mm for an isolated patch element results in a return loss (S11) of -35 dB at 26.3 GHz Furthermore, the measured S11 for the proof-of-concept sub-array with the above elements is better than -10.0 dB at 27.7 GHz. However, the impedance match and the operating frequency can be fine-tuned to 26 GHz by adjusting the feed network dimensions. Lastly, good agreement is observed between the measured and simulated S11 for the sub-array for both right hand and left hand CP. The goal of this effort is utilize the above sub-array as a building block for a larger NxN element array, which would serve as a feed for a reflector antenna for satellite communications.

articleTitle: Small millimeter wave printed antenna arrays for 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A number of small millimeter (mm) wave printed antenna arrays for 5G applications are presented. These antennas are candidates for medium mobility 5G applications that need to have smaller form factors than base stations but not as small as cell phones and tablets. A variety of arrays is presented with gains around 10dBi-14dBi and number of elements 4 and 8, respectively. All antennas have been fabricated on standard PCB with standard methods. Measurements and simulations are presented.

articleTitle: Antenna terms and measurement techniques for active receiving arrays
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The radio astronomical antenna engineering community has developed figures of merit and a measurement technique based on noise characterization for active array receivers. The figures of merit are included in the recent revision of IEEE Standard 145, and the measurement technique is proposed for inclusion as a test procedure in an upcoming update of Std. 149.

articleTitle: Novel on-body microwave antenna array testbed for highly-sensitive measurements of wrist bone signature
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Osteoporosis represents a major health problem, resulting in substantial increases in national health care costs. Current methods to detect osteoporosis rely upon ionizing techniques such as Dual-energy X-ray Absorptiometry (DXA) and Quantitative Computed Tomography (QCT). The objective of this work is to create and validate a low-cost non-ionizing method, which uses modern RFID technology, and to construct the corresponding testbed.

articleTitle: Graphene-based terahertz polarization converters
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, broadband and ultrathin graphene-based polarization converters operating at terahertz (THz) frequencies are designed and presented. The cross-polarization converter is constituted by a periodic L-shaped patterned graphene monolayer placed on a dielectric spacer layer and terminated by a gold substrate. This subwavelength design can convert linearly polarized waves to their cross polarized version operating in reflection. Next, a circular polarization converter is presented operating in transmission, which is based on arrays of rectangular graphene patches positioned over a thin dielectric substrate. This THz design can convert the linear polarized incident wave to circular or elliptical polarized transmitted radiation. Both polarization converters are ultrathin and work over a broad frequency range and for different incident angles. In addition, they have tunable responses and are envisioned to become the building blocks of future integrated THz systems.

articleTitle: 3D printed 77 GHz Planar Yagi-Uda Antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A proof of concept 3D printed Yagi-Uda antenna for automotive radar at 77 GHz and 3D printed fabrication plan are presented. The initial design on Connex VeroWhite yields a return loss of 12.7 dB at 73.2 GHz, and 8.7 dBi phi-pol realized gain in the endfire direction, with cross-pol 20 dB down. Two 3D printed fabrication plans are discussed. The fabricated antenna and measured results will be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: Improvement on the multi-mode beams divergence of oam array by using fabry-perot cavity
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The multi-mode OAM beams generated by a circular phased antenna array are always in divergent directions, which restrict the practical application. To relieve this drawback, the Fabry-Perot (FP) cavity is employed to meliorate the beam orientation, and enhance the directivity of the OAM array. The Fabry-Perot cavity consists of a ground plane, an air cavity and a partially reflecting surface (PRS) composed of periodic complementary circular patches and apertures. The simulated results verify the effectiveness of the proposed design.

articleTitle: Dual-band frequency reconfigurable MIMO antenna with continuous tuning range
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 2-element dual-band frequency reconfigurable multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna is presented. Consisting of meandered slot antennas as the elements, the proposed antenna is planar and provides large and smooth frequency transition in two bands from 1.35-1.62 GHz and 1.95-2.2 GHz. The frequency reconfigurability is achieved through varactor diode loading across the slot. Isolation between antenna elements is improved by etching out an isolation structure in the ground plane which results in a minimum 20 dB isolation in the entire operating band. The antenna is analyzed for MIMO evaluation parameters and shows good performance.

articleTitle: Cavity-backed slot ESPAR cross array with two-dimensional beam steering control
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel cavity-backed slot ESPAR cross array with plane-independent beam scanning capability is presented in this paper. As with conventional ESPAR antenna, the parasitic cavities are fed by the center driven cavity and terminated with tunable capacitors. Due to the difficulty of achieving E-plane coupling and minimizing cross coupling between the E- and H-plane parasitic elements there are relatively few reported two-dimensional beam steering ESPAR designs. In this work it is demonstrated that these challenges can be overcome by exploiting the cavity arrangement and geometry to control the coupling between cavities. Independent E- and H-plane beam steering control is achieved by dynamically changing the load impedance of corresponding parasitic elements. It is shown that this ESPAR cross array is able to steer the beam from -24 to 24 degrees in the E-plane and -20 to 20 degrees in the H-plane; the demonstrated beam steering performance in either plane is comparable to ESPAR antennas only able to operate in a single plane.

articleTitle: Design of dual-frequency HMSIW cavity antenna for Ka band application
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel design of half-mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) cavity based antenna is presented for dual-frequency application in Ka band (26-40 GHz). Two HMSIW cavities are placed side by side and are excited through the help of inductive coupling window followed by a section of HMSIW line. As a result, the cavities are excited at TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">110</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">HM</sup> mode and the open end dielectric aperture of the HMSIW cavity starts radiating into free space. The two HMSIW line are connected to the input SIW feeding line with the help of a SIW to HMSIW power divider. The proposed antenna resonates at 26 GHz and 29 GHz while maintaining a compact design configuration which makes it suitable for application in LMDS frequency band.

articleTitle: Isolation enhancement of patch antennas using metamaterial superstrate
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A system integrated with multiple antenna elements suffers from the adverse effects of mutual coupling arising from the close proximity of the elements. This paper proposes a method to increase the isolation between microstrip patch antenna elements by using a metamaterial superstrate. By using this technique, it is possible to increase the isolation up to the level of 30dB at the resonant frequency with an edge to edge distance of λ 0/18.5 between the antenna elements. At the same time, the gain and efficiency of the antennas are also enhanced.

articleTitle: Wideband wide-slot antenna array with protrusion for wide-angle scanning
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An X-band wide-slot linear array with protrusion for one dimensional wide-angle scanning is presented. The antenna element is based on a normal printed rectangular wide-slot structure, which is then folded to form a compact cavity to achieve a wide beamwidth in E-plane while retains its wide band characteristic. Metal protrusions are set between the elements in the array to improve the antenna active reflection coefficients during scanning. The simulated results demonstrate that the proposed array obtains a 40% relative bandwidth of active reflection coefficients less than -10dB, covering frequency range of 8~12GHz, within the maximum scanning angles of ±60°.

articleTitle: GA-Optimized reflectarray elements for broadband orthogonal-polarization conversion
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes novel reflectarray resonant elements for broadband orthogonal polarization conversion designed by genetic algorithm(GA). These elements have two axially symmetrical structure to realize the phase difference of -180° between the orthogonal two linearly polarized waves, while keeping the reflection-phase range of 360° with the linearly phase-curves from 13 GHz to 17 GHz.

articleTitle: Mutual coupling reduction in two elements UWB notch antenna system
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a two elements UWB (3.1 GHz-10.6 GHz) MIMO antenna is presented. A notch frequency at 5.8 GHz is interpolated within the UWB spectrum by using a dual of electromagnetic bandgap cells coupled to the antenna feeding line. By introducing a system of electromagnetic bandgap cells between the two antennas elements, the achieved results demonstrate nearly below -10 dB reflection coefficient over the spectrum and -1 dB at the notch frequency. Also, deposition between the two antennas is achieved to exceed 20 dB. The obtained results are simulated using full wave simulations.

articleTitle: OAM modulation induced in millimeter waves using impedance matched flat phase plate
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) based communication has been investigated as it provides an additional degree of freedom to the electromagnetic waves which enables to transmit and receive data in various OAM modes at a given operation frequency, thus increasing the data rate. A method for designing very low reflective flat spiral phase plate that generates OAM modes is proposed in this paper. Such phase plates could provide one or more OAM modes at a signal frequency irrespective of the polarization. The design incorporates variable sizes of perforated unit cells along with matched layers to provide good impedance matching, and the flat disc shape of the phase plate provides the advantage of being compact and easy to install. The OAM phase plate is designed for operation around 30 GHz frequency.

articleTitle: The vortical radio waves realized by helical antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The helical antennas (HAs) work as three different types with respect to various revolution length, which are the normal-direction helical antenna (NHA), the axial-direction helical antenna (AHA) and the conical-direction antenna (CHA). In this letter, the vortical radio waves carrying the multiple orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes generated by the NHAs and CHAs is proposed. The results of the NHAs and CHAs radiating the vortical radio waves carrying the OAM in modes of l=±1, ±2, ±3, ±4 are presented. Through the simulated results, for the OAM mode l, there is the spiral phase front with l*2λ phase variation along the concentric circle in the phase pattern. For the CHA with modes larger than 1, the null amplitude of electric field in the axial direction exist, and the null amplitude area expands more with the mode increasing.

articleTitle: Miniaturized tunable artificial magnetic conductor for low LTE band
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Antennas operating in the lower band of the LTE spectrum (700-960 MHz) have conventionally required thicknesses around a hundred millimeters when placed over metallic reflectors. Miniaturized Artificial Magnetic Conductors (AMC) metasurfaces have been shown to reduce the profile (height) of these antennas while maintaining compact lateral dimensions, but at the expense of operating bandwidth. Adding tunability restores the possibility of adjusting the operating frequency over a large bandwidth. In this paper, a highly miniaturized and tunable AMC covering the lower LTE band is proposed. The novel unit cell achieves an 83 % reduction in the largest dimension compared to conventional unit cell at the highest frequency f0=960 MHz. Simulation results show that the proposed AMC surface has the potential to be used with either tunable or broadband low profile electrically small antennas.

articleTitle: Transmit array as a viable 3D printing option for backhaul applications at V-band
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Two designs of high gain dielectric lens for a V-band backhaul antenna, compatible with 3D printing, are compared. The available printing materials still have significant losses, which limit the performance of traditional focusing dielectric lenses, as the dome elliptical lens. Herein, we show that an all-dielectric transmit array can present several mechanical and electrical advantages, especially when high gains are required. We demonstrate that even with a compact transmit array (F/D = 0.67) it is still possible to comply with the usual bandwidth (57-66 GHz) and gain (>30 dBi) requirements for backhaul applications.

articleTitle: An integral equation scheme for plasma based thin sheets
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An integral equation formulation for a thin dielectric sheet is presented using the surface equivalence theorem. The advantageous properties of plasma waves, chief among them surface wave propagation are briefly discussed. Numerical results are presented to illustrate the scattering properties of the sheet with different material properties.

articleTitle: A novel efficient multiple input single output RF energy harvesting rectification scheme
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work an implementation of an ambient radio frequency harvesting system utilizing multiple input single output approach is demonstrated. Measurements of typical ambient radiation have been conducted with respect to power levels and frequency to determine which communication signals are suitable for harvesting. The measurement campaign showed that the WiFi frequency band at 2.45 GHz is a good candidate for indoors applications. A Greinacher voltage doubler is used for the rectification. A multiple input single output - MISO scalable scheme approach is implemented that is able to provide a DC differential output voltage. Simulated and experimental results proved the MISO rectenna to be an efficient scheme for RF harvesting.

articleTitle: Multi-linear polarization reconfigurable center-fed circular patch antenna with shorting posts
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel multi-linear polarization reconfigurable antenna with shorting posts, which can achieve four linear polarizations (0°, 45°, 90°, 135°), has been proposed. By switching the diodes between two groups of shorting posts, four linear polarizations can be realized. The dimensions of the proposed antenna are about 0.56λ× 0.56λ× 0.07λ at 2.4 GHz. The measured results agree well with the simulated ones.

articleTitle: A broadband patch antenna array for Q-band applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broadband patch antenna array is developed for Q-band applications. The proposed antenna element fed by substrate integrated waveguide(SIW), can be fabricated with a single-layer laminate by standard printed-circuit board(PCB) technology, which makes the antenna low cost and easy to integrate with planar millimeter-wave (mm-wave) circuits. Based on the principle of multimode broadband antennas, by loading a conventional patch with a rectangular radiator, the simulated -10dB impedance bandwidth of the antenna element is extended to 12.8%(39.5-44.9GHz). while the bandwidth of the 2 × 2 array is 13.5%(39.3-45.0GHz), with peak gain of 10.8-13.6dBi.

articleTitle: Full duplex antenna subsystem for handheld radios
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces a design of a monostatic simultaneous transmit and receive (STAR) antenna system based on a circular array of four dipole antennas fed in phase modes 0 and 1. The proposed antenna system is employed for the narrow band handheld radio applications. Ideal and actual commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) beamforming networks (BFNs) are used to validate the proposed design. The impact of nearby scatterers, e.g. human hand and head, is also studied, and return loss > 10 dB and a system isolation > 29 dB, are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Optimized design of THz microstrip antenna based-on dual-surfaced multiple split-ring resonators
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: With the huge increasing need of wide-band wireless/mobile communication, the 5G or even further future generation systems based on millimeter-wave or even higher frequency band like terahertz (THz) waveband has been attracting more and more hot research on the related antenna design. In this paper, an optimized design of one kind of the THz microstrip antenna based on the dual-surfaced multiple split-ring resonators (DSMSRRs) is presented. Attached on both surfaces of the antenna substrate, each layer contains the same MSRRs connected with a feeding line correspondingly. The total two feeding lines are overlapped from the top view while the MSRRs structure on each surface is connected with each feeding line in an opposite direction from one to the other. The well performance of even current distribution on MSRRs of both surfaces can be achieved at the resonant frequency of around 300 GHz. Some numerical results are verified by the test ones of a fabricated antenna model according to the scaling effect.

articleTitle: A t-shaped feed structure to enhance the performance of a polarization diversity antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a T-shaped feed structure is presented that enhances the performance of a polarization diversity antenna. It is a four-port network that consists of two input ports and two output ports. The -10 dB relative impedance bandwidth is 6.64 GHz from 2.31 GHz to 8.95 GHz, i.e., 117.9% and the isolation is at least 29.7 dB within the same band. Furthermore, the insertion loss is less than 0.5 dB in that band between 2.33 GHz to 8.93 GHz.

articleTitle: Active metasurface for a reconfigurable reflectarray antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An active metasurface is used as a reconfigurable reflectarray antenna. The metasurface is composed of unit cells incorporating voltage-controlled varactor diodes, where the dispersion responses of the cells can be tailored. A prototype is fabricated and far-field antenna measurements are performed. We experimentally demonstrate frequency agility over a broad frequency range and beam scanning mechanisms.

articleTitle: A UWB near-field contactless sensor for solid and liquid material characterization
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 3–10 GHz contactless sensor for liquid and solid material sensing is proposed. The sensor setup is based on utilizing two printed UWB Vivaldi antennas coupled to each other at their radiative near-field region with the material-under-test (MUT) placed in the middle. The sensor setup is fabricated with an overall size of 15.6×6.1 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Liquid chemical detection, and thickness sensing of thin dielectric slabs are successfully carried out using the proposed contactless sensor as a proof of concept.

articleTitle: Re-expressing the solution of maxwell equations using two new auxiliary scalar potentials
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel set of auxiliary potentials for reformulating the solution of source-free electromagnetic problems is proposed. This new formulation reduces the number of auxiliary potentials from four (the scalar electric potential and the three components of the vector magnetic potential) to two. The well-known but not unique auxiliary definition for the magnetic flux density, i.e. the vector magnetic potential, is replaced by another possible definition that uses only two scalar functions. Hence, the electromagnetic fields can be derived using this new formulation yielding a new description for electromagnetics by implying that the electromagnetic fields originate from a pair of scalar potentials, and secondly, lowering the computational time needed to calculate the fields than the time needed by the classical methods. To validate the derived formulation, an electromagnetic problem is successfully solved by this formulation and favorably compared with the classical one.

articleTitle: 2.4GHz monopole antenna on flexible substrate for implanting sensor
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design and measurement of a 2.4GHz monopole antenna on flexible substrate for implanting sensor. This antenna is based on a monopole antenna with coplanar waveguide feed line in order to realize the surface mounting device. The antenna size is 8.0 mm × 35 mm and peak realized gain is 1.21 dBi at 2.45GHz in simulation. This antenna has a unidirectional radiation.

articleTitle: A polarization reconfigurable RFID reader antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel RFID reader antenna with polarization reconfigurable performance is proposed. The radiating part of the reader is a printed square ring, and a reconfigurable feeding network with an embedded PIN diode is introduced to reconfigure polarization. The proposed reader antenna can be linear and circular polarized at the 910–930 MHz band by switching ON/OFF the diode. The reader antenna was fabricated and measured and its performance proves it suitable for wireless communication, diversity systems and portable devices.

articleTitle: An ultra-wideband low-phase noise local oscillator for phased array antenna system
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An ultra-wideband low-phase noise local oscillator (LO) for the phased array antenna system operating from 11 GHz to 19 GHz is proposed. A phase-locked loop (PLL) frequency synthesizer is adopted in the design where a 100 MHz crystal oscillator is used as a reference frequency. Experiment results show that the output of the ultra-wideband LO agrees well to the predicted results with high stability and low phase noise.

articleTitle: On the cause of radiation from dielectric resonator antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a physical insight into the cause of radiation from dielectric resonator antennas (DRAs). We analyzed the surface electric current distribution on the antenna's conducting elements. The surface current was then used to find the total radiated field. We conclude that the surface conduction currents on all the conducting elements of the antenna are the major contributors to the far-field radiation. The displacement current, on the other hand, has minimal contribution to radiation.

articleTitle: A new configuration for ultra compact implantable antenna based on SIW L-CRLH concept
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we introduce new configuration of ultra compact implantable antenna. The antenna is designed using the inductor loaded composite right left handed geometry in substrate integrated waveguide configuration. The antenna is designed for the IMS biomedical band with center frequency = 2.42 GHz at which the return loss is less than 15 dB. The antenna has small size (15×15 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) with 6 mm feed length. The designed implantable antenna size is only 3.5 % compared to conventional microstrip patch antenna. The obtained results are achieved using full wave simulations.

articleTitle: Broadband dual-polarized high gain lens antenna array for base station applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broadband dual-polarized high gain lens antenna array for macro-cell base station applications is proposed. Using the lens structure, high gain performance can be obtained and the horizontal half power beamwidth can be controlled. The proposed antenna array shows that wide operating bandwidth can be generated successfully to easily cover 1.71-2.69 GHz operating bands. Port-to-port isolation is better than -30 dB. The measured results show that the half power beamwidths in the horizontal plane and vertical plane are about 43°-56° and 9°-11°, respectively. The antenna gain can be enhanced to an acceptable level ranging between 16.0 and 17.5 dBi for the lens antenna array.

articleTitle: Planar fan-beam reflective array antenna based on non-bianisotropic complementary split-ring resonators (NB-CSRRs)
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel fan-beam reflective array antenna is presented in this work. The proposal is made up of a linear planar arrangement of small antennas with a ground plane spaced from the array, acting as a parasitic reflector. The main idea consists in using non-bianisotropic complementary split-ring resonators (NB-CSRR) as radiating elements, which are fed in phase to achieve broadside radiation. This approach allows obtaining a fan-beam antenna with reduced dimensions, compared to conventional designs, which are usually based on half-wave dipoles or patches. As a proof of concept, an 8-elements array antenna prototype working within the C-band frequency band has been designed and fabricated, showing good agreement between simulated and measured results.

articleTitle: A reactive impedance surface for enhancing antenna isolation on cylindrical platforms
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An investigation into a design of a reactive impedance surface that can be used for wide bandwidth enhancement of isolation between transmit and receive antennas mounted on a cylindrical radio-frequency (RF) repeater is discussed in this work. Physical isolation measurements and numerical studies for the surface are considered. Up to 17 dB of isolation enhancement is achieved with the designed surface between the antennas at the lowest frequency of operation.

articleTitle: Compact center-fed ridged waveguide slot array for SAR applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new, simple, probe-fed technique for a ridged waveguide slot array is presented. The application is for satellite synthetic aperture radar (SAR). The array is fed in the center by a coaxial probe whose inner conductor is attached to the ceiling of the ridged waveguide. An example design of a 6-element slot array with the probe is evaluated by simulation. The -10 dB return loss is around 4% and the cross polarization is well below -33 dB. The feed structure offers good mechanical stability and low voltage around the feed to prevent electrical breakdown, which are critical factors for a rocket launch and for the space environment respectively.

articleTitle: Coupled transmission line array antennas with exceptional points of degeneracy
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We explore for the first time a new paradigm for coupled transmission line (CTL)-based array antenna utilizing an exceptional point of degeneracy. An EPD represents a point in the spectrum of eigenmodes of a CTL with both gain and loss at which eigenmodes coalesce and it is a ubiquitous concept that can be applied to a variety of devices. This condition is realized in CTLs loaded with multiple active devices and radiating elements when a gain and loss balance is achieved. We demonstrate the EPD condition in microstrip CTLs and conceive a novel scheme to design low-threshold radiating grid oscillator; where the radiation threshold scales as N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> where N is the number of antennas. The EPD leads to high power efficiency of operation and with a very stable oscillation frequency. This new operational principle would enhance the efficiency of spatial power combiners and active antennas, robustness of oscillations, as well as the tunability and reconfigurability of antenna arrays for mm-wave and 5G applications.

articleTitle: Through-the-wall indoor tracking and navigation using deep-sub-wavelength magnetoquasistatics
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Recent progress in magnetoquasistatic field-based techniques have enabled decoupled and linear solutions for position and orientation sensing in non-line-of-sight environments at short to long ranges above ground. By utilizing the deep-sub-wavelength regime of the MQS source, we describe a method to enable position sensing in the indoor environment. The technique enables accurate positioning of a mobile device within a few skin-depths into a heavy multi-path building environment.

articleTitle: Design of dual-band pattern reconfigurable cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel dual-band dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) with reconfigurable radiation pattern has been proposed. The antenna adopts cylindrical dielectric resonator (DR) and coplanar waveguide ground fed, which has the potential to achieve dual-band characteristic. Some parallel parasitic strips on the bottom with two pairs of switches are printed on the two opposite sides of the cylindrical DR. The lengths of parasitic elements change in a way of reflector and director of Yagi antenna by controlling the switches ON or OFF, which makes the proposed DRA work at two modes with different radiation pattern characteristic.

articleTitle: Linear-linear basis functions for source reconstruction using magnetic-field integral equations in very-near-field measurements
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Linear-Linear (LL) basis functions are used to solve magnetic-field integral equation (MFIE) in the planar very-near-field measurement of the antennas and reconstruct the equivalent currents. Such choice reduces the inaccuracy in comparing to Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG) basis functions. This method is obtained with a slight change in existing RWG based codes.

articleTitle: A planar dipole antenna with parasitic elements for beamwidth enhancement across a wide frequency band
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The unidirectional dipole antenna with wide beamwidth is required for the increasing coverage range in wireless communication systems. In this paper, top-loaded metallic posts are loaded on the reflector plane of the planar dipole antenna for wideband beamwidth enhancement. The simulated results indicate that both E-plane beamwidth and H-plane beamwidth of the proposed antenna increase to about 100° across the fractional bandwidth of 34.8%, ranging from 1.9 to 2.7 GHz.

articleTitle: Ku-band wideband space-borne waveguide slot array antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Ku-band wideband high gain space-borne waveguide slot array antenna optimized by genetic algorithms is presented. Wide bandwidth is ensured by utilizing E-T wideband power divider and partition feed distribution of the array. Respects referring to higher modes, slot couplings, slot end shapes and other factors are given fully consideration in design process. Precision processing and salt bath brazing are employed to maintain the good conformity with respect to aperture shape, besides, high strength is also guaranteed. Two factors mentioned above play an important role for the possible coherent measurement. Results obtained by multipaction test, vibration and thermal cycle test verify the good properties of the large dimension fan beam payload array antenna. Measurements acquired by planar near field test show that the gain is 33.8 dB with radiation efficiency up to 76%, and side lobe levels of the two main planes are -19 dB and -20 dB respectively, meanwhile, the VSWR bandwidth better than 1.5 is about 400 MHz.

articleTitle: A configurable and repeatable multipath channel emulator
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: As Internet of Things (IoT) systems become more pervasive, there will be greater need for wireless devices that can operate reliably under less than ideal propagation conditions. IOT environments can be expected to have large signal path losses due to non-line-of-sight (NLOS) conditions, reflective surfaces and/or moving components in the environment. One example is a IoT network deployed in the highly reflective and blocking environment of a factory floor. In this work, a highly configurable, multipath channel emulator is presented. The emulator itself utilizes a reconfigurable antenna array and has over 200 million different configurations that are software controlled. There is also a database of over 2000 predefined channel conditions, ranging in severity from Ricean to hyper-Rayleigh, each of which can be readily recreated.

articleTitle: Frequency-controlled beam scanning array fed by spoof surface plasmon polaritons
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose frequency-controlled broadband and broad-angle beam scanning array based on spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs). The conventional planar spoof SPP waveguide consisting of double-sided corrugated unit cells is split into two branches. After being split, each spoof SPP waveguide branch is used to feed a row of circularly metallic patches for radiations. The proposed structure can realize wide-angle beam scanning from backward direction to forward direction as the frequency changes, breaking the limit of traditional leaky-wave antennas. It is shown that the scanning angle can reach 93 degrees with an average gain level of 9.6 dBi.

articleTitle: Facet based investigation on the composite EM scattering from ship over sea surface
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper mainly focus on the composite scattering from sea surface with electrically large targets. For this purpose, a refined facet scattering field model combined with the GO-PO hybrid method is presented to calculate the scattering from a ship target on sea surface. When dealing with the coupling scattering between the ship and sea surface, the GO-PO method can consider the mutual shaded effect between the patches on target and the facets on the sea surface. Thus, it is more reasonable to calculate the second scattering contribution of different patches. numerical simulation for the composite scattering of a ship target and sea surface verify the validity of the proposed model and scattering properties of a composition scene are analyzed.

articleTitle: Reverberation chambers for flexible over-the-air testing of internet-of-things devices
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The reverberation chamber is an accurate and frequently used tool for over-the-air testing of wireless devices. One main benefit of this method is the flexibility of the test volume, given the uniform field emulated within the chamber. This characteristic becomes even more important for the emerging test requirements of Internet-of-Things devices, which may have very different form factors compared to traditional devices. In this investigation the total radiated power and total isotropic sensitivity are measured for three models of Bluetooth devices. The measurements are repeated in three different reverberation chamber setups with very different sizes, with the aim to investigate if aligned results can be obtained.

articleTitle: Magnetic induced heating of gold-iron oxide nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This study investigates the heating characteristics of aqueous solutions of nanoparticles (NPs) through a magnetically induced field. Through simulation and experimental studies, key parameters that affect the temperature profiles of magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) are identified. Specifically, the influence of magnetic field strength, MNPs concentration, MNPs composition, and coil size was explored as a way to understand the correlation between the NPs structure and the magnetic induced heating process.

articleTitle: The impact of introduced coupling elements on characteristic mode
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper gives a detail discussion about the impact of introduced coupling elements on characteristic mode. Different types of inductive coupling elements (ICEs) and capacitive coupling elements (CCEs) placed on plate structure and box structure have been taken into account. The eigenvalue, mode current and far-field of the combined structure with coupling elements are evaluated. In comparison with the original body, mode current of combined structure has changed in some degrees due to the presence of the coupling elements. But eigenvalue and mode far-field are in close proximity to the original. The impact on characteristic mode provides physical explanation about how coupling elements excite the desired characteristic modes. Information provided by CM of the combined structure can be used to optimize the size and geometry of the coupling elements.

articleTitle: Broadband window-type circular polariser based on frequency selective surfaces
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broadband circular polariser is designed based on window-type frequency selective surface. The window is derived from subtraction of different squares. The proposed polariser has both advantages of wide operational bandwidth and high transmission coefficients. To prove this design, a new polariser working in X-band is optimized and fabricated. Experimental results show that the measured axial ratios lower than 3dB range from 7.21–13.43GHz, with the transmission coefficients more than 0.81. Meanwhile, the polariser is insensitive to the incident angle, which could obtain the operating frequency band at 8–13GHz with the incident angle increasing to 30°.

articleTitle: A mask matching tiling optimization method for clustered phased arrays
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel tiling optimization approach based on a mask matching strategy for the design of tiled phased arrays is here presented. Optimal complex coefficients, generating a power pattern satisfying some design constraints, are clustered into tiles of domino shape. The best tiling configuration fitting the desired requirements is obtained through an exhaustive search approach evaluating each solution with a mask matching strategy. A simple numerical example is reported to validate the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Graphene Microwave Resonators
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Design, fabrication and analysis of graphene based resonators at microwave frequencies are presented. Chemical Vapor Deposited (CVD) graphene is used to fabricate the resonating stub, where Raman spectroscopy has been adopted to confirm the layer number of graphene. The measurements were carried out from 12 GHz to 28 GHz. The results of graphene resonator's input impedance show that graphene could work well as a resonating unit in the short-end resonating structure, demonstrating that graphene based resonators can find a lot of applications in developing guided graphene based devices at microwave frequencies.

articleTitle: Miniaturized vivaldi antenna based on low frequency resonance for WLAN application
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A miniaturized dual-band Vivaldi antenna based on low frequency resonance is presented. Compared with traditional traveling wave mode Vivaldi antenna, the proposed antenna has a smaller size due to the use of self-resonant mode. The antenna is designed to operate at WLAN 2.4/5.2/5.8 GHz band and has a physical dimension of 25 × 28 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. A prototype was fabricated and tested, the results show that the proposed antenna can provide two working bands with the -10 dB bandwidth of 2.35-2.58 GHz and 5.1-5.9 GHz, which covers the entire WLAN frequency range.

articleTitle: A novel double-layer leaky-wave antenna array for radiation efficiency improvement based on substrate integrated waveguide
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel double-layer leaky-wave antenna (LWA) array for radiation efficiency improvement based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) is proposed. The LWAs are integrated on the first layer of the array, and a SIW waveguide is designed on the second layer. The input power is fed into one of the LWAs, and the remaining power at the end of this LWA is coupled into the SIW waveguide on the second layer through coupling slots. The power is then transmitted and coupled into another unfed LWA on the top layer again. As a consequence, the radiation efficiency gets improved, as well as the gain, while the structure of the antenna maintains in a compact size. Simulation results are given to demonstrate the efficiency of the design.

articleTitle: Channel capacity analysis of different mobile antenna array topologies in the outdoor urban environment for 5G mm wave system
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The 15 and 28 GHz frequency bands have been identified as interesting candidates for future 5G cellular communication systems. In this paper, based on ray-tracing simulations, we investigate the channel capacities at 15 and 28 GHz for a number of different array processing techniques, including beamforming, spatial multiplexing, and two types of hybrid beamforming. This is done for an 8×32 multiple input multiple output system, for the single user case. The hybrid beamforming techniques combines the beamforming and spatial multiplexing techniques, in order to reduce the number of analog-to-digital converters and thereby reducing the system complexity, while still maintaining multiplexing capabilities for improved system capacities. The achieved channel capacities the hybrid beamforming techniques with up to four parallel streams outperforms pure beamforming, but does not reach capacities close to that of full spatial multiplexing. This indicates that the outdoor channel can support multiplexing of more than four parallel data streams to a single user.

articleTitle: Mm-wave 2D beam-steering focal plane array with microfluidically switched feed network
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Microfluidic focal plane arrays (MFPAs) are attractive for realizing low-cost beam-steering at mm-waves with a compact structure. Recently, a microfluidically switched feed network concept has been introduced for improving the bandwidth performance of these arrays. Specifically, a selectively metallized plate inside a microfluidic channel is placed over a feed network consisting of gaps. Due to the strong capacitive coupling between the plate metallizations and the feed line (through a channel wall thickness <;10 μm), metallizations that overlap with gaps act as RF switches. This paper, for the first time, reports the experimental verification of this concept through the realization of an 8 element 30 GHz MFPA. The measured gain value (>22 dB) and experimental switch characterization demonstrate that the switches exhibit <;0.1 dB insertion loss (IL) and result in low-loss wideband feed networks. In addition, extending the concept to 2D beam-steering is demonstrated with an 8×8 array design.

articleTitle: Optimizing signal coverage in the azimuth plane of conformal microstrip antennas by widening their sectorial beamwidths
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: New broadband data exchange applications are often characterized with a desire to use antennas generating a few sectorial beams. For such applications we have studied various multi-beam, dual-band and dual-polarized conformal antennas. The paper compares performance of two quite different cylindrical antenna designs, each generating four beams in the azimuth plane.

articleTitle: PT-symmetric epsilon-near-zero plasmonic waveguides
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Plasmonic waveguides exhibit an effective epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) response at their cut-off frequency. In this work, we demonstrate a nanoscale parity-time (PT) symmetric nanophotonic device based on gain medium embedded inside the nanochannel of a plasmonic waveguide. The effect of introducing gain is more than loss compensation and can cause a plethora of new interesting phenomena. In particular, the interplay between loss and gain will lead to super scattering at the exceptional point obtained close to the ENZ resonance frequency. This interesting effect is made possible by introducing an active material with small gain coefficient inside the plasmonic waveguide. When the proposed active waveguide is illuminated by two counter-propagating plane waves, the output ENZ power becomes unidirectional. In addition, the ENZ response can be dynamically modulated from strong scattering to perfect absorption just by changing the phase difference between the two incident waves. Strong fields are obtained in the nanochannel of the proposed PT-symmetric plasmonic waveguide, which are found to drastically boost optical nonlinearities, leading to strong optical bistability and switching at the ENZ resonance.

articleTitle: MASCRAD events: Observations and analyses of cases with contrasting hydrometeor forms
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present observations and analyses for several cases with contrasting hydrometeor forms, recorded by several ground instruments at the MASCRAD (MASC + Radar) snow field site, radiosondes, and polarimetric radars. The instrumentation includes the multi-angle snowflake camera (MASC) and 2D-video disdrometer. The study focuses on microphysical characteristics analysis and is aimed at improving the radar-based winter-precipitation estimation.

articleTitle: Generation of an orbital angular momentum mode based on a cassegrain reflectarray antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose how to generate OAM mode using a Cassegrain type reflectarray instead of parabolic reflector. The Cassegrain reflectarray antenna is fabricated and measured to generate the l = 1 OAM mode.

articleTitle: Antenna G/T degradation with inefficient receive antennas at HF (2–30 MHz)
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the antenna G/T degradation incurred when communications systems use very inefficient receive antennas. This work is relevant when considering propagation predictions at HF (2–30 MHz), where it is commonly assumed that antennas are efficient/lossless and external noise dominates over internally generated noise at the receiver. Knowledge of the antenna G/T degradation enables correction of potentially optimistic HF predictions. Simple rules-of-thumb are provided to identify scenarios when receive signal-to-noise ratios might be degraded.

articleTitle: Minimizing gain roll-off in rotman lens antenna using phase gradient transmission lines
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a simple method to minimize the gain roll-off of the Rotman lens antenna with wide scans. Phase gradient transmission lines are used to neutralize a precipitous drop in the power efficiency of Rotman lens when the scan angle increases. To validate the proposed method, a Rotman lens antenna at X band with 8 beam ports and 9 array ports are designed and simulated. The results show that the gain roll-off of Rotman lens antenna can be improved from 5.5 dB to 2 dB over a 90-degree beam coverage.

articleTitle: Investigation of alternative array configurations of nanowires for maximum power transmission at optical frequencies
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a computational analysis and comparison of nanowire arrays for efficient transmission of electromagnetic power at optical frequencies. A reliable simulation environment involving the multilevel fast multipole algorithm for fast iterative solutions of surface integral equations is used to accurately compute field intensity and power density values in the vicinity of nanowires in diverse configurations. The results demonstrate favorable properties of honeycomb structures that can provide efficient power transmission in comparison to other arrangements.

articleTitle: Study of free-space coupling into mm-wave whispering-gallery mode resonators for a radioastronomy receiver
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the coupling mechanism of a free-space Gaussian beam into a whispering-gallery mode resonator through a dielectric lens is mathematically modeled and numerically solved by means of the Schelkunoff-Waterman method (the so called T-matrix method). This approach allows in principle, to quickly analyze the performance of different near-field coupling mechanisms with arbitrary excitations. The aim is to efficiently excite a WGM into a nonlinear dielectric resonator in order to detect the weak mm-wave radiation from the cosmic microwave background (CMB) by up-converting the signal into the optical domain via the nonlinearity of the medium.

articleTitle: Coupled topologically protected metawaveguides
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The appearance of a photonic band gap in the dispersion relation of a coupled lines structure realized with two topologically protected metawaveguide is here presented. We show its possible exploitation to realize multiport devices and an electronically tunable approach which can be used to modulate the eigenfrequencies of the resulting structure is proposed.

articleTitle: Soft-matter electronics and multifunctional materials with polydisperse liquid metal suspensions: Material architecture, principles, and applications to programmable matter
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Soft elastomers embedded with a polydisperse suspension of liquid metal (LM) droplets exhibit a unique and extraordinary combination of electrical, thermal, and mechanical properties. Eutectic gallium-indium (EGaIn) LM alloy is used for the dispersion phase on account of its low viscosity, negligible toxicity, and ability to form an emulsion with liquid polymer. Because the alloy is liquid at room temperature, it can alter the electrical and thermal properties of the composite - giving it metal-like bulk features - while preserving the mechanics of the elastomer matrix. These soft multifunctional materials can function as stretchable circuit wiring, high-k dielectric insulators, or heat dissipating films in a broad range of emerging “soft-matter” technologies. In particular, we look at applications to physically-reconfigurable system capable of reversible shape change.

articleTitle: A comparison of 24 GHz and 2.55 GHz MIMO measurements in two indoor scenarios
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: MIMO measurements at 24 GHz and 2.55 GHz are compared for two buildings consisting of classrooms and offices on two college campuses. The results indicate that mutual information for 4×4 MIMO with 15 dB SNR is very similar, suggesting similar multipath structure for the two different bands. Path loss is approximately 30 dB higher at 24 GHz, mainly due to the reduced receive aperture at the higher frequency. These results suggest that 24 GHz may be a suitable replacement for near and medium range indoor wireless applications currently using the 2.4 GHz ISM band.

articleTitle: On the phase center analysis of linear phased-array antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the phase center of linear phased-arrays is investigated. A far-field formulation is applied to evaluate the phase center location for different beam scan angles and under multiple element-failure conditions. The phase center is found to be scan invariant and lies at the geometric center of the array when all elements are functional and under a symmetric amplitude excitation. When one or more elements fail, the phase center follows a centroid function given by the element locations weighted by the element amplitude excitations. This work has applications in phased arrays used for feeding reflector antennas for multiple-beam systems.

articleTitle: Structural and electromagnetic design considerations for very large space antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes the design and analysis of a 24-element dipole array which serves as an optimized feed structure for a 150-meter cruciform reflector antenna for satellite communications in the 1-2 GHz range. The radiation pattern for this structure was calculated using a Method of Moments based computational electromagnetics code yielding an overall 47 dBi reflector gain. The effect of incorporating this optimized feed is an overall performance improvement on an initial cruciform reflector antenna design by minimizing spillover and undesirable side lobes. Performance versus size-and-weight tradeoffs are discussed as is a detailed description of the cruciform antenna's mechanical design and its resultant RF characteristics.

articleTitle: Higher order electromagnetic modeling in current and charge integral equation method
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel higher order scheme of current and charge integral equation (CCIE) is introduced for the accurate electromagnetic modeling in the wide frequency band. The higher order hierarchical vector bases are adopted for the current expansion, whilst the orthogonalized polynomials are utilized as scalar bases for the charge expansions. A numerical result is given to show the stable performance at wide frequency band.

articleTitle: An efficient hybrid CEM approach to modeling backscatter of forest clutter
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a novel hybrid Computational Electromagnetics (CEM) modeling framework for simulating the backscatter from forest clutter when sensed by UHF and VHF radars.
