publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A multiple parameter reconfigurable antenna is presented in this paper. The antenna is a microstrip patch which consists of a driven circular patch antenna and four circular parasitics. The reconfigurable operation of the antenna is realised by six embedded switches on the driven element and the parasitics. Two switches, embedded within the driven element are used to switch between circular polarisation (CP) and linear polarisation (LP). Whereas the embedded switches within the parasitics are used to alter the main beam direction. The antenna is capable of yielding CP radiation when the main beam is directed towards boresight. The antenna operates at 10.6 GHz. There is alignment between the -10 dB impedance bandwidth(BW) (6.6%) and the 3 dB axial ratio (AR) BW (1.4%) of the antenna. Furthermore, the main lobe gain is approximately constant for all steering angles.

articleTitle: Design of broadband reflecting metasurfaces for polarization conversion
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broadband linear polarization converter based on a reflecting metasurface is presented. The polarization converter is composed by a periodic arrangement of metallic particles, positioned in a square lattice with a periodicity T equal to 4.6mm. The metallic elements are printed on a metal-backed Rohacell HF31 layer with a thickness of 3mm. The unit cell topology is optimized by using a genetic algorithm. The polarization converter works from 7.3 GHz to 29.01 GHz. Since the genetic algorithm provides arbitrary cell geometries where surface currents are not excited, a refinement procedure is proposed for removing unnecessary pixels. The highest working frequency polarization converter obtained at the end of the refinement process is extended up to 32.88 GHz thus obtaining a relative bandwidth of 129.54%.

articleTitle: Hybrid cross approximation for electric field integral equation based scattering analysis
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The hybrid cross approximation (HCA) algorithm is studied as an alternative means for the low-rank compression of the electric field integral equation (EFIE) operator. The HCA combines the advantages of both the interpolation and the adaptive cross approximation (ACA) based methods. It produces a much reduced rank as compared to the rank generated from an interpolation-based degenerate approximation. The rank's growth rate with electric size is also reduced to that of the ACA-based method. Meanwhile, it preserves the advantages of the interpolation-based method in reduced computation and better convergence. Numerical examples demonstrate that the HCA is computationally more efficient than pure ACA for the same prescribed accuracy in generating an H-representation of the EFIE operator.

articleTitle: Transparent metasurface with prescribed aperture field
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We theoretically demonstrate the mechanisms to funnel electromagnetic energy through any desired prescribed aperture field distributions, using transparent metasurfaces with inhomogeneous impedance profiles. It is shown that a single inhomogeneous impedance surface is sufficient to mold the near-field distribution at will, while 100% transmission is achieved. The results are derived analytically and demonstrated through numerical examples of subwavelength field localization. A related technique based on the Weston condition is also discussed. Our method provides a very general recipe to synthesize transparent surface impedance profiles with interesting connections to the extraordinary light transmission phenomenon. Our designs may find interesting applications in sensing, particle trapping, and energy harvesting.

articleTitle: A single radiator with four decoupled ports for four by four MIMO antennas and systems
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a new way to implement four by four MIMO antennas in a mobile terminal. By properly choosing the position of the feeding and shorting pin on only one radiator, the proposed design can offer four decoupled and uncorrelated antenna ports. All of the four antennas resonant at the 3.5GHz band. The superiority of the proposed antenna is verified by measurement. Measured S-parameter, total efficiency and envelop correlations between each port demonstrate that the proposed design is simple and effective for any LTE-Advanced enable systems.

articleTitle: Tai-Chi-Inspired pancharatnam-berry phase metasurface for dual-band RCS reduction
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a new metasurface inspired by Tai-Chi shape, which is applicable to dual-band radar cross section (RCS) reduction. The Tai-Chi-shape unit cell features a rotational self-complementary property. The metasurface, composed of such cells with different rotations, exhibits randomly distributed phase shift covering 2π range, giving rise to a diffusion of backscattering. Therefore, the RCS of the metasurface is substantially reduced compared to one of the equal-sized metallic plates. The full-wave simulation results show that the proposed metasurface can obtain nearly 8dB RCS reduction from 14.7GHz to 20.6 GHz and from 22.7GHz to 23.7GHz with polarization-independent performance.

articleTitle: A smart wireless energy harvesting system with adaptive beamforming and power management
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A high level design of a smart wireless energy harvesting system is presented. The energy harvesting system is designed to be adaptive to varying loads and input powers. The system also utilizes a phased array antenna to adaptively scan the beam for maximum power tracking. Simulated and experimental results for the major subsystems of the harvester are presented.

articleTitle: Wideband RF and analog self-interference cancellation filter for simultaneous transmit and receive system
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: To address the limited spectrum, current communication systems employ either frequency division duplex (FDD) or time division duplex (TDD) transceivers. These duplexing techniques exploit orthogonality of the time/frequency resources, to reuse the spectrum. A popular approach for implementing full duplex communication without increasing resource utilization is the simultaneous transmit and receive (STAR) scheme. However, the implementation of STAR systems is hindered by the high power transmitted signal which inevitably couples to the receiver, causing higher interference in the band of interest. It is therefore necessary to suppress this interference. In this paper, we present the design and implementation of a 2-stage interference cancellation at the RF and analog domain. This results in 50dB suppression of the coupled signal across a wide bandwidth of 500MHz.

articleTitle: Mode analysis of 1-Bit reflectarray element using p-i-n diode at W-band
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the working modes of 1-bit reflectarray cell with one p-i-n diode at W-band are discussed in detail. The structure of the unit cell and the model of the p-i-n diode at W-band is presented first. The modes of the unit cell at ON/OFF state of p-i-n diode are described using the resonance cavity theory. A positive phase shift of 180° and a negative phase shift of 180° can be achieved in different cases by using different capacitances. The ability of 1-bit phase shift could be achieved in both cases, which increases the design feasibility of W-band reconfigurable reflectarray.

articleTitle: Broad-band cavity-backed and probe-fed microstrip phased array antenna in X-band
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of a broad-band cavity-backed microstrip phased array antenna is presented in this paper. The array antenna uses novel single layer cavity-backed microstrip patch elements supporting broad operating frequency band. The better angle scan performance of the array antenna can be obtained because of the using of the independent probe feeding technique. The design has been experimentally validated with an X-band planar 8×8 array. The array antenna providing 33.6% bandwidth with VSWR lower than 2. And the operating frequency range cover 7.9 ~ 11.1GHz. The antenna array supports wide angle scanning up to a maximum of 30 degrees at the whole operating frequency band. Consequently, a broadband cavity-backed microstrip phased array antenna with wide scan performance is successfully verified.

articleTitle: On-package mm-wave FSS integration with 3D-printed encapsulation
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work outlines the design, simulation, and fabrication of a millimeter-wave (mm-wave) frequency selective surface (FSS) integrated directly onto a 3D-printed die encapsulation. The cross-shaped slot FSS is designed to function as a bandpass filter centered at 77 GHz for on-package tunability. Stereolithography (SLA) 3D printing is used to fabricate encapsulations for silicon dies attached to a metallic QFN leadframe. Surface profilometry is used to assess the roughness of the SLA-printed surfaces, yielding roughness 25× lower than standard fused deposition modeling (FDM) 3D printing techniques. Finally, inkjet printing is used in a post-process fashion to fabricate the package-integrated FSS directly onto a 3D-printed die encapsulation as a proof-of-concept demonstration.

articleTitle: Wideband monostatic spiral array for full-duplex applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel co-polarized wideband monostatic antenna array for full-duplex or simultaneous transmit and receive (FD/STAR) applications is proposed. The developed approach incorporates antenna elements orientation and beam-forming network (BFN) to theoretically eliminate the interference from the TX to RX. The array is composed of four dual function TX/RX balun-fed two-arm Archimedean spiral antennas. Measured isolation with the RF enhancement layer of 40dB-60dB, VSWR<;2, and TX BFN power loss <;10% are achieved over 2:1 bandwidth. Good correlation between the TX and RX co-polarized radiation patterns is also demonstrated.

articleTitle: Wideband Ku-band antennas using multi-layer direct digital manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Design and performance of a fully-printed Ku-band aperture coupled patch antenna manufactured by making use of a direct digital manufacturing (DDM) approach that integrates fused deposition of acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS) thermoplastics with in-situ micro-dispensing of conductive silver paste (CB028) is reported. Microstrip line characterizations demonstrate that the microstrip line feed loss of the antenna is minimized by printing ABS in parallel with the line directions. A wideband (20%) performance is achieved by employing a multilayer printing approach. Compared to existing work in literature, the presented antenna stands out as being fully-printed, operating within the Ku-band, and exhibiting high radiation efficiency (6.5 dB gain) with wide bandwidth performance.

articleTitle: Hybrid-fed microstrip patch antenna for MPAR application
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a high-isolation, low cross-polarization dual polarized patch antenna for the Multi-function Phased Array Radar (MPAR). The proposed antenna is fed by a balanced probe feed and a slot-coupled feed. The input isolation between horizontal and vertical ports is more than -52 dB and the cross-polarization level for both horizontal and vertical polarization is less than -32 dB in the entire bandwidth. The simulation results of a designed single element are presented.

articleTitle: Theory of electromagnetic intelligent agents with applications to MIMO and DoA systems
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose the concept of electromagnetic intelligent agents (EM-IA) as a general framework for a new generation of antenna systems concurrently employing electromagnetics, communication theory, and artificial intelligence within one integrated platform. The proposed strategy emphasizes certain machine learning aspects that can be gleaned from communication-system-theoretic models carefully constructed using the antenna current Green's function formalism when applied to Tx/Rx antennas and the environments inside which they live. The system intelligence feature is enacted through reprogrammable artificial neural networks attached to the antennas' terminals and trained by data generated through the electromagnetic model. The proposed EM-IA scheme is demonstrated with a concrete example geared toward adaptive mutual coupling compensation in receiving MIMO and DoA array systems operating within dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable reflectarray antenna for microwave detection and imaging
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a design of a reconfigurable reflectarray antenna. A reconfigurable unit cell element based on varactor diode is first designed, fabricated and tested at X-band. Measured reflection phase range equal to 305° is obtained by tuning the diode biasing voltage. A reconfigurable reflectarray antenna of 10 × 10 elements is designed based on the proposed unit cell element. A prototype of the reflectarray antenna is fabricated and tested to validate the ability of pattern control. This reflectarray is used in a prototype compressive sensing detection system to detect threat objects in shoes.

articleTitle: Benchmarking computational electromagnetics with exact analytical solutions of canonical electromagnetic scattering problems
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Solutions of canonical electromagnetic scattering problems may be used to benchmark computational electromagnetics methods. While the list of known exact analytical solutions is limited, this list extends significantly beyond classical solutions for the scattering from metallic bodies such as the sphere, the 2D metallic wedge, and the infinite circular cylinder. In fact, recently developed exact solutions exist for geometries involving cavities, sharp edges, apertures, and propagation across different media. Unfortunately, many articles discussing computational electromagnetics solutions frequently propose validations or benchmarks with geometries as simple as a sphere and then jump into comparisons with very complex objects such as a numerical model of an airplane. In such cases, validations with simpler, but yet challenging benchmarks should provide additional evidence of their accuracy. In many cases, comparisons with exact solutions for benchmarking purposes are quite straightforward to implement.

articleTitle: A small RFID tag antenna for metallic object using characteristic mode
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A small UHF RFID tag antenna for metallic object using characteristic mode theory (CMT) is presented in this paper. The tag antenna is composed of a rectangle loop and the metallic object. The rectangle loop is used as an inductive coupler element (ICE) to excite a specified characteristic mode current of the metallic object. In this case, the metallic object itself will act as the main radiator. The loop is printed on the ceramic material with a high relative dielectric constant and placed at a current maximum of a desired mode. The satisfactory result proves that the desired characteristic mode has been partially excited by this small loop.

articleTitle: Validation of the polynomial for RF absorber reflectivity for the prediction of anechoic chambers
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Indoor antenna ranges must have the walls, floor and ceiling treated with RF absorber. The normal incidence performance of the absorber is usually provided by the manufacturers of the materials, however, the bi-static or off angle performance must also be known. In reference [1], a polynomial approximation was introduced that gave a prediction of the reflected energy from pyramidal absorber. In this paper, the approximations are used to predict the quiet zone (QZ) performance an anechoic chambers. These predictions are compared with full wave analysis performed in CST Suite. The results show that the polynomial approximations can be used to give a fairly accurate prediction of the QZ performance of anechoic chambers.

articleTitle: Pharaonic ankh-key millimeter wave broadband antenna design and fabrication for 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new design of millimeter-wave antenna is proposed to work on the 60.5-72 GHz frequency band with more than 11 GHz bandwidth. A low cost, single layer and easily fabricated design is achieved with a peak gain of 8.4 dBi. The simulated and measured results showed satisfying parameters enhancing this design to be used at millimetre wave frequencies for short-range wireless communication applications, such as 5G applications and V-band applications.

articleTitle: Cold & hot tests of an S-band antenna for high power microwave systems
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present results of simulation, fabrication, and testing of an S-band narrow-wall longitudinal slot antenna designed for high-power-microwave (HPM) systems. A key aspect of the proposed antenna structure is the use of longitudinal slots in the narrow-wall of a rectangular waveguide as elements of the slot array to enhance the power handling capability of the antenna. Cold test of the antenna showed excellent agreement with the simulated return loss and radiation patterns. The radiation pattern measured in high power testing with a source power of 0.8MW also demonstrated good agreement with the simulated radiation pattern. This source power level is slightly below the predicted maximum input power handling capability of 1.15MW, at high elevation (in Albuquerque, NM). This work demonstrates that this narrow-wall longitudinal slot antenna is well suited to HPM applications.

articleTitle: Compact CP antenna based on resonant quadrifilar spiral structure for UHF RFID handheld reader
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact circularly polarized (CP) antenna based on the resonant quadrifilar spiral structure for the application of UHF RFID handheld reader is proposed and demonstrated experimentally. Such an antenna indicates stable circular polarization performance and wide radiation beamwidth. The gain bandwidth (>2 dBic) can cover the frequency band from 902MHz to 928 MHz, which is suitable for most of the popular UHF RFID systems in the world.

articleTitle: A planar leaky-wave antenna offering well designed leakage on the 2D aperture using printed width modulated microstrip lines
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel planar leaky-wave antenna (LWA) based on quasi-periodic width-modulated printed strips is investigated. Each single strip is obtained by a repetition of several unit cells with different lengths and modulations in order to keep the desired value of the phase constant when changing the attenuation along the line. The overall antenna surface consists of an arrangement of 9 such transversely periodic printed strips. Therefore, the radiated field can be fully controlled geometrically. This results in backward radiation by the n = - 1 spatial harmonic; i.e., the pointing angle θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P</sub> = -19° in the E<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">θ</sub>(φ = 0°) plane is realized by a proper design of the periodic sequence of the proposed array of unit cells enabling aperture control. A numerical example with an incident surface-wave excitation demonstrates the validity of the method.

articleTitle: Application of near-field phase transformation to steer the beam of high-gain antennas in two dimensions
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Low-cost and efficient methods of steering highly directive antenna beams will play a major role in emerging communication systems. This paper outlines a method based on near-field phase transformation, to steer the beam of a fixed high-gain antenna. It has been implemented and tested using two rotating metasurfaces placed at sub-wavelength spacing in the near-field region of a base antenna. This method yields low-profile and planar antenna systems that can steer beam to any direction within a large conical region. Unlike mechanically-steered dish antennas, the height and volume of the antenna system remain constant while steering. Only two thin metasurface require rotation; the rest of the antenna system, including the high-gain base antenna, is totally stationary. Due to lack of active devices, these antenna systems are more efficient, do not suffer from thermal issues and non-linear distortion, and can handle more power.

articleTitle: Miniaturization of base-station antenna element
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A miniaturized ±45° dual-polarized magnetoelectric dipole antenna element for cellular base-station application is proposed in this paper. The antenna element is realized by exciting a pair of planar electric dipole antennas and a pair of quarter-wave vertically shorted patch antennas simultaneously, which performs as crossed electric and magnetic dipoles. The corners of the planar electric dipole antennas are truncated for miniaturization purpose. The height of the walls surrounding the dipole is optimized for stable radiation patterns. As a result, the proposed antenna element can have the size reduced from 0.8λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> to 0.59λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, yet achieving a similar performance, where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the wavelength at the center frequency.

articleTitle: Novel fishnet-like chiral metamaterial structure with negative refractive index and low losses
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work a composed chiral metamaterial structure constituted by the combination of a composite chiral metamaterial and a modified fishnet structure is presented and numerically analyzed. This new fishnet-like chiral metamaterial features two wide frequency bands wherein the refractive indices are negative and exhibits lower losses than its constituents do.

articleTitle: Composite Floquet scattering matrix for the analysis of time-modulated systems
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a rigorous and efficient semi-analytical method for the analysis of complex periodically time-varying linear systems using generalized Floquet scattering matrices (FSMs). Our approach can be applied to linear networks with an arbitrary number of periodically time-varying multi-port elements. As an example, this method is applied to an angular-momentum biased magnet-less circulator, showing excellent agreement with other numerical approaches.

articleTitle: Examination of the sensing radius of open-ended coaxial probes in dielectric measurements of biological tissues
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A number of emerging electromagnetic diagnostic and therapeutic devices are designed based on estimates of benign and malignant tissue dielectric properties at different frequencies and temperatures. Accurate tissue dielectric measurements are crucial for the development of these technologies. Although the dielectric measurement procedure is straightforward, several factors can introduce uncertainties and errors into dielectric data. These errors or confounders can be strictly related to the acquisition system or to the intrinsic properties of the investigated tissues. Generally, uncertainties are higher in the dielectric measurement of diseased tissues, due to their heterogeneity and complex structure and composition. These confounders can be minimized by clearly defining the measurement sensing volume, and characterizing the tissue distribution within that volume. The volume is defined by sensing depth and radius. In this work, early-stage experiments are presented to investigate the sensing radius for biological heterogeneous tissues, with the aim of providing more accurate dielectric measurements to support medical device development.

articleTitle: C-band self-oscillating active integrated antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a small-sized self-oscillating active antenna directly integrated microwave FET oscillator operating in C-band. A bended monopole lies over a truncated ground plane. One of ends directly connects to drain terminal of FET, other connects to gate terminal via weak-coupling gap. It forms a feedback loop circuit approximately. Characteristics of passive antenna and oscillator have been obtained using simulators. The proposed active antenna operates at 5.05 GHz. The passive antenna has end-fire radiating direction and 2.31 dBi realized gain. The output power spectrum shows that fundamental frequency has 10.1dBm power level.

articleTitle: Low-cost Gas Sensors utilizing mm-Wave Radars
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Carbon nanotube (CNT) gas sensors have been the subject of extensive research due to their electrical sensitivity to small quantities of gases. In this work, we demonstrate a novel concept system of a low-cost gas sensor utilizing a compact millimeter-wave radar operating at 60 GHz. Characterization of the mm-wave properties of CNTs on paper substrates is performed. When exposed to gas, significant changes in the magnitude of the backscattered signals from the CNT paper sensor can be observed. A compact mm-wave radar was used to interrogate the passive sensors and detect the changes in the backscattered signals, enabling real-time gas monitoring. Compared to prior art utilizing RF technologies, this new mm-wave enabled system promises to be of a much higher sensitivity with the potential of being realized at a much lower cost.

articleTitle: Multiview techniques for mm-wave imaging
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An analysis of different strategies for an efficient implementation of multiview millimeter-wave imaging systems is presented. The goal is to show the impact on Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image quality of different strategies to combine multiple SAR images obtained with a portable mm-wave scanner in order to obtain a full image of the area-under-scan. Simulation results for a 15 cm linear array working in the 75-79 GHz frequency band are presented.

articleTitle: Impacts of RF shimming on local SAR caused by MRI 3T birdcage coil near femoral plate implants
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Numerical studies of local specific absorption rate (SAR) were conducted for femoral plate implants in MRI 3T birdcage coil. Both the quadrature excitation and RF shimming conditions were evaluated in anatomical models of human body. All the results were normalized to 2W/kg average whole body SAR and Q-Matrices formalism method was used to improve the SAR calculation efficiency. The RF shimming procedure homogenize the magnitude of B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1+</sub> field in femur region. Under RF shimming condition both the value and location of the worst local SAR point were changed. The maximum local SAR is 573 W/kg under quadrature excitation condition and 154 under RF shimming condition. As the results suggested, significant impacts on local SAR near femoral plate implants due to RF shimming were observed.

articleTitle: Comparison of crossover recombination operators in GA-optimized sparse linear array design
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Mitigation of sidelobe energy in sparse array radiation patterns is often approached through numerical design of the array layout. In this work, a comparison of three different recombination operators in a genetic algorithm (GA) optimization routine is presented. The problem space explored is a distributed array consisting of multiple separate platforms and is modeled as a sparse linear array consisting of 9 elements within a span of 1000λ, each with a minimum distance of 50λ separation. The GA was used to optimize the location of the elements by minimizing the sidelobe energy within a 10° window.

articleTitle: Metamaterial-enhanced dual polarized HMSIW antenna for MIMO applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A metamaterial-enhanced dual-polarized antenna based on two half-mode SIW (HMSIW) resonators is presented. The dual polarization operation is realized by two orthogonally arranged HMSIW elements fed by the coaxial line probes. The isolation and the peak gain of the MIMO antenna are improved by a 2 × 8 metamaterial (MTM) array between the two HMSIW elements. The simulated isolation of this antenna is higher than 23 dB within the operation bandwidth and the maximum gain achieves 6.8 dBi for each polarization. This dual polarized HMSIW antenna has compact size and low profile and is suitable for Multiple-Input-Multiple-Output (MIMO) communication terminals.

articleTitle: Stroke detection based on an improved artificial fish swarm algorithm
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Stroke detection is to detect brain blood clot based on microwave imaging technology. To solve the stroke detection issue, this paper proposes an improved artificial fish swarm algorithm to overcome the problem of local optima, and to improve the global search ability and convergence speed. By the optimization of artificial fish swarm algorithm and brain simulation model, the stroke location is detected efficiently.

articleTitle: 3D-printed lens antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, we present a flat lens design using the Dial-a-Dielectric (DaD) approach to realize permittivities that are not available off-the-shelf. To show the efficacy of this design, we present comparison results with legacy design. We compare results of a flat lens using commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) materials combined with 3-D fabrication material. In contrast with the Transformation Optics approach, the present design does not employ metamaterials (MTMs) that can be narrowband and lossy.

articleTitle: Characterization of metascreens based on babinet's principle and generalized sheet transition conditions for metafilms
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The scattering properties of metascreens are characterized based on Babinet's principle and generalized sheet transition conditions for metafilms. Through this method, the reflection and transmission coefficients of metascreens could be computed analytically, under arbitrary incident angles and polarizations, once the surface susceptibilities of corresponding complementary metafilms have been extracted through two sets of simulations. The validity is demonstrated through comparison between analytical results and full-wave simulations.

articleTitle: Preliminary investigations into a simple and effective rectenna for RF energy harvesting
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Design, realisation and measurements of an effective rectenna system for dedicated wireless energy harvesting at 2.45 GHz ISM band are presented. The rectenna consists of a microstrip patch antenna array and a 2-stage Cockcroft Walton voltage multiplier circuit. The harvested power from a dedicated RF source is successfully used to operate a selection of typical electronic devices such as a 2.1v green LED, digital clock timer and digital humidity sensor, up to the range of 3.5 meters.

articleTitle: An on-body watchband antenna for the applications of wearable systems
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wearable antenna based on the metal watchband is proposed. A prototype of a TISSOT® classic watch is used for the demonstration. The width of the strap has a slight impact on the radiation patterns. However, the variations of the feeding position would sharply influence the matching performance. A fractional bandwidth of 77.8% could be obtained when feeding to the side of the dial at 2.46 GHz, which falls into the ISM (Industrial, Scientific, and Medical) band. The main lobe is fairly wide in both E and H plane, which enables the strap antenna a good adaptation for the versatile gestures of the arm. The measured results show good agreement with that of the simulations, which indicates the antenna a potential choice for the applications of wearable systems.

articleTitle: Impedance bandwidth of a slotted waveguide array: Impact of waveguide length and element shape
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The slotted waveguide array is a suitable as standalone antenna and subarray for large array antennas. Its design is complicated, in particular for understanding the impedance bandwidth. As a resonant array of resonant elements, the bandwidth is naturally small, but the role of the main parameters - the waveguide length, the number of slots, and the slot shapes - on the impedance bandwidth is not widely understood. This paper contributes a study which illuminates these roles. Analytic modelling of the slots and waveguide and their interaction is not yet sufficiently accurate to draw specific design conclusions. The complexity of configuration calls for a simulation approach. The results here give direct design information and can assist with formulating transmission line modelling. They show that the impedance bandwidth against the waveguide length for a given slot configuration follows a reasonable trend whereas the impact of the element shape is secondary, and is generally more complex for the larger bandwidths.

articleTitle: VHF/UHF Kapton supported antenna for cubesat applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper addresses an original concept for very low mass planar flexible Kapton supported antenna for cubesat application. In order to illustrate the concept a dual-band VHF/UHF planar cross dipole antenna is presented. This circularly polarized antenna is compatible with the integration requirements for a cubesat mission and demonstrates very good performances in terms of input matching and radiation pattern.

articleTitle: On controlling the propagation characteristics of microstrip transmission lines using embedded micron-sized particles and static h-fields
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Methods to control the propagation characteristics of printed microstrip transmission lines (TLs) has many uses in phased-array scanning, tunable apertures and reconfigurable antennas. In this paper, a unique method of changing the propagation along a microstrip TL with multiple magneto-static responsive structures (MRSs) is introduced. Each individual MRS is sub-wavelength in size and does not require a directly connected biasing circuit. In particular, the MRS consists of two parallel conducting planes separated by a dielectric material (forming a capacitor) and a cavity with micro particles that can be orientated/aligned (i.e., moved) using magneto-static fields. The particles can thus be manipulated using biasing fields such that the two conducting planes can then be connected and disconnected, changing the MRS state between capacitive (disconnected) and inductive (connected). The simulation and measurement results in this paper show that the effective permittivity of a 50Ω microstrip TL can be changed using MRSs.

articleTitle: A low-profile dual polarized antenna with enhanced bandwidth for 2.4 GHz WLAN application
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a novel low-profile dual polarized antenna for 2.4 GHz application. The proposed antenna consists of a circular patch with four curved T-stubs and a differential feeding network. Due to the parasitic loading of the curved T-stubs, the bandwidth has been improved. Good impedance matching and dual-polarization with low cross polarization have been achieved within 2.4-2.5 GHz, which is sufficient for WLAN application. The total thickness of the antenna is only 0.031A,<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub>, which is low-profile when compared with its counterparts.

articleTitle: A millimeter-wave connected antenna array for 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, a beam switched antenna system based on a planar connected antenna array (CAA) is proposed at 28 GHz for 5G applications. The antenna system consists of a 4 × 4 connected slot antenna elements. It is covering frequency band from 27.4 GHz to 28.23 GHz with at least -10dB bandwidth of 830 MHz. It is modeled on a commercially available RO3003 substrate with ϵ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> equal to 3.3. The dimensions of the board are equal to 61×54×0.13 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The proposed design is compact and low profile. A Butler matrix based feed network is used to steer the beam at different locations.

articleTitle: An accurate combined source integral equation for perfect electrically conducting bodies
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The electric field integral equation (EFIE) for perfect electrically conducting objects is augmented by a weak form combined source side condition. Thereby, the solution of the resulting combined source integral equation (CSIE) is unique and the interior resonance problem is circumvented. The discretization of electric and magnetic surface current densities and the testing of the electric field is solely performed with Rao-Wilton-Glission functions. Simulation results of scattering by a sphere demonstrate the good iterative solver convergence and excellent accuracy, as compared to EFIE as well as magnetic and combined field integral equations.

articleTitle: A wideband and wide-angle scanning circularly polarized array with low profile
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wideband and wide-angle scanning circularly polarized array with low profile is introduced. The proposed array is composed of three annular sub-arrays with tilted elements and a ripple-shaped ground plate. A case with 64 elements is designed and simulated. The simulation results demonstrates that array scanning gain fluctuations less than 2.26 dB at the center frequency and 3 dB in the operation bandwidth (from 8 GHz to 9.1 GHz) within two-dimensional scanning angles over ± 60°.

articleTitle: Active e-field gain: Toward a standard description of MEAs
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A Multi Element Antenna (MEA) is an array of antennas that can be driven independently. MEAs used by Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) wireless communication systems help optimize Capacity and Throughput under varying propagation environment conditions. This article describes the “Active E-field Gain” which, together with its NxN S-parameter matrix can completely describe an MEA.

articleTitle: Efficiency analysis of a conformal SCMR system for wearable devices
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The human body will be used to conduct measurements of efficiency in a wireless power transfer (WPT) system using Conformal Strongly Coupled Magnetic Resonance (SCMR). The test points for the human body are shown in figure. 2b below. We will analyze the SCMR systems response to different parts of the body and the impact they have on the efficiency of operation. Our analysis is conducted through accurate simulations and validated through physical implementation.

articleTitle: Planar sleeve antenna with left-handed choke structure
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A planar composite right/left-handed (CRLH) transmission line (TL) is applied to a choke structure of a sleeve antenna. The dispersion relation of the CRLH TL is designed as the left-handed (LH) branch at around 600 MHz. |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| characteristic and radiation patterns are calculated and compared with those of the conventional sleeve antennas. The length of the LH choke structure is 0.06 wavelength at 636 MHz.

articleTitle: Direction finding by time modulated linear array
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel direction finding method with the time modulated linear array (TMLA) is proposed and verified, by establishing the relationship between the incident angle and the generated harmonic characteristic matrix (HCM). The principle is that the generated HCM because of the periodical modulation varies with the incident direction of the RF signal. Compared to the existing direction finding method, the proposed method has simple structure and low calculation complexity. Numeric simulation is provided to examine its performance and an 8-element S-band TMLA is constructed to verify its effectiveness.

articleTitle: A single-source surface integral equation formulation for composite dielectric objects
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a single-source equivalence formulation to solve for the scattering from composite dielectric objects. In the proposed formulation, all regions of the composite dielectric object are replaced by the surrounding free space medium and an equivalent electric current density on their boundary. Since the formulation only uses a single equivalent current source, it requires 4 times less memory storage than the PMCHWT formulation, and could result in up to 8 times faster solution time.

articleTitle: Application of multiplicative regularization for electrical impedance tomography
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A multiplicative regularization scheme with edge-preserving characteristics is applied to the inversion of electrical impedance tomography (EIT) data. This scheme employs a multiplicative cost function of a weighted L2-norm regularization function and the data misfit function. It avoids the use of a weighting factor when the regularization term is added to the cost function and allows an adaptive weighting between data misfit and the regularization function. Gauss-Newton method is used to minimize the multiplicative cost function. In this work, we extend the weighted L2-norm regularization scheme onto a triangular grid with an updated formula for gradient and divergence operators. This scheme is tested using synthetic data. The reconstructed images show good piecewise constant characteristics and noise-resistance performance.

articleTitle: Antenna beamforming using multiplicative array processing
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Beamforming with conventional array processing utilizes linear, additive processing techniques to combine the signals from the different array elements. In this project, a multiplicative processing technique is proposed for combining the signals from antenna arrays for beamforming. The multiplicative processing technique is shown to emulate the performance of larger array apertures than the aperture size of the actual array measurements. Simulations are used to show that the proposed method produces direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimates commensurate with those produced by linear processing of measurements from much larger aperture sizes. It is also shown that the multiplicative processing of measurements from smaller apertures performs as well as linear processing of measurements from larger apertures, for separating signals from multiple sources. The sensitivity of the multiplicative processing technique to noise is also investigated.

articleTitle: Investigations on effects of finite ground plane on slot antennas using characteristic modes
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work attempts to investigate the effects of finite size of the embedding conducting plane on the performance of a simple narrow rectangular slot antenna. The slot mode is identified and a modal impedance modeling of the antenna is obtained using Theory of Characteristic Modes.

articleTitle: 7.2 to 1 ultra-wideband dual-linear polarized phased array with 60° scanning
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present an ultra-wideband dual-linear polarized phased array that scans down to 60° in both E and H planes. The dual-linear polarized array employs a tightly coupled dipole array (TCDA) topology that achieves an ultra-wide bandwidth from 2.5GHz to 18GHz (7.2:1) with total a height less than 12mm (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">low</sub>/10). The array consists of cross-located tightly coupled dipoles and is integrated with a folded Marchand balun that serve as an impedance transformer and a feeding network. To improve scanning performance, the traditional dielectric superstrate is replaced with a frequency selective surface (FSS) structure that facilitates fabrication process. The developed TCDA scans down to 60° in both E and H plane across the entire 7.2:1 band with voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) VSWR<;4. Corresponding port-to-port isolation is kept at less than 20dB at broadside and when scanning.

articleTitle: Reflector backed high gain photoconductive THz antenna using conical GaAs horn and Si lens
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A high gain photo-conductive antenna (PCA) using an optimal design of GaAs conical horn, Si lens and a gold reflector is proposed in this paper. Optimal design of GaAs horn, feeding circular waveguide-section and diameter of the aperture and hence Si-lens, dramatically increases the gain of the antenna. Proposed horn and Si-lens augmented antenna provides a maximum realized gain of 25 dBi along the axis of the horn. Undesired back radiation of the PCA is reduced by 10 dB using a gold reflector placed on the opposite side of the horn and Lens. Proposed high gain photoconductive antenna design concept can be used for designing efficient THz radiators.

articleTitle: Sidelobe level and sideband suppression in time-modulated linear arrays by NSGA-II
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel approach based on nondominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) is proposed to suppress sidelobe level (SLL) and sideband level (SBL) in time-modulated linear antenna arrays. The SLL and SBL of a time-modulated linear array can be reduced by optimizing the excitation amplitudes as well as the switch-on time intervals of each element. A 32-element linear array has been synthesized to show the effectiveness of the approach.

articleTitle: Miniaturized implantable patch antenna for near-field communication at ISM band
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present an implantable patch antenna designed for near-field communication with an external repeater device. The geometry is composed of a X-slot and four T-slots that increase the electric-length, thus miniaturizing the antenna, achieving a diameter of just 8 mm (0.064λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>) for an antenna operation at 2.4 GHz. Moreover, the input reflection coefficient exhibits robust performance for different implantation depths. Lastly, we calculate a maximum input power imposed by Specific Absorption Rate regulation, according to Federal Communications Commission (FCC) and International Commission on Non-Ionizing Radiation Protection (ICNIRP).

articleTitle: Planar metasurface for parabolic reflector antenna: Frequency agility and beam steering
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A planar reconfigurable metasurface is used as a parabolic reflector for antenna applications. The metasurface is composed of unit cells incorporating voltage-controlled varactor diodes, where the dispersion responses of the cells can be tailored. The phase characteristics of a parabolic reflector is engineered by judiciously controlling the bias voltage of the varactor diodes on the planar metasurface. The metasurface is illuminated by a microstrip patch antenna. Performed measurements show a directive radiated beam from the antenna system. Frequency agility and beam steering performances are also produced by reconfiguring the metasurface reflector.

articleTitle: Mutual coupling reduction in millimeter-wave MIMO dielectric resonator antenna using metamaterial polarization rotator wall
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An effective technique for reducing the mutual coupling between two mm-wave ridge-gap dielectric resonator antennas (DRA) using a novel technique is investigated and presented. This is achieved by embedding a metamaterial polarization rotator (MPR) wall between the two DRAs, which are placed in the H-plane. Using the proposed MPR wall, the TE and TM modes of the antenna become orthogonal which reduces the mutual coupling between the two DRAs. The proposed MPR wall is composed of 7×2 unit cells along the E-plane. The mutual coupling is reduced between 8 to 14 dB when the proposed MPR wall is placed between the antennas. Moreover, the proposed MPR wall does not affect the antenna characteristics.

articleTitle: Ultra small dual band antenna design for implantable devices
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present an ultra small dual band antenna for both wireless power transmission (WPT) and radio frequency communication (RFC). A novel LC resonator circuit is applied for signal isolation of two frequency bands. We have shown the transmission performance of both WPT and RFC based on the simple circuit theory. The designed antenna is fabricated with the size of 7 × 7 × 0.65 mm. It achieves -11.2 dB WPT effciency and -38.6 dB RF antenna gain from 1 cm inside a human body phantom, both of which are state-of-the art performance at the same antenna volume.

articleTitle: A 28 GHz compact vertically-polarized dipole for 5G smartphone edge
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a compact 28 GHz vertically-polarized SIW-fed dipole for future 5G smartphones. The dipole is implemented using vias in standard PCB process to fit at the edge of the smartphone providing fan-beam in the elevation plane for wide coverage. Additional parasitic vias are employed in front of the dipole to serve as directors for enhanced gain achieving 7 dBi peak gain. Also a via fence is added surrounding the dipole to suppress back radiation. The fabricated prototype achieves 2.7 GHz matching bandwidth, 96% radiation efficiency, 16 dB front-to-back radiation ratio and 96° fan-beam coverage in the elevation plane.

articleTitle: Wideband low-profile circular polarization slot antenna based on metasurface
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wideband low-profile circular polarization (CP) slot antenna is proposed based on the corner-cut square metasurface structure. Both simulations and measurements are performed to demonstrate the CP antenna and good agreements are obtained. The proposed antenna exhibits a measured impedance matching bandwidth of 32% and an AR bandwidth of 20% centered at 5.6 GHz.

articleTitle: Modeling and measuring of antenna array s-parameters and radiation efficiency
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The S-parameters of an electrically small antenna, modeled as a 2-port device can be calculated using specifically sized Wheeler caps. However, having antenna S-parameters are not sufficient for modeling S-parameters of an array of antennas as that does not model mutual antenna coupling. This paper proposes a model, which accounts for mutual coupling, and permits the calculation of array S-parameters. It is achieved by modeling mutual coupling as a 2-port device connecting the antenna element 2-port devices. In this paper, a two-element antenna array was used to demonstrate the operation of the model. Signal flow diagram of the model is presented and equations to calculate the radiation efficiency were derived. A two-element antenna array prototype was fabricated with two identical monopoles positioned greater than λ/2 apart at all frequencies of interest. The proposed model was verified using experimental outcomes and simulations for four frequency points. Derived equations can be applied directly to determine the radiation efficiency of a two-element antenna array. This model can be extended to a larger antenna arrays as well.

articleTitle: Feed system optimization for convex conformal reflectarray antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this communication, the possibility of enhancing the performances of Convex conformal Reflectarray Antennas (CRA) adopting an ad-hoc feed system properly designed is investigated. In particular, a feed horn with proper illumination of the here considered CRA has been designed, exploiting particular tecniques. The results show an increase of the efficiency (from 28% to about 46%), with respect to the case in which the same reflector is illuminated by a rectangular horn [4]. Further enhancement of SLL and bandwidth have also been obtained.

articleTitle: Wideband single-layer Fabry-Pérot cavity antenna with a radial variation of the cavity permittivity
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broadband single-layer Fabry-Pérot Cavity antenna formed by a thin metallic frequency-selective-surface over a grounded non-uniform dielectric slab having a radial variation in the permittivity is designed. The performance of the proposed design is investigated using full-wave simulations.

articleTitle: A wideband CPW-fed monopole antenna with linear and circular polarizations
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A coplanar-waveguide (CPW)-fed monopole antenna for applications of the multi-system integration has been presented in this study. The enhancement of impedance bandwidth and circular polarization in the microstrip rectangular monopole antenna using following techniques: using asymmetrical CPW feeding structure and adding three grounded sleeve strips. By tuning the width of one side of the CPW ground plane, increase of impedance bandwidth and excitation of circular polarization at 1.57 GHz are achieved. Three parasitic inverted-L conducted strips are connected to the ground plane to further extend the impedance bandwidth. The measured impedance bandwidth of a S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> <; -6 dB ranges from 0.65 to 2.85 GHz and the measured 3-dB axial-ratio bandwidth is about 150 MHz. The proposed antenna covers most of commercial wireless communication systems, such as GSM, GPS, DCS, PCS, IMT-2000, WLAN, and LTE.

articleTitle: 4× 2-slot element for 30-GHz planar array antenna realized using SIW cavity and fed by microstrip line line-ridge gap waveguide
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 4 × 2 planar rectangular slot antenna array is designed at 30 GHz. The rectangular slots are etched off in the top layer of substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) Cavity. SIW Cavity fed by a printed feeding network based on the ridge gap waveguide (RGW) technology through a coupling slot. A prototype working at 30 GHz band was designed and simulated. Simulated results show that the prototype achieves a-10-dB impedance bandwidth from 29 to 31 GHz (6.67%). The peak gain at broadside is 13.3 dBi at 30 GHz. The radiation pattern is stable within the operating bandwidth.

articleTitle: An equivalent-circuit model of miniaturized split-ring resonator
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present a new miniaturized split-ring resonator (SRR) to be easily employed in the practical realization of SRRs and derive its equivalent circuit model to accurately predict the resonance frequency. The results of the resonance frequency obtained by the developed equivalent circuit model are in very good agreement with the simulated results.

articleTitle: Efficient environment model for intra-wagon millimeter wave ray-tracing simulation
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In the intra-wagon scenario, extensive structures such as the carriage roof, the glass of windows, luggage racks, etc., influence wave propagation. Through building up a variety of intra-wagon models based on different levels of detail of the relevant objects, ray-tracing simulations are made for millimeter wave channels. By comparing with characteristics in the delay and angular domains, we determine the most suitable environment model that can enable designers to attain ideal accuracy of simulation as well as high efficiency for network planning.

articleTitle: Series-fed planar dipole array antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A planar dipole array antenna operating around 2.4 GHz is presented. The array has five dipole elements that are excited in phase to reduce the elevation beamwidth for reducing undesired multipath signals and increase gain. The array is fed from the bottom with a single coaxial connector which sequentially excites all array elements in phase via a twin wire transmission line. The antenna is just 8mm wide and 1.27mm thick.

articleTitle: Materials for liquid RF electronics: Long term operation of gallium liquid metal alloys in reconfigurable RF applciations
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Room temperature liquid electronics offers the potential of rewiring and reconfiguring functionality in real-time. One of the most promising materials recently explored for these components is gallium liquid metal alloys (GaLMAs) because of their non-toxic and self-healing properties. Unfortunately the reactive nature of the surface, with both oxygen to form a thin viscoelastic skin and alloy formation with solid metal electrodes, results in the need for better control over these interfaces. This control needs to be achieved while maintaining appropriate RF properties and reliability of the fluidic electronic components. In this work, we provide a new material set to control the interface of GaLMAs and characterize the effects on RF performance.

articleTitle: Conformal Cavity-Backed slot antenna embedded in a conical platform for end-fire radiation
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a low-profile cavity-backed slot antenna embedded into a conical platform to achieve end-fire radiation. Three closely spaced slots are etched out of the cavity wall to achieve supergain as well as to broaden the bandwidth. Simulated results show that the conformal antenna can achieve an impedance bandwidth from 9.3 to 10.81 GHz and maximum gain of 9.5 dBi. A prototype of the conformal array configuration with six separate antenna elements is fabricated and tested. Measured results are in good agreement with simulated ones.

articleTitle: Alignment correction for antenna scans in imaging
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose a software correction technique to eliminate the misalignment errors in the measurement of antenna radiated fields for frequency-diverse imaging. It is shown that by using RF fiducials integrated into the antennas, the effect of rotation (range and cross-range) and offset misalignment errors can be corrected to a good accuracy, holding significant potential for applications where precise alignment is required for antenna field measurements.

articleTitle: Development of a circularly polarized L-band SAR deployable mesh reflector antenna for microsatellite earth observation
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The first circularly polarized L-band synthetic aperture radar (CP-SAR) antenna on-board the small satellite mission GAIA-II is presented. The antenna is a deployable mesh reflector antenna, with gain larger than 30 dBic and narrowband around center frequency of 1.275 GHz. The main mission of GAIA-II is land deformation monitoring and disaster prevention and mitigation. The current work describes the development of a compact CP L-band antenna onboard the microsatellite CP-SAR, focusing the design & simulation of the reflector dish and structures.

articleTitle: A conformal dual-polarized all-metal vivaldi array for feeding broadband luneburg lens
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper demonstrates a design of dual-polarized Vivaldi array to feed high-gain broadband Luneburg lens. The proposed conformal Vivaldi array, placed around the lens surface, is composed of 8 × 4 horizontal polarized elements and 7 × 3 vertical polarized elements. The performance of the entire 3-D graded index Luneburg lens antenna (30 cm diameter) has been evaluated based on simulated radiation patterns using commercial full-wave electromagnetic software.

articleTitle: Doppler radar phenomenology in small commercial unmanned aerial systems
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper discusses the Doppler radar signature of the spinning blades of a small commercial unmanned aerial system (UAS). This phenomenology is closely related to the well-known jet engine modulation (JEM) effect on the radar signature. We analyze this signature using analytical, numerical and experimental methods, all based on the Doppler spectrum of the radar response. This procedure's goal is to detect the presence of a rotating object and estimate its spinning rate. Our preliminary results show that operating the radar at high frequencies should afford more robust detection of the JEM signature in the presence of noise, clutter and interference.

articleTitle: Accuracy preserving computation of asymptotically smoothed layered medium Green's functions in finite precision arithmetic
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The catastrophic cancellation due to singularity subtraction when computing layered medium Green's functions (LMGFs) is discussed. An efficient and accurate method based on Taylor series expansions is proposed for computing LMGFs to a prescribed accuracy in finite precision arithmetic.

articleTitle: A frequency tunable origami spherical helical antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel origami spherical helical antenna. This antenna operates in normal mode and its operating frequency is tunable from 1.77 GHz to 2.32 GHz for applications of TV or Radio stations. By tuning the scaling factor of each step on the origami pattern, the fabricating process can be greatly simplified, and this antenna can be fabricated at a low cost on light-weight planar substrate.

articleTitle: E-plane RWG-to-SIW Transition Power Splitter for Ka-Band SATCOM Application
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A transition power splitter, consisting of metallic rectangular waveguide and substrate integrated waveguide, is presented for large-scale millimeter-wave antenna array systems. The power is coupled between the RWG and the SIW through two centre-slot transition, one etched on the SIW ground plane and the other cut through metallic RWG narrow side wall. The 3-dB RWG-SIW (T-junction) transition splitter was designed and simulated by the HFSS full-wave solver. The simulated S-parameters of the splitter is presented, showing a return loss (RL) better than 10 dB and insertion loss (IL) are better than 0.60 dB.

articleTitle: Wideband FSS superstrate for millimeter-wave antenna gain enhancement
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wideband Frequency Selective Surfaces (FSS) which is used as a superstrate for a patch antenna to form a high-gain resonant cavity antenna is presented. This FSS consists of two metal structures separated by a substrate in the middle. It exhibits a wide stop-band in the 60GHz band. Further a panel of this FSS is implemented as a superstrate for antenna gain enhancement. It is observed that a broadband gain enhancement of 5.9dB with variations less than 2dB throughout the operating band is obtained.

articleTitle: Discretely-sampled partial aperture receiver for orbital angular momentum modes
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Spatial modes, such as orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes, are of interest for creating high spectral-efficiency line-of-sight wireless links in propagation environments with limited diversity gain. Four-element receive arrays have been designed using a Monte-Carlo method so as to enable the simultaneous reception of four different OAM modes. A test-bed operating in the 5GHz band has been developed to validate the principle experimentally. The test bed's transmitter is an eight-element uniform circular array, which allows the generation of OAM modes with mode numbers l = ϵ {±3, ±2, ±1,0}. The receiver is a four element array, and all elements in the transmit and receive arrays have a dedicated programmable phase shifter to facilitate rapid adjustment between modes.

articleTitle: Power harvesting for wearable electronics using fabric electrochemistry
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a new method of power harvesting for wearable electronics that is based on epidermal electrochemical dressings dampened by a bodily exudate (sweat, wound exudate, etc.). Generation of DC power is achieved via an electrochemical process that enables transfer of electrons from silver-to zinc-printed dots using the bodily exudate as an electrolyte. Contrary to existing power harvesting methods (e.g., RF or solar), the proposed method is fully-flexible and does not require bulky circuits or any sort of rigid components. Proof-of-concept results are presented, demonstrating: a) unobtrusive DC power generation in the μW range, and b) a batteryless epidermal sensor that identifies open wounds underneath its surface. Overall, this technology is expected to be of utmost significance for powering wearable electronics in military, healthcare, sports, and emergency applications, among others.

articleTitle: Broadband RCS reduction by gradient index meta-surface composed of Jerusalem-shaped patches
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A gradient index meta-surface composed of Jerusalem-shaped unit cells is proposed to provide a discontinuous reflected phase gradient distribution for manipulating incident wave in broadband. The Jerusalem-shaped unit cells are located on a high dielectric constant substrate with a perfect conducting ground, and their sizes are adjusted to achieve a desired gradient phase distribution. The proposed meta-surface can focus the reflected wave to fixed angles, which exhibits potential application in backward scattering reduction. Both the simulation and measurement results show that the backward radar cross section (RCS) of the proposed meta-surface can be reduced as large as 10 dB within the range from 16.5 GHz to 22.5 GHz, comparing with that of the metal plate with the same size.

articleTitle: Efficiency improvement in TMA using complementary mode switching
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes complementary mode switching to increase efficiency of Time Modulated Arrays. The complementary mode is defined in the paper and the corresponding radiation pattern is studied. It is shown that the radiation pattern of sidebands is not changed, while power level in the fundamental harmonic has 16.6 dB enhancement for a 20 element linear array, which is highly desired for wireless communication.

articleTitle: A broadband microstrip array antenna with rectangular waveguide mode transition at millimeter-wave band
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a broadband microstrip array antenna with rectangular waveguide mode transition operating at lower E-band is proposed. The microstrip array antenna is corporate-feed structure configured by microstrip line with a mode transition from rectangular waveguide. Broadband operation can be achieved by using a slit in the transition and employing a set of feed point in the center of microstrip-line feeder which also results in fixed-beam radiation. Validity is confirmed by the evaluation of a fabricated antenna. This antenna is suitable for E-band applications such as mobile back-haul.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave thin metasurface enabling polarization-controlled beam shaping
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel Metasurface exhibiting different beam shaping characteristics according to the polarization of incident waves. The Metasurface is composed of numerous unit cells operating as a spatial phase filter providing different phase shifts depending to the incident polarization. Metallic patterns constituting the unit cell are designed to have different geometry along the two dimensional direction utilizing the proposed design methodologies. It is demonstrated that this structure can have different reactance value depending on the polarized direction of the incident waves. The proposed Metasurface is designed by arranging combinations of the unit cells having passband characteristic but different phase variations as a function of the incident polarization at 28 GHz. Finally, it is demonstrated that for x-polarized waves the proposed Metasurface operates as a convex lens achieving 13 dB gain enhancement while for y-polarized waves the Metasurface operates as frequency selective surface (FSS) just providing passband property without any gain enhancement.

articleTitle: A frequency selective surface with nano square ring resonators for enhancing banknote security
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a frequency selective surface designed with nano square ring resonators (SRRs) as a security feature on banknote. Each SRR is in nanoscale and operates in the wavelength of 400–700 nm. SRR is made of aluminum on polyethylene terephthalate (PET) substrate and top coating. Simulations are performed on 3 SRR models to study the effects of physical geometrical changes on the reflection (|S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>|) and transmission (|S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>|) coefficients. The lowest |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| is −25.91 dB achieved by model C, at incident wavelength of 750 nm and |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>| maximum of −3.355 dB at incident wavelength of 705.88 nm. When a frequency selective surface with SRRs is incorporated onto a banknote, the front and rear sides can display colors differently under white light, as shown in the results.

articleTitle: Power amplifier and antenna integration utilizing capacitively coupled feeding mechanism
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new integration technique for antenna and Power Amplifier (PA) without complex impedance matching network is presented. This method helps to reduce the losses, power consumption and overall size of the RF front-end modules without affecting the efficiency of the PA. This design technique utilizes a capacitively coupled feeding mechanism to control the input impedance of the antenna. By optimizing the antenna dimension the impedance of first two harmonics (2.4 and 4.8 GHz) of a Class-B PA can be matched without additional matching circuit and the PA can provide a maximum efficiency of 70% at the operating frequency of 2.4 GHz. Thus, the proposed integration technique reduces the overall size of the RF front-end module without affecting the output efficiency of the PA. The antenna provides an axial beam with a maximum gain of 6.18 dBi and 87% radiation efficiency.

articleTitle: A wideband, circularly polarized slot antenna
