Three benchmark functions were used to assist in the selection of such crucial PSO parameters as population size and maximum number of iterations. The optimal RCA has a peak gain of 19.6 dB, overall 3-dB gain bandwidth of 55% and a small footprint.

articleTitle: Scattering studies on sorted materials of high-speed rail scenario for propagation channel simulations
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The accurate deterministic modeling for wireless channel is required tools especially at high frequency, such as ray tracing which can be regarded as a superposition of the line-of-sight (LOS), reflected, diffracted, scattered rays. In this study, we fully investigate the constructive materials in high speed railway scenario in the first place, and extract the dominant materials for scattering character measuring. The measurement campaign is well design for future deducing material permittivity and development of scattering model of these materials.

articleTitle: Modeling and dielectric characterization of EMI/EMC ground test for the evaluation of the electric propulsion thruster emissions
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new EMI test facility for electric propulsion (EP) thrusters has been developed at Aerospazio Tecnologie. The facility consists of a cylindrical dielectric vacuum tank placed in a semi-anechoic room, connected through a gate valve to a Large Vacuum Test Facility. The electromagnetic characterisation of the facility, along with subsequent measures of the radiated emissions of a Hall effect thruster, is presented.

articleTitle: Chirp scaling algorithms for SAR imaging under high squint angles
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Four improved chirp scaling algorithms (CSAs) are proposed to reconstruct images from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data received at high squint angles. The proposed methods reconstruct better SAR images with less computational load and memory than the conventional CSA.

articleTitle: Normal vs tangential polarizations in metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this study we categorize metasurfaces with respect to the direction of their polarization currents i.e., either tangential or normal to the metasurface plane. We theoretically investigate whether or not normal polarization currents can add extra degrees of freedom in engineering the reflection and transmission characteristics of functional metasurfaces. We then present a general formalism in which two different metasurface design scenarios with distinct polarization directions perform equally in engineering desired reflection and/or transmission properties. The result of our study provides a valuable tool to choose the most convenient approach in the design of functional metasurfaces.

articleTitle: Integrated two-beam antenna array featuring dual-circular polarization
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A concept of an integrated antenna array featuring two independent beams and dual circular polarization has been described. The antenna array consists of two radiating elements which are excited at two orthogonally placed feeding ports with the use of four appropriately connected 3-dB/90° directional couplers. Therefore, such an array generates two symmetrically located beams having right-handed circular polarization (RHCP) and identical two beams having left-handed circular polarization (LHCP). The presented concept has been verified by the design and measurements of an antenna array operating at 2.4 GHz frequency range.

articleTitle: Single-pixel mm-wave imaging using 8-bits metamaterial-based compressive reflector antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a single-pixel millimeter-wave (mm-wave) imaging system, capable of performing spectral coding by using a Compressive Reflector Antenna (CRA). The CRA is designed by coating the surface of a parabolic reflector with 8-bits metamaterial absorbers (MMAs). By specially designing the codes, the mutual information between successive measurements is reduced, leading to an enhanced sensing capacity. The imaging performance of the proposed mm-wave imaging system is evaluated using synthetic data. Preliminary results show that the proposed 8-bits metamaterial-based CRA system outperforms the equivalent one without MMAs in terms of imaging quality and sensing capacity.

articleTitle: Dual-polarized fixed-beam high-gain array antenna for microwave and mm-wave applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: There is a long-standing need for low-profile antennas with fixed-direction high gain in both polarizations. The design challenge for such an an array is that the elements and feed should be low loss and low cost. A new design using crossed slot elements for such a broadside fixed array is presented. The structure comprises an array of sub-arrays of slot elements with waveguide feeding. The design has excellent radiation properties (gain, pattern shape, polarization purity, bandwidth) and is suitable for microwave and millimeter-wave frequencies. An example design is presented that has a gain of 12 dBi, aperture efficiency of 54%, and a polarization isolation of 40 dB, all over a bandwidth close to 10%. An advantage of this structure is its scalability to increase its size and provide higher gain without major modifications and without increasing the loss significantly - a major advantage of waveguide-fed slot arrays. For example, the radiation efficiency of a 4×4 array using aluminum is ~99% from simulation.

articleTitle: Wideband frequency analysis using volume surface integral equation and taylor series expansion
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper present a Galerkin-type method of moments (MoM) solution of volume surface integral equation (VSIE) and Taylor series expansion (TSE). This VSIE-TSE scheme is developed for the wideband frequency analysis of composite metallic and dielectric (CMD) structures. By expanding the exponential of the Green's function into a Taylor series, the impedance matrices can be efficiently calculated and generated, when the frequency sweeping process. In comparison with the conventional VSIE method, our scheme requires much less computational time while the accuracy remains at the same level. Several numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the VSIE-TSE scheme.

articleTitle: A conformal rotman lens
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: One of the challenges of designing UAVs is the limited amount of interior space for components. The communication, navigation, and radar systems all compete for this limited space. Phased array antenna systems, in turn, save space, weight, and power by steering the antenna electrically versus mechanically. Rotman lens devices (Fig. 1) are a particularly efficient means providing the correct amplitude and phase waveform inputs to a phased array antenna to allow this steering. However, the elongated, flat shape of a Rotman lens makes it cumbersome to fit the confines of a UAV.

articleTitle: Scattering properties of parity-time symmetric nanoparticle dimers
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We study the unusual scattering response of a parity-time (PT) symmetric pair of subwavelength nanoparticles with complex conjugate permittivities. The poles and zeros of the scattering cross section are analytically derived, showing intriguing properties. In the complex plane of the relative permittivity, we find interesting opportunities for scattering engineering, including conditions for extremely low or large scattering efficiencies that can be merged together to induce very sharp scattering features. Our results pave the way to a plethora of novel phenomena in nanophotonics based on balanced loss and gain.

articleTitle: WLAN wideband-notched UWB slot antenna using I-shaped MTM
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A miniaturized UWB polygon-slot antenna with WLAN wideband-notched Characteristics is presented. The proposed planar coplanar waveguide-fed antenna has a wideband-notched property from 5.3 to 5.9 GHz, is realized by one pair I-shaped MTM unit cells symmetrically etched on the fork-shaped patch. The antenna is fabricated onto low-cost FR4 substrate, and its overall dimensions are 21.5×19 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. It provides impedance bandwidth of 124% covering from 3.1 to 13.3 GHz rejecting band notch, a maximum gain of 4.1 dBi at 10.9 GHz, high radiation efficiency over 86% and nearly stable radiation patterns.

articleTitle: Simple beam control of end-fire antenna using FSS for MM-wave applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a simple beam tilting of an end-fire antenna by integrating a Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) at 30 GHz is proposed. A modified uniplanar compact FSS (MUC-FSS) is designed to obtain a bandpass in the desired direction and a bandstop in the other direction. Simulation results of integrating the proposed FSS (1 layer of 3×5 unit cells) under the directors of the antenna show that the main beam radiation tilts in the end-fire direction by +27° and -17° when the FSS structures are rotated by 90° at 30 GHz. A bandwidth from 28GHz to 33 GHz and a realized gain of 11dB are obtained from simulation, without much variation, for the antenna when adding the periodic structure.

articleTitle: Floquet analysis of parametric huygens' metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An exact Floquet analysis is proposed to determine the steady-state response a uniform parametric Huygens' metasurface. Under periodic modulation of the resonant frequencies of the Lorentzian surface susceptibilities of the metasurface, the unknown scattered fields are expressed as Floquet series. Using the Floquet form of the fields in conjunction with the Generalized Sheet Transition Conditions (GSTCs), the amplitudes of the new harmonic components are then conveniently determined by solving the resulting set a linear fields equations.

articleTitle: Error analysis for time modulated arrays
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we study the effect of hardware non-idealities on the performance of Time Modulated Arrays (TMAs). In a TMA structure, RF switches are used to shape the beam and steer it. A real switch has a nonzero switching time, which could be different from one switch to another one. In this paper, considered implanted eight element array in the presence of errors, which errors have reasonable ranges and then compare real patterns with the ideal pattern for four harmonics. Frequency of carrier is 1.3GHz and switching frequency is 1MHz. Different time errors have a little effect on beam pointing and beam width error. For side lobe level (SLL) error, various error sources have same influence on different harmonic. But maximum power of main lobe error has more depend on the harmonics, higher harmonic means more error.

articleTitle: Frequency-domain interferometric imaging and velocity vector estimation using networked ultra-wideband 80-GHz array radar systems
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: For tracking multiple moving targets, a multi-radar system employing ultra-wideband millimeter-wave array antennas is introduced. To separate the multiple echoes and the different Doppler velocities of the targets, the frequency-domain interferometric technique is used and is followed by an interferometric imaging process. The system consists of multiple radar modules that are well-separated, allowing measurements of the Doppler velocities from different lines of sight. Thus, in addition to constructing high-resolution images, the multi-radar system is able to estimate the velocity vector of each target, which has been demonstrated in practice through measurements.

articleTitle: Applications of using conformal SCMR system for batteryless wearable sensor device
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Two wearable sensor applications by using Conformal Strongly Coupled Magnetic Resonance (SCMR) wireless power transfer (WPT) system is presented. SCMR system was used to replace the battery system in these wearable sensors. The advantage of removing battery system with a WPT system is presented. Design of different shape SCMR transmitter/receiver is also discussed and demonstrated in this paper.

articleTitle: A novel polarization independent angularly stable high impedance surface for antenna miniaturization
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel ultrathin high impedance surface (HIS) whose response is independent of polarization and incidence angle of the incident wave is presented. The proposed HIS reflects the incident electromagnetic wave with unity magnitude and zero phase reversal over the operating frequency band 1.7–3 GHz. Due to very small unit cell size 0.1λ, the surface does not cause any scattering and surface waves. The designed HIS is then applied to a standard patch antenna to improve the gain. The use of HIS results in a very compact antenna design as compared to the conventional ground plane that must be placed at distance of λ/4 to attain maximum gain. Increase in gain, compactness in size and prevention of the surface waves are the major advantages achieved by using proposed HIS instead of conventional ground plane.

articleTitle: Study of microwave energy localization in human tissue
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a study of the microwave energy localization for pathologic treatment of the knee in human tissue. For the computational study, we have developed the finite difference time domain (FDTD) electromagnetic (EM) solver and FDTD thermal solver. The simulation test using these solver was performed for a 2D knee model with the tumor at 915 MHz. The time reversal (TR) algorithm was proposed the effective beam focusing at the target position. The detailed results are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Multi-layer dielectric rod antenna with stable patterns over decade bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A six-layer dielectric rod antenna is designed for symmetric and stabilized wide-beam radiation from 4 to 40 GHz. The desired HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> mode is excited in the rod by means of a 50-Ω Vivaldi feeding within a compact overall antenna structure. The study shows that the antenna has symmetric patterns with VSWR below 2:1, efficiency above 75%, and E/H-plane 10-dB beamwidths over 100° over the examined frequency band.

articleTitle: Tri-band planar monopole antenna with dual band circular polarization
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A tri-band planar monopole antenna with dual band circular polarization for 3G, WiMAX and WLAN applications is presented. The antenna consists of monopole arms on one side of an FR4 substrate attached to a slotted feedline and a slotted ground plane on the other side of the same substrate. The antenna has a total size of 25 × 35 × 1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Measured results show that the antenna has a -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 9.7% (2.05-2.26 GHz) for the lower band, 11.3% (3.41-3.82 GHz) for the middle band and 60.2% (4.89-9.11 GHz) for the upper band. The simulated axial ratio (AR) bandwidths are 4.4% (3.55-3.71 GHz) and 57.9% GHz (4.69-8.52 GHz).

articleTitle: On the impact of velocity on the train-to-earth MIMO propagation channel: Statistical observations and qualitative analysis
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We provide measured data collected from 97 trains completing over 7000 journeys in Sweden showing that the throughput over LTE is impacted by train velocity. In order to explain these observations we assume that the underlying causes can be found in the implementation of the MIMO system into LTE Rel. 8 and the diffuse scattering of signals from ground reflections.

articleTitle: Long slot Van Atta array for far-field wireless power transfer
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of a Van Atta array of long slots is presented for far-field wireless power transfer (WPT). The proposed array overcomes the scanning and bandwidth limitations of Van Atta arrays based on resonant elements for WPT applications. The proposed array consists of four slots with eight input ports, resulting in 32 access points. The Van Atta scheme is implemented by connecting pairs of input ports with coaxial cables. Measurements validate the design at a center frequency of 5.8 GHz. Monostatic RCS measurements show that the array has a -10 dB beamwidth of about 118° in the E-plane. The scanning performance of the array is preserved in the considered band: 4.8-6.2 GHz.

articleTitle: A compact 4-element LTE MIMOantenna design for mobile phone
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The channel capacity of a MIMO (Multiple Input Multiple Output) system is affected greatly by the mutual coupling (MC) between antenna elements in the case of the compact configuration. In this paper, a compact 4×4 multi-band MIMO antenna system with high isolation and low correlation for mobile handsets is presented. Each antenna element has the size of 30×12×7mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The average measured efficiency of the proposed antenna is 45% at low band (701-785 MHz) and 74% at high band (1710-2690 MHz). Both the simulated and measured isolations are less than -12 dB, and the envelope correlation coefficients basically satisfy the communication requirements.

articleTitle: Antenna design for ultra-compact Bluetooth devices
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a solution for an ultra-compact antenna for small Bluetooth devices. The work considers the battery and the electronic components influence in the antenna design process for a real device, i.e. a Bluetooth tracker. Three different models for representing the battery and the main electronic components are studied: (i) a simple model that represents both battery and components by a ground plane; (ii) a model that represents the battery realistically and the components by a ground plane and (iii) a model that represents realistically both battery and components.

articleTitle: Direction of arrival estimation using compact MIMO array for portbale devices
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Accurate direction of arrival (DOA) estimation attracts more intention for smart devices in wireless communication. However, designing compact antenna array for estimation with high accuracy is challenging. In this work, a closely packed MIMO array is particularly designed for proper amplitude ratio over different angles. Combining with the phase information, the accuracy and robustness of the estimation is improved, with phase ambiguity eliminated as well. Simulation results show that the proposed MIMO array obtains a maximum and averaged RMS error of 2 degrees and less than 1 degree, respectively, over the entire azimuth plane with an SNR of 10 dB. It performs well at both high and low SNR scenarios, and can be easily integrated in devices such as Wi-Fi router.

articleTitle: Exploiting antenna array configurations for efficient simultaneous wireless information and power transfer
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Different patch antenna array configurations for Simultaneous Wireless Information and Wireless Power Transfer - SWIPT - were simulated and evaluated. The scope of the work is to provide configurations that can be used to minimise the interference between information and power transfer as well as provide some beamforming capabilities. Our assumption for all the evaluated structures are that two receive antennas are used for RF energy harvesting and one antenna is used for information exchange. The choice for two antennas for energy harvesting is based on that a differential DC output full-wave rectifier is used. Our analysis is based on patch antennas.

articleTitle: An LTCC beam-switching antenna with high beam overlap for 60-GHz mobile access points
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We present a flat switched-beam antenna that achieves a wide angular coverage (±38°) and limited scan losses in V-band. The system features two broadband continuous transverse stub (CTS) arrays, each fed by a pillbox beamformer. The two antennas are designed so that the radiated beams are interleaved. In this way, high beam overlap levels (-3 dB) and low side lobe level are simultaneously attained. A switch network excites one of the two apertures at a time and selects the desired beam. The system is fully integrated in a low-profile multilayer low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) module. The proposed architecture and technology are suitable for millimeter-wave access points in next generation mobile networks.

articleTitle: Virtual Humans for antenna/implant modeling
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Numerical simulation of the electromagnetic, thermal and mechanical responses of the human body to different stimuli in MRI safety, antenna research, electromagnetic tomography, and electromagnetic stimulation is currently limited by the availability of anatomically adequate and numerically efficient cross-platform computational models or “virtual humans”. The objective of this presentation is provide a comprehensive review of modern human models and body region models available around the world and their important features. The major emphasis is made on various model applications in Computational Electromagnetics (CEM) and antenna-related research.

Author Keywords: CEM applications in medical fields electromagnetic safety assessment

articleTitle: The vertigo array for grating lobe reduction
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes a new grating lobe-reduction technique that uses the concept of sparse or aperiodic arrays. This method does not affect the gain and HPBW with respect to a uniform lattice. The method implements an iterative analytic formulation, which is based on a geometric transformation of the element position, starting from an initial uniform lattice. In addition, the method implements criteria for avoiding mechanical interferences between adjacent elements. The resulting performances of such an array, called “Vertigo”, show a grating lobe reduction in the order of 20 dB, compared to an array with a periodic triangular lattice.

articleTitle: Analysis of structural effects on conformal antenna performance
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The effects of the presence of carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) bulkheads near a broadband conformal spiral antenna are studied. It is found that certain arrangements of the bulkheads are more conducive to antenna gain and polarization bandwidths. The feasibility of manufacturing the antenna using additive manufacturing technique e.g. conductive silver ink cured at around 121°C temperature is also demonstrated.

articleTitle: Aperture controlled substrate integrated h-plane horn antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The H-plane integrated horn antenna equipped with hard internal E-walls, and soft external H-walls is introduced. The lateral hard walls of the horn resolve the tapered nature of the horn aperture and provide the antenna with uniform aperture distribution at the hard frequency band. The external soft surfaces around the aperture suppress the aperture scattered waves in order to reduce the antenna back radiation.

articleTitle: Toward a terahertz quasi-optical vector network analyzer
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose the design of a quasi-optical directional coupler toward the implementation of the first quasi-optical terahertz (THz) vector network analyzer (VNA). With the proper use of lenses and splitters, we design a quasi-optical topology that isolates the reference from the measured signal. This configuration could pave the way for the first true THz VNA by implementing standard photonic-based THz sources and detectors. The quasi-optical topology is simulated at 300-400 GHz and the numerical results show a first proof of concept of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Experimental validation of multi-layer coil inductance estimation method
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An inductance estimating method, which has recently been suggested, was experimentally validated on circular multi-layer coils in this paper. The coil structure is treated as spiral coils connected in series. The parameters required for the estimation were obtained from a series of simulations involving a pair of spiral coils. The estimation was validated through a series of measurements. The result was shown to be very accurate.

articleTitle: Radar cross section reduction of dipole antenna using checkerboard surface
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The radar cross section (RCS) reduction technique for dipole antenna using checkerboard surface is investigated. The checkerboard surface is used as ground of dipole antenna instead of a metal ground. In the operating frequency band of the antenna, the checkerboard surface can reflect electromagnetic wave nearly in phase, thus the radiation performance of the antenna is not degraded. However, for the out of band case, the scattered fields by two types of subarrays of the checkerboard surface are out of phase, which lead to reduced RCS of the antenna when compared with that loaded with metal ground. Results show that broadband RCS reduction can be achieved with few influence on the radiation properties in terms of both S-parameter and radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Study of antenna systems located on complex platforms by using characteristic mode analysis and related techniques
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The paper investigates the problems of excitation of Characteristic modes on a complex platform and the realization of desired radiation patterns using the Characteristic mode analysis (CMA) and related techniques. The excitation issue is examined theoretically and an analytical approach to deriving the excitation fields needed to obtain a specified CM is presented. The problem of placing user-specified antennas on a complex platform to realize a desired pattern is also discussed.

articleTitle: All-metallic dual-beam antenna with a low profile
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a compact all-metallic dual-beam patch antenna is presented. The two short edges of the patch are connected to the ground via two shorting walls, and the two long edges are connected to the ground via two columns of shorting strips. Owing to the asymmetric arrangement of shorting strips, dual beam operation can be achieved. The profile of the proposed antenna is only 0.06λ. The simulated results show that the -10 dB impedance bandwidth is 5.5% (5.88 ~ 6.21 GHz). The two beams are directed at ±45°. The peak gain is about 9 dBi, and the cross polarization is very small.

articleTitle: Numerical dispersion and stability proof of the WLP-FDTD method
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, the numerical dispersion of the three-dimensional (3-D) finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method with weighted Laguerre polynomials (WLP) is presented. The phase velocity of numerical wave modes is relevant to the direction of wave propagation, grid discretization and time-scale factor. Additionally, the unconditionally stability for marching-on-in-order WLP-FDTD scheme, with the growth factor no larger than 1, is proved from Fourier analysis of a monochromatic wave.

articleTitle: Characterizing antennas in the time and frequency domains
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Our antenna definitions standard currently has no terms that describe antenna performance in the time domain, possibly due to the complexity of the equations. However, if we express the antenna equations using quantities related to the square root of power, we obtain simple expressions valid in both the frequency and time domains. This leads to a number of new terms that should be considered for inclusion in the next revision of the standard. Doing so would provide a common language for discussing antenna performance in the time domain. It also would also add phase information to common frequency domain terms, such as antenna gain and radar cross section.

articleTitle: Novel 3D-printing enabled antenna design for future wireless intra-chip interconnect
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel antenna design that is enabled by 3D printing technology for future wireless intra-chip communications is proposed in this work. Vertical quarter-wavelength monopoles are used for intra-chip communication, which avoids substrate-caused low antenna radiation efficiency. The monopoles are surrounded by specially-designed dielectric distribution. This additional design degree of freedom allowed by 3D printing technology is used to tailor antenna radiation pattern that enhances the desired link and reduces the undesired crosstalk spatially. A 60 GHz prototype is designed, fabricated and measured. The measurement results agree well with the simulation results. The demonstrated path loss of the desired link at a distance of 17 mm is only 12 dB, which is more than 10 dB better than the theoretical value for 60 GHz monopoles based on Friis transmission equation and previously reported work.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable frequency selective surface for fabry-perot cavity antenna system
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents reconfigurable Fabry-Perot Cavity (FPC) antenna systems to switch one mode to other with respect to near- and far-field performance. The fluidic channel is created and integrated into the FPC system. The channel is filled with air or deionized (DI) water. The fluidic FPC systems are compared to a fixed FPC design without the fluidic housing. Simulation and measurement results are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: On the shadowing distribution for ultra wideband in-body communication path loss modeling
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Current path loss models for ultra wideband in-body communication are usually based on finite-difference time-domain simulations. Due to the computational complexity they include only a limited number of transmitter-receiver pairs. We propose a new channel modeling approach based on a plane wave propagating through a multi-layered dielectric. With this approach it is possible to calculate the path loss of many more transmitter-receiver pairs. Hence, the statistical distribution of the path loss can be evaluated better. Our results show that the standard deviation of the path loss increases in fact drastically with distance between transmitter and receiver. For distances of more than 100mm it gets much larger than the standard deviation proposed in literature. That means the variation in path loss might in reality be much higher than current models indicate.

articleTitle: Control of scattering patterns of a phased array with swtiches loaded annular slot elements
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We demonstrate that the scattering patterns of a phased array can be controlled with switches loaded annular slot elements. When these switches are off, the elements can radiate efficiently as annular slot antennas. On the other hand, when these switches are on, the incident wave can be reflected by these elements to a desired angle, determined by the locations of the switches.

articleTitle: 2-D cross slotted W-band waveguides array
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper discusses the design of an 8×16 cross slotted rectangular waveguide array. The array produces a gain of 25 dB at 86 GHz. Great isolation is achieved between the Left Hand Circularly Polarized (LHCP) and Right Hand Circularly Polarized (RHCP) patterns over the entire Half Power Beamwidth (HPBW). Feeding the array at different ports enables both LHCP and RHCP radiation patterns. The array can be proposed for space communication in addition to its ability to be deployed into terrestrial communication systems.

articleTitle: Advanced techniques for GPR microwave imaging: An experimental study
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work deals with the retrieval of the dielectric characteristics of unknown objects buried in a lossy soil. The reconstruction performances of two deterministic inverse scattering (IS) techniques are assessed on real ground penetrating radar (GPR) data collected in an archaeological site in Cavallino (LE, Italy). Both approaches exploit a multi-resolution (MR) strategy to keep low the ratio between problem unknowns and non-redundant data. Moreover, they are respectively based on a multi-frequency (MF) and frequency-hopping (FH) approach for enabling the processing of wideband measurements. An illustrative experimental result is shown to verify the effectiveness and the potentialities of the two GPR-IS methodologies for archaeological investigations.

articleTitle: Reactively loaded arrays based on overlapping sub-arrays with flat-top radiation pattern
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design of reactively-loaded antenna arrays featuring a pulse-shaped radiation pattern for limited scan-angle applications is presented. The use of the reactive loading allows reducing the complexity of the feeding structure, eliminating the need for complex overlapping beam-forming networks and permitting a drastic reduction in the number of control points.

articleTitle: Parasitic antennas for small metallic platforms
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the feasibility of utilizing metallic body of an airplane as a radiator is investigated. Characteristic mode analysis is applied to an airplane model to find the natural resonant surface current distributions on the platform. For a UAV model considered here, its first dominant mode is studied and parasitic elements that can excite such mode are designed. This mode is excited using well-positioned array of four small half-loops on the wings of the UAV. It is shown that the parasitic elements can effectively excite the platform to radiate VHF radiation at around 70 MHz. Simulation results show that array of the parasitic loops and the body of the UAV produce an antenna with 2.45 dBi gain enhancement compared to the case of small loops array in the absence of the UAV platform.

articleTitle: The effect of antenna mutual coupling in a mimo radar system
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper develops a mathematical model, complete with antenna mutual coupling and radio frequency circuit blocks, for a multiple-input multiple-output radar system. Simulations using the model demonstrate that mutual coupling causes the observed angle of a target to shift from its actual angle and increases the side lobe level of the MIMO radar virtual array response.

articleTitle: Wideband amplitude-only direction finding subsystem with conical spirals
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper we present a direction finding antenna subsystem utilizing two modified conical spirals. Antennas are squinted symmetrically along the systems axis, enabling an amplitude only direction finding function. The design is meant to achieve better front to back ratio than preexisting systems, and thereby higher efficiency and longer detection range. Presented here is a system exhibiting a 23:1 bandwidth available for a range of possible direction finding functions and fields of view.

articleTitle: Continuous beam steering antenna with large 2D coverage for 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A gap waveguide continuous beam steering antenna is proposed in the 60-GHz band for 5G applications. The antenna is composed of two parts: i) a quasi-TEM feeding network, ii) a slotted radiating plate. The relative mechanical rotation between the two parts generates a phase gradient across the radiating part and the beam radiated in the upper hemisphere can be scanned continuously. The antenna is developed in hollow waveguide with a contactless technology to ease the mechanical movement between the antenna parts. The proposed antenna has been validated numerically and experimentally in the 60-GHz band. Very good agreement has been obtained between simulations and measurements. The antenna field of view reaches ±60°. and its bandwidth equals 13% for VSWR<;2. The losses within the structure are 0.5dB. Finally a large 2D beam coverage can be obtained by combining frequency scanning and mechanical rotation of the two antenna parts; these results are also confirmed experimentally.

articleTitle: Path loss frequency dependence at 2–26 GHz in an urban macro cell environment
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents path loss frequency dependence in an urban macro (UMa) cell environment on the basis of measurement campaign results using three frequencies between 2 and 26 GHz. For a 3rd Generation Partnership Project UMa model above 6 GHz band, the dependence is shown by 20log(f). The measurement results show that the dependence is similar in Line-of-Sight areas but that in Non-Line-of-Sight areas it increases as distance increases. They also show that the dependence appears to be caused by the dominant diffraction path in long distance areas, which has large frequency dependence.

articleTitle: Research on the electromagnetic wave scattering characteristics of time and space inhomogeneous plasma sheath
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A hypersonic vehicle is covered by an inhomogeneous and time-varying plasma sheath when it reenters the Earth's atmosphere. To investigate the effects of scattering in the plasma sheath on electromagnetic (EM) wave, the JE convolution-finite-difference time-domain algorithm is applied to three-dimensional time and spatially inhomogeneous plasma. The radar cross-section (RCS) of plasma sheath is analyzed. The RCS of different pressures, temperatures, incident angles, and cyclotron frequency are calculated. Results show that these parameters in plasma sheath have noticeable effects on EM wave.

articleTitle: Low-RCS frequency reconfigurable antenna with polarization conversion metasurface and phase tunable reflector
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a high-gain low radar cross section (RCS) frequency reconfigurable antenna based on metasurfaces is presented. The top-layer metastructure is constructed by polarization conversion metasurface (PCM) and partially reflecting surface (PRS), which is placed above the antenna at the height of fh. Phase tunable reflectors surround around the antenna source, forming the bottom-layer one. When an out-of band incident wave is illuminated on the PCM surface, transmission wave is redirected into noncritical directions with respective to symmetrical arrangement of PCM-PRS unit and its mirror unit. The Fabry-Perot (F-P) resonator cavity formed by PRS and the phase tunable reflectors contributes to the in-band radar cross section reduction (RCSR). Simulated results show that the operation frequency can be dynamically tuned from 8.7GHz to 10.1GHz and the gain enhancement is about 6.5 dB. Remarkable wideband RCSR is obtained ranging from 8.3~20 GHz and the RCS curves can be tuned with the variation of antenna frequency in both polarizations.

articleTitle: Characteristic modes for U-slot's feed placement
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Recently, DIResF is reported for the first time in [1] to design a U-Slot without feed location optimization. In this paper, theory of characteristic mode (TCM) is used to analyze the effect of vertical probe feed location variation on impedance matching of antenna. It has been shown that feed location at center (xp=0, yp=0) gives the best impedance matching in DIResF. However, Its variation in the direction of vertical currents (i.e. x-axis) decreases the eigen value of participating current mode due to its capacitive effect. While, variation in horiznotal direction(i.e. y-axis) increases the eigen value due to its inductive effect.

articleTitle: Comparison of radiation pattern modeling methods for GPS controlled reception pattern array
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A four element dual-linear polarized pin-fed patch antenna array is modeled as a controlled reception pattern array for anti-jam GPS applications. Full-wave electromagnetic simulation is used to refine the model and account for parasitic effects such as mutual coupling. The effects of using full-wave simulated antenna radiation patterns rather than analytically calculated patterns for calculation of weight vectors to implement null steering are explored.

articleTitle: A power dependent frequency selective surface
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a power dependent nonlinear square loop FSS which provides transmission at low power and reflection at high power is proposed. The nonlinear property of this structure is realized by utilizing the nonlinear property of diodes as the diode can have `on' and `off' state at high and low power level, respectively. To have a accurate estimation of the property of diodes and study the performance of the FSS, co-simulation of full wave simulation and circuit simulation is carried out. Spice circuit model of the diode is used which is very accurate model of the diodes. A threshold power of 0 dBm/unit is achieved for the power dependent FSS.

articleTitle: A novel SMA fed substrate integrated E-plane horn antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel SMA fed substrate integrated E-plane horn antenna is proposed in this paper. The antenna is built by binding two printed circuit boards. Copper strips are inserted at the interface between two circuit boards to support longitudinal current that is excited by an SMA adapter. Copper plated through holes are drilled along the propagating direction to support vertical current. A trapezoidal dielectric load using the same substrate material is used to improve gain and impedance matching.

articleTitle: Synthesis of a multi-beam dual reflectarray antenna using genetic algorithms
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the results of an initial study on the use of genetic algorithms to synthesize multi-beam patterns for dual-reflectarray antennas operating with a single feed per beam architecture. Under the simple two-dimensional center-fed case considered, the method shows promise when compared to a traditional bifocal synthesis method with regard to spillover efficiency.

articleTitle: 4–40 GHz conical spiral antenna recessed in a cavity
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper considers conical spiral antennas recessed in cavities for 4 to 40 GHz broadside wide beam applications. It is shown that a conical configuration has positive gain within 120 degrees field of view in free space, which is wider compared to a planar spiral. As expected, the cavity greatly affects the antenna radiation, such that field of view is reduced to 100 degrees and broadside gain shows significant variation. Relation between the gain variation and cavity/aperture resonances is discussed. In spite of using absorber for suppressing cavity modes, radiation efficiency is higher than 65%, and it is better than 80% at frequencies above 10 GHz.

articleTitle: A compact SIW butler matrix with straight delay lines at 60 GHz
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new structure of 60-GHz substrate integrated waveguide Butler matrix based on silicon dioxide is proposed. Straight delay lines are employed to realize the required 45° and 0° phase shifters in the Butler matrix, which makes the Butler matrix more compact in width. The simulations show that the insertion losses are below -2.7 dB and the reflections and isolations are lower than -15 dB from 58 GHz to 62 GHz. The overall size of the designed Butler matrix is 23.7 mm×8.8 mm.

articleTitle: 24–71 GHz PCB array for 5G/ISM
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Millimeter-wave 5G mobile architectures need to consolidate disparate frequency bands into a single, multifunctional array. Existing arrays are either narrow-band, prohibitively expensive or cannot be scaled to these frequencies. In this paper, we present the first ultra-wideband millimeter-wave array to operate across six 5G and ISM bands spanning 24-71 GHz. Importantly, the array is realized using low-cost PCB. The paper presents the design and optimized layout, and discusses fabrication and measurements.

articleTitle: 2.5D quasi-axisymmetric finite difference frequency domain modeling
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new 2.5D quasi-axisymmetric Finite Difference Frequency Domain (FDFD) algorithm for sources with arbitrary locations and polarizations greatly extends strict 2D axisymmetric modeling which requires on-axis or azimuthally-symmetric source distributions. Field expansions in sinusoidal modes are required, so multiple discretized Helmholtz operators A(m) must be constructed and inverted for each mode index m. Although convergence of the background and total fields can be relatively slow, particularly in the vicinity of the ring sources used in the expansion, convergence of scattered fields is reasonably fast. Excellent agreement with both analytic solutions and existing 2D axisymmetric FDFD simulations is demonstrated.

articleTitle: A study of directional antenna for recycled energy improvement in electromagnetic wave energy harvesting
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A recycled energy method using a dual directional antenna is proposed about the electromagnetic wave energy harvesting to convert electric power from electromagnetic waves in this paper. It is possible to convert much electric power by applying the dual directional antenna using the 180-degree hybrid circuit to the electromagnetic wave harvesting. In this research the recycled energy is considered by the indoor environment using the ray tracing method and it is reported that the recycled electric power by the dual directional antenna improved more than the single directivity antenna.

articleTitle: Circuit model for single-layer single-resonant ultra-thin FSS absorbers with wide bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Electromagnetic absorbers based on frequency-selective surfaces have been explored for many applications. It is often useful to represent these devices using a circuit equivalence, which provides a physical insight into underlying performance capabilities and limitations. Yet, absorbers tend to deviate from their ideal circuit representations for ultra-thin implementations where coupling between layers becomes significant. To date, there has been little investigation into the corrective measures required to compensate for parasitic coupling associated with ultra-thin absorbers. In the paper, a circuit model is proposed for a broadband absorber comprised of a single-resonance FSS cascaded with a PEC-backed substrate. The thin nature of the absorber is shown to introduce undesirable coupling between the FSS and PEC layers, resulting in non-ideal performance. Two corrective measures are outlined with the goal of retuning the absorber for maximum bandwidth.

articleTitle: Miniaturized SIW filter antenna with loadable sensor for various microwave sensing applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) based filter antenna has been proposed for wireless sensor network applications. The proposed antenna consists of a fractal slot loaded miniaturized high-Q evanescent mode SIW bandpass filter section which provides a narrow pass band before the cut-off frequency of the unloaded SIW. A square patch monopole with partial ground plane, acting the radiating element, is cascaded to the filter. The sensor element can be integrated to the antenna on the slot area according to choice of applications. Depending on any measurable physical parameter, the dielectric constant of the sensor element changes and it affects the resonant frequency of the loaded filter antenna which can tune over a wide range. The antenna provides narrow band, high tuning range and easy integration to active circuits.

articleTitle: A wideband, high-gain, CPW-fed, circularly-polarized, l-shaped slot antenna array
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A single-fed, wideband, circularly-polarized (CP), 2 × 2 antenna array is presented. The array feed design is based on the sequential rotation feeding technique. A compact, wideband, CP coplanar waveguide (CPW) slot antenna is proposed as each of the array elements. It is shown that the proposed antenna performance is significantly enhanced when it is placed in the array arrangement. The impedance bandwidth of the array is 66.7% (from 1.5 GHz to 3 GHz) and its axial ratio (AR) bandwidth is 53.2% (from 1.7 GHz to 2.95 GHz) for AR <; 3 dB. The antenna array has a stable radiation pattern and a gain of greater than 6 dBi over the entire CP frequency band. The overall size of the antenna array is 170 mm × 170 mm.

articleTitle: Channel simulation of adaptive beamforming at 60GHz millimeter-wave band under high-speed railway scenario
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Millimeter-wave(mmWave) Beamforming(BF) for high speed trains(HSTs) scenario has been investigated in this paper. Throughout the paper, We have designed a patch antenna array and BF Scenario for HSTs, the analysis of path loss, received power and Rician k-factor are obtained with ray tracing simulator at 60GHz band. In summary, we have gained valuable results in adaptive BF based HSTs communication.

articleTitle: Design of a frequency reconfigurable, terahertz folded antenna for photomixers
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design of a frequency reconfigurable folded dipole antenna for terahertz photomixers. The proposed folded antenna can operate at two different frequencies, namely 330 GHz and 590 GHz, increasing the radiation efficiency at both frequencies. The reconfiguration of the antenna is achieved by means of Nano-Electro-Mechanical Systems (NEMS) switches. The proposed antenna has a radiation resistance of 465 Ω and 216 Ω, providing an improvement by a factor 2.2 and 2 at 330 and 590 GHz, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of NEMS reconfigurable folded antenna for terahertz photomixers.

articleTitle: Indoor localization with UWB and 2.4 GHz bands
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose an approach based on time of arrival (TOA) using both ultra-wideband and IEEE 802.15.4 at 2.4 GHz technologies to achieve an enhanced localization accuracy. To this end, experimental TOA measurements have been performed for both technologies in an indoor university campus area with LOS and NLOS propagation conditions. The experimental results pointed out different estimation of localization regarding the used technologies and propagation conditions. This difference is used to identify how to use both technologies in order to increase the accuracy of localization.

articleTitle: Wideband axial-mode helical antenna with 3D printed proliferated radome
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a special axial-mode quasi-tapered helical antenna with 1.9:1 bandwidth is presented. The diameter profile of this design consists of a conical bottom section for achieving wider bandwidth at lower frequency end and uniform top section for achieving higher gain at the higher frequency end. To support and protect the antenna element, a proliferated radome made of polylactic acid (PLA) material was manufactured using 3D printing. This paper discusses about the design concept, tradeoff, as well as simulated and measured performance comparison of a fabricated prototype.

articleTitle: Bandwidth and F-B ratio enhancements of an electrically-small crossed-dipole antenna using an NFRP reflector
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a compact single-feed crossed-dipole antenna backed by a near-field resonant parasitic (NFRP) element is proposed to enhance the bandwidth and front-to-back (F-B) ratio of the electrically small antenna system. The NFRP element is designed to not only act as a reflector, but also to generate an extra resonance with circularly polarized (CP) radiation for the antenna system. The extra resonances are utilized to broaden the antenna bandwidth. The final design with an overall size of 35 mm × 35 mm × 13.7 mm (0.184λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> × 0.184λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> × 0.072λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> at 1.575 GHz) has a |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| <; -10 dB bandwidth of 20.3% (1.485-1.820 GHz), a 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 9.46% (1.510-1.660 GHz), and a maximum F-B ratio of 9.8 dB. Relative to the crossed-dipole antenna without a reflector, the proposed design increases the F-B ratio from 0 to 9.8 dB and achieves approximately 150% and 400% increases in |S|<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| <; -10 dB and 3-dB AR bandwidths, respectively.

articleTitle: Deterministic synthesis of conformal linear aperiodic antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A deterministic approach to the synthesis of general aperiodic circular arc antenna arrays is presented. The proposed technique is aimed at the analytical determination of the optimal array element density and excitation tapering useful to mimic a desired radiation pattern. In particular, the developed antenna placement method does not require any optimization procedure, resulting in a dramatic reduction of array design times.

articleTitle: On hertz and the speed of light
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Experiments carried out in 1888 by Heinrich Hertz are generally considered to have validated Maxwell's theory. In this paper we present measurements made with replicas of the antennas used by Hertz when he attempted to measure the wavelength of the fields radiated by his spark-excited dipole. Hertz determined the dominant frequency f of these waves from the static capacitance and inductance. Here we show that the experiment Hertz designed to determine the wavelength X would have succeeded in establishing that these waves travel at the speed of light, as Maxwell predicted, had he properly understood the distribution of the transient standing wave involved with reflection. If, for example, he had used the first minimum in his measured distribution of the H-field as a quarter-wavelength and had he corrected an error made in computing the capacitance, he would have concluded that the wave velocity was fλ ≈ 3.4 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> m/s, close enough to the speed of light to be persuasive. As it was at the time, however, he could only feel sure that the wave velocity was finite.

articleTitle: A compact and broadband CPW-fed folded-slot antenna for c-band application
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a compact and broadband CPW-fed antenna with FR4 substrate. The Y-shaped monopole radiation element and the unequal arms were used to broaden the antenna bandwidth and compress the antenna structure. The simulated and measured results are presented, showing that a satisfactory performance is achieved. The effects of different unequal arms on the antenna performances are discussed as well.

articleTitle: A wide-band dual-polarized reconfigurable slot-ring antenna/array with a compact CPW feeding structure
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A wide-band dual-polarized reconfigurable slot-ring antenna/array using a compact CPW feeding structure is presented. By using a CPW feeding mechanism, the mutual coupling between the two orthogonal feeding lines is reduced significantly compared to the traditional microstrip feeding method while maintaining the antenna bandwidth. Furthermore, the CPW feeding network is more compact than the microstrip feeding network which is an important factor in large antenna arrays.

articleTitle: Computations of scattering by shaped dielectric lenses and a comparison with measurements
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Scattered field computations of shaped dielectric lenses irradiated by an array, are presented using two techniques reported recently by the authors, (a) A Spheroidal modal expansion that can be expressed in terms of a linear combination of orthogonal spherical modes and (b) A hybrid of geometrical optics and spherical modal analysis to predict the EM fields over a near field spherical surface surrounding the lens. For a verification of the methods, comparisons have been made for lens-array combination with results obtained from an EM flow solver. Here we present a third method by sectioning the shaped lens and computing the fields on a measurement surface, by adding the fields contributed by the approximated spherical sections. Significantly, also presented is a set of computations using these techniques for spheroidal lenses irradiated by 1×2 and 2×2 arrays in C-band, and validated with measured results obtained in an anechoic chamber. There is a far better agreement for the computational methods with measured results, as compared to EM flow solvers. Further these methods need only a fraction of its time for computations and are as independent of lens shape.

articleTitle: Ray-based reconstruction algorithm for multi-monostatic radar in imaging systems
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A ray-based reconstruction algorithm for multi-monostatic millimeter-wave radar systems uses time-of-flight data from groups of adjacent transceivers to generate a point cloud representing the target being scanned. Since this reconstruction algorithm uses only the time-of-flight data for specular reflection points, it is less computationally demanding than conventional methods.

articleTitle: Investigation of wireless channel asymmetry in indoor environments
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Asymmetry is unquestionably an important characteristic of the wireless propagation channel, which needs to be accurately modeled for wireless and mobile communications, 5G networks, and associated applications such as indoor/outdoor localization. This paper reports on the potential causes of propagation asymmetry. Practical channel measurements at Khalifa University premises proved that wireless channels are asymmetric in realistic scenarios. Some important conclusions and recommendation are also summarized.

articleTitle: Advanced directional networking: LTE vs WiFi radios
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Advanced Nodes are the main components of Physical Layer based fully-directional networks. They consist of sets of appropriately programmed antenna arrays that enable them to conform to the standards of the radio being used. This paper provides an in-depth comparison of advanced nodes implementations for the two main choices of radios: 3GPP's Long Term Evolution (LTE) and IEEE 802.11 (WiFi). Component-by-component comparison is carried out, investigating several implementation aspects as well as estimated performance (in terms of standard performance metrics such as bit error rate, data rate, capacity, coverage radius) for the two radios. Based on the comparison, the associated implementation trade-offs are analyzed which help in choosing between the two radios.

articleTitle: A sparse forcing conformal array synthesis method
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose a sparse forcing synthesis approach for the design of conformal arrays. The method is based on alternate projections and l<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> minimization to achieve a sparse solution. The preliminary results shown are very promising.

articleTitle: A compact LTE multi-band loop antenna with additional 3400–3800 MHz coverage for mobile phone application
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper a multi-band loop antenna for 4G-LTE mobile phone application was proposed. The antenna has a compact volume of 60×6×5mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and covering 824-960, 1710-2530, 3400-3800 MHz with over 60% simulated efficiency.

articleTitle: A 6–18 GHz cavity-backed log-periodic-slot end-fire antenna for conformal application
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 6-18 GHz log-periodic slot-inspired cavity-backed end-fire antenna for conformal application is proposed in this paper. The log-periodic structure with 10 slot elements is applied to cover 6-18 GHz frequency band and the metallic cavity is placed under each slot element to keep wideband performance and prevent the effects of large metallic holder on the radiation pattern. A dielectric cover is used to improve the antenna performance and a broadband microstrip-CPW transition are inserted in the antenna as the feeding network. With these novel designs, the proposed antenna shows experimentally a good return loss and end-fire gain performances in the frequency range of 6-18 GHz. The proposed antenna also keeps low-profile and easy flush-mounted characteristics.

articleTitle: Phase agile BST-loaded dual resonance reflectarray design at Ka-Band
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a K<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sub>-band tunable dual resonance reflectarray element, its design methodology, limitations, and design tradeoffs are presented. Tunability is achieved by loading the antenna element with Barium Strontium Titanate (BST) thin film. The effects of limited frequency tuning, coupling conditions, and inherent loss is investigated using full-wave simulations. A unit cell design demonstrating an overall phase range of 360° and an average loss of 8.25 dB at 30.97 GHz is realized.

articleTitle: Design of rf/microwave planar crossovers using pure-series-connected lumped elements
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-compact planar crossover is presented and designed by using the pure-series-connected lumped elements. The basic structure of the crossover is inspired by the window-shaped 0-dB branch line coupler. Due to the perfect symmetry, the structure is analyzed by the even-odd mode theory and each lumped element can be determined analytically. Finally, the proposed crossover is fabricated. The measured results shows that 20 dB isolation and return loss can be achieved at the operating frequency, while the fractional bandwidth of 15-dB isolation/return loss is about 13.5%.

articleTitle: Impedance-ground modulated coplanar waveguide matching transformers with applications to miniaturized wilkinson power dividers
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose a novel design concept to continuously vary the widths of the signal trace and grounds of a conventional coplanar waveguide (CPW) to achieve a predefined matching characteristic of a transmission line transformer. Theoretical analysis is established, optimized and evaluated for a compact transformer. Then, a miniaturized 1 GHz CPW Wilkinson power divider (WPD) is designed and simulated to validate the design procedure. Simulations show input port matching below -30 dB, output ports matching/isolation below -15 dB, and transmission losses of -3.1 dB at the design frequency.

articleTitle: Dual frequency band RCS reduction using checkerboard designs
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Checkerboard surfaces, combining two different EBG structures, can realize a wide frequency bandwidth for a 10-dB RCS reduction because the scattered fields from checkerboard surfaces are re-directed toward four quadrants. This paper exhibits dual-frequency band checkerboard EBG surfaces with 10-dB RCS reduction bandwidths of 61% and 24% by utilizing two dual-band EBG structures, while the surfaces maintain scattering in four quadrants. Bistatic RCS of dual-band checkerboard surfaces are compared to the RCS of the corresponding PEC surface. Excellent agreement is obtained between measurements and simulations.

articleTitle: A compact monopole antenna for smartphones
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact monopole antenna with a volume of only 8×32×5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> for smartphones applications is presented. The antenna consists of two meander monopoles, having an S-shape and L-shape, on one side of the substrate and a tuning stub on the other side. Simulated and measured results show that the antenna has a dual-band of 824-960 MHz and 1700-3800 MHz which can cover the frequency bands for the GSM850, GSM900, DCS, PCS and UMTS systems and also Band 40, Band 41, Band 42 and Band 43 in the LTE system. The results in gain, efficiency and radiation pattern are also presented.

articleTitle: Experimental verification of a MoM-based efficient design approach to direction finding antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Communications Electronic Support Measure (CESM) systems operating in the VHF and UHF bands have been typically based on arrays designed accordingly to regular geometries. Uniform Circular Arrays (UCAs) are common and well-established examples but not applicable in all possible cases due to installation constraints. Irregular geometries may be exploited for such cases yet their design process is mainly a matter of “Trial and Error” attempts, aided by the designers' personal experience. In this contribution, a new design methodology supported by fast full wave simulations by Method of Moments (MoM) is described, aiming at reducing dramatically the time needed to find an effective solution to the installation problem.

articleTitle: Design of a v-band wideband circularly polarized microstrip patch array element for applications in body area networks
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A circularly-polarized, cavity-backed microstrip patch antenna, aperture-coupled fed through SIW, is presented. The antenna is designed for off-body communications in body area networks applications. The antenna provides an impedance bandwidth of 13%, with a gain of 7.2 dBc and cross-polarized levels of 18 dB at 60 GHz, and an axial ratio bandwidth of 7.6% using a single feed.

articleTitle: A modified square loop antenna radiating a circularly polarized conical beam: Its application to tilted beam formation with enhanced gain
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A square loop antenna is newly analyzed to radiate a conical beam, using the moment method. The loop has a single feed and two corners are truncated for circularly polarized (CP) radiation. It is revealed that the antenna shows a gain of 9 dB, which is higher than that of a conventional loop by 2 dB. This leads to further analysis of a modified square double-loop antenna that radiates a CP tilted beam. It is found that an enhanced gain can be obtained in comparison with that of a conventional double-loop antenna by 1 dB.

articleTitle: A dual band circularly polarized square patch for indoor positioning systems
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the development and characterization of a dual-band left hand circularly polarized square mi-crostrip antenna for WiFi applications (2.45GHz and 5.20 GHz) with a single feed point. The proposed design is achieved via a central slot and four symmetrical T-shaped slits on the patch sides. The antenna is then arranged in a cubic set-up for MIMO applications. Experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: High gain linearly polarized wideband UHF antenna based on substrate integrated coaxial line feeding network
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A high gain antenna array for the ultra high frequency (UHF) radio frequency identification (RFID) universal bandwidth (840-960 MHz) is herein proposed. A corporate feeding network is designed with substrate integrated coaxial line (SICL) technology in order to minimize losses due to dispersive mode propagation. Suspended E-shaped patches are employed to broaden the frequency band and improve antenna gain. A 2 ×2 antenna array prototype is manufactured and measured, revealing a sufficient S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> <; -10 dB bandwidth to cover the universal UHF RFID band, and a gain larger than 11 dBi within the bandwidth of interest.

articleTitle: A compact circularly polarized antenna for in-body wireless communications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A compact single-fed circularly polarized (CP) patch antenna, operating at Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) band of 2.42–2.48 GHz, is investigated for implantable telemetry applications. Slow-wave effect is introduced by embedding reactive triangle patches to the proposed antenna, thus obtaining a compact size of 9.6 × 9.6 × 1.27 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The slits are adopted and their sizes are adjusted asymmetrically, generating circular polarization. The simulated results show that bandwidths of the 10-dB return loss and 3-dB axial-ratio are around 12% (2.26– 2.55 GHz) and 3.2% (2.41–2.49 GHz) at ISM band, respectively. Besides, the simulated maximum gain reaches −25.3 dBi.

articleTitle: Investigation of stability issue in marching-on-in-degree scheme for TD-EFIE
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The marching-on-in-degree (MOD) method has been presented earlier to solve time-domain electric field integral equations to for transient electromagnetic scattering phenomena. Although the MOD scheme is assumed to be stable compared with marching-on-in-time one (MOT), there is few numerical or theoretical investigation on the recursive operations of MOD. When marching to very high degree of associated Laguerre polynomials, the MOD schemes may result in instability solutions. Therefore, the stability issue of MOD method is studied in this paper.

articleTitle: A gain-enhanced rectangular patch antenna with artificial magnetic conductor ground
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A kind of composite antenna with an artificial magnetic conductor ground is designed in this paper. This antenna consists of a 3×3 hexagonal annular gap artificial magnetic conductor unit cells and a rectangular patch antenna fed by coplanar waveguide.
