The in-phase reflection is suitable for the composite antenna. The distance between the patch antenna and the ground is 0.1λ at zero-phase reflection frequency for gain enhancement and low profile. The experimental results show that the relative operating bandwidth of the composite antenna is 23.3%, and the gain is more than 9dB.

articleTitle: A circular polarization selective surface employing Jerusalem cross-based polarizers
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a circular polarization selective surface formed through cascading a linear polarizer with a low reflection circular polarizer based on Jerusalem cross unit cells. The small cell size and low reflectivity of the circular polarizer allows the design process to be modularized whereby each component is synthesized separately, simplifying the design methodology and reducing the computational costs. The sub-wavelength CPSS cell is approximately 0.13λ×0.13λ, has a profile of ~0.7λ, and offers axial ratios of 1 dB and 3 dB over 4.4% and 11.1% fractional bandwidths at around 20 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Integration rules and time domain integral equation stability
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Because the mathematical analysis of time domain integral equations is fraught with difficulty, researchers are often forced to use experimental means to characterize the stability of their approaches. The difficulty inherent in this approach is that the variables affecting the success or failure of an experiment necessarily depend on a computer implementation of potentially hundreds of thousands of lines of instructions hiding unknown assumptions and even errors. In this work, the importance of different integration orders for near and far basis functions is investigated, and demonstrated to have an enormous effect on the stability of the implementation. Methods previously thought unstable for difficult problems are shown reliable with tiny changes over broad choices of parameter values.

articleTitle: Waveform-selective scattering control through circuit-based metasurfaces at the same frequency
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this study we introduce circuit-based metasurfaces that enable us to control scattering parameters at the same frequency. These metasurfaces are composed of conducting periodic units as well as several circuit elements including schottky diodes, which rectify the frequency component of an incoming wave to mostly zero frequency. The rectified signal is then controlled by time-domain responses of other circuit components such as capacitors and inductors even at the same frequency in response to waveform, namely, pulse width. The use of waveform-selective metasurfaces is expected to give us an additional degree of freedom to control electromagnetic properties, thereby leading to development of new kinds of electromagnetic applications and devices.

articleTitle: A novel method of direction of arrival estimation for large parabolic reflector antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel approach of direction of arrival (DOA) estimation for large parabolic reflector antenna based on focal-field distributions is proposed. First through simulation, we get the focal field distribution with different incident direction. And then the data received by the array feed is restored by interpolation algorithm. Finally the direction of incoming plane wave can be identified by matching the restoration data with simulation data. Numerical simulation results demonstrate satisfactory performance of the approaches.

articleTitle: Design of MAW spiral antennas for direction-of-arrival sensing using the cramér-rao bound
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work describes new design guidelines for modulated arm width (MAW) spiral antennas for optimal dual-polarized direction-of-arrival (DOA) sensing. These guidelines lead to an improved field of view over conventional designs. Using a four-arm MAW spiral with a modulation ratio of 1.6 and an expansion factor of 1.8, a four-degree field of view of ±29° in elevation and 360° in azimuth is obtained over a 3.6:1 bandwidth.

articleTitle: Skin tissue characterization of canine at microwave and millimeter-wave frequencies
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The development of an effective electromagnetic-based skin cancer detection system requires an accurate dermal layer characterization. As an initial step towards modelling human skin tissues and building a microwave system for human skin scanning, animal trials are usually performed starting with characterizing and modelling of animal skin tissues. This paper presents in-vitro permittivity measurements of excised canine head skin tissues in the frequency range of 1-13 GHz. Moreover, a comparison of modelled results for canine samples with human skin tissues across a wider band of 1-50 GHz indicates that Ridge Back Cross skin tissues provide a similar trend to the human skin characteristics and can serve as a possible alternative for testing the envisaged skin cancer detection system.

articleTitle: A single-fed circularly polarized using water substrate patch antenna with small size low-profile and broadband
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A single-feed circularly polarized (CP) patch antenna, characterized by small-size, low-profile and broadband, is proposed for UHF band applications (389MHz-610MHz). Its substrate, made up of water and rogers4003a, will greatly reduce the value of Q, so it can achieve wider bandwidth. The radiation structure consists of four planar spirals, a cross shaped microstrip line, and a T-shaped dipole The final prototype of the antenna, with an overall size of 200 mm× 200 mm× 1.732 mm (0.25 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> ×0.25 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> ×0.002 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> at 389 MHz) is simulated. The −10 dB bandwidth of the antenna is closed to 44%, and a 3 dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 19%, the gain of this antenna can achieve to −1.5dB.

articleTitle: A wideband switched beam antenna system for 5G femtocell applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work introduces a wideband switched beam system for femtocell 5G base stations. The system consists of a 4 × 1 Vivaldi linear array and a 4 × 4 Butler matrix able to operate from 1.9-5.1 GHz. A soft surface is introduced along the outer edges of the vivaldi elements of the array for side lobes and back radiation suppression.

articleTitle: Continuous updating of radio environment maps for millimeter-wave networks with beamforming
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Mobile stations in future mm-wave communications networks will likely employ beamforming arrays. These networks will require rapid determination and updating of narrow transmit and receive beams. Network-level optimization using cognitive radio techniques requires a protocol in which each station shares some combination of position, transmit beam, and received signal information. Selection of a representation of the transmit beam and the spatial structure of received signals entails a tradeoff between completeness and protocol data rate. In this paper we describe the components of suitable protocols, estimate the associated data rate, and demonstrate that this rate is reasonable even for lossless representations and when the number of beams is very large.

articleTitle: Wide band multi-beam cylindrical lens
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel ultra-wideband multi-beam cylindrical lens antenna for operation in the frequency range from 8 GHz to 18 GHz using parallel plate techniques is designed and fabricated. The cylindrical lens consists of four excitation ports, two parallel plates that are filled with teflon and a flare in order to produce four distinct fan-beams scanning in the azimuth plane with a minimum gain of 15 dB. CST Microwave Studio is used to analyze and optimize the antenna. The 3 dB E-plane and H-plane beamwidths are 10° and 30°, respectively, which can scan 40° in the azimuth plane with four distinct beams. The minimum gain of each beam is about 15 dBi at 8 GHz and 18 dBi at 18 GHz. There is a good agreement between the simulated and measured results.

articleTitle: Inverse scattering and compressive sensing as advanced e.m. design tools
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper we propose the adoption of the inverse scattering theory for the synthesis of profiles which are able to scatter an imposed scattered field. The design procedure moves from the Contrast Source Inversion (CSI) method. Moreover, by taking inspiration from the ℓ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>-norm penalized least square problem, a compressive sensing (CS) inspired inversion scheme is considered for the synthesis of sparse dielectric profiles.

articleTitle: Innovative array architectures for 5G communications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An innovative iterative scheme which combines parametric optimization techniques and convex programming strategies is proposed as a design tool to assess feasibility and limitations of next generation phased array architectures for 5G backhauling applications. The proposed design technique is aimed at (i) identifying the lattice geometry and minimum array aperture (complying with bandwidth, directivity, and steering range requirements) and (ii) computing the optimal excitation coefficients (to satisfy sidelobe constraints) for a 5G backhauling scenario. Preliminary numerical examples are shown to validate the proposed methodological approach and architectures in 5G backhauling scenarios and to deduce relevant applicative guidelines.

articleTitle: OAM 3D vector field visualization with CFDTD on CUDA GPUs
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper outlines an efficient technique for displaying 3D vector fields during conformal FDTD field updates on CUDA GPUs, while incurring only a small computational overhead and using a small configurable memory allocation. A 10GHz OAM phased array is presented as an example where 3D vector visualization shows the development of the OAM mode.

articleTitle: A novel THz radar imaging system using the radon transform
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this study a novel THz system is presented for 2D or 3D radar imaging. The system implements a Computerized Tomography's (CT's) algorithm that records the Radon Transform (RT) of an object and reconstructs the image using the Inverse Radon Transform (IRT). As such, the imaging system is comprised of a simple linear antenna that significantly simplifies the system topology and results in a compact and real-time imaging system. This configuration can be used for earth observation applications, standoff security monitoring and surveillance. In this work, the design of the novel THz imaging system is presented and simulation results of a phantom object at 300 GHz are verifying the proof of this concept.

articleTitle: A novel compact reconfigurable UWB antenna for cognitive radio applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel reconfigurable antenna covering a 10:1 bandwidth is designed and fabricated for cognitive radio applications. The proposed novel antenna covers 400 MHz to 4 GHz frequency range, while keeping its size suitable for potential MIMO applications. The wide frequency configuration is obtained by combining ultra-wideband (UWB) monopole configuration together with tunable matching network via two different signal paths from the feed point. The first path is directly connected to the UWB antenna, which covers 1-4 GHz operation frequency range. The second path, for frequency range between 400 MHz and 1 GHz, goes through a tunable matching network, which matches the UWB antenna. Two discrete switches are used to toggle between the lower and higher operating bands. Simulated and measured results are presented.

articleTitle: Potential integral equations in electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, a new integral equation (IE) based formulation is proposed using vector and scalar potentials for electromagnetic scattering. The new integral equations feature decoupled vector and scalar potentials that satisfy Lorentz gauge. The decoupling of the two potentials allows low-frequency stability. The formulation presented also results in Fredholm integral equations of second kind. The spectral properties of second kind integral operators leads to a well-conditioned system.

articleTitle: A novel dual-band beam-switching antenna based on active frequency selective surfaces
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel design of a dual-band beam-switching antenna based on active frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) is presented. The antenna is composed of two layers of active cylindrical FSS and fed by a dual-band dipole at the center. The FSS layers are divided into on and off state sectors in both inner and outer layers. Each sector consists of columns of metallic strips with on or off state diodes. To achieve a dual-band matching, the inner FSS layer is transmissive at lower band in both on and off state. Also, it is reflective in the on state and transmissive in the off state at higher frequency band. The outer layer is a reflective surface in on state and transmissive in off state in both frequency bands. In each state of operation, the on state sectors operate as a reconfigurable reflector at both frequency bands and convert the omnidirectional radiation pattern of the dual-band dipole to a directive one. By switching the states of diodes, the antenna can scan the entire azimuth plane. The fullwave simulation results show the antenna operates at 0.75 GHz-1 GHz and 1.7 GHz-1.9 GHz simultaneously, with maximum gain of 6.4 dBi and 10 dBi respectively, and can be used in the base stations of wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Dual-band wilkinson power divider using uniplanar metamaterial-based EBGs
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The integration of a metamaterial-based electromagnetic bandgap (MTM-EBG) structure into the branches of a Wilkinson power divider (WPD) allow the device to exhibit dual-band behaviour, for which each band possesses insertion loss within 0.3 dB of conventional devices. The successful application of MTM-EBGs into such a device suggests similar dual- or multi-band functionalities are possible through their integration into a wide range of microwave devices.

articleTitle: Monostatic RCS analysis for armed and unarmed UAV
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the analysis and numerical results of back scattering field of armed and unarmed Unmanned Air Vehicle (UAV) are presented. Simulations using Physical Optics (PO) method in Ansys HFSS software for monostatic Radar Cross Section (RCS) were made in 1 GHz, and 9 GHz. Since the electrical size of the target is twice as large as the wavelength, the order diffraction field is not considered. The fractured area from the first order will be sufficient to calculate the RCS of the target. Effects of ammunition quantity of modeled UAV with ammunition on RCS are compared in different frequencies.

articleTitle: A novel differential inverse scattering methodology in biomedical imaging
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An alternative differential framework for the existing integral-based electromagnetic inverse problems is proposed. This differential form, supplemented by the corresponding boundary conditions, overcomes the existing limitations of the integral-based inverse problems, i.e. considering the imaging antennas as point sources, the essential homogeneity along one axis, and the necessity of using a background matching medium. These limitations result in reconstructing two-dimensional images with certain level of error, and the practical problems associated with selecting suitable dielectric properties of the background medium. Thus, the ability of the proposed technique in reconstructing accurate three-dimensional images, including the dimensions and real structure of the imaging antennas and avoiding the essential use of matching medium, are unique advancements in solving inverse electromagnetic problems. To validate this proposed novel method, a biomedical inverse electromagnetic problem in head imaging is successfully solved.

articleTitle: A novel T-junction waveguide power divider with anti-phases and broad bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel integratable planar T-junction waveguide power divider with anti-phase outputs and full bandwidth of standard WR28 waveguide is proposed. It is basically a E-plane waveguide T-junction with its input port rotated around the axis of the two output ports by 90 degrees to form a planar structure. In order to verify the concept, a standard waveguide port THE junction divider is designed as an example. From the results, the reflection coefficient is lower than -20dB and phase difference between the two output ports is within 180 degrees in the full bandwidth from 26.3 to 39.4GHz.

articleTitle: A surface plasmon polariton inspired patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A patch antenna augmented with a magnetic surface plasmon polariton (SPP) spiral is proposed. It is fed by a small loop antenna. The final prototype of the optimized antenna has an overall size of 80 mm × 80 mm × 1 mm. Simulation results show that it has three working frequency bands; the -10 dB impedance bandwidth of each is: 1.99-2.52 GHz, 3.22-4.26 GHz and 4.71-5.16 GHz. These three working frequency bands all have field distributions characteristic of a scatterer with an excited, localized SPP mode. The peak gain achieved by this antenna is 6.5 dB.

articleTitle: Notable gain enhancement of curvilinear elements using a circular HIS ground plane
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Two curvilinear radiating elements (loop and spiral) are placed above a circular HIS ground plane. It is shown through simulations and measurements that in addition to the bandwidth enhancement compared to a rectangular HIS ground plane, the gain increases by an additional 3 dB when a circular HIS is used instead of the conventional HISs due to the radial phase profile.

articleTitle: Compact single/multi bands frequency reconfigurable antenna using PIN diode controlled meta-surface
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A frequency re-configurable single/multi bands antenna is proposed. It consists of a rectangular patch antenna and PIN diode controlled Meta-Surface, placed on the top of the patch. Square Split Ring Resonator (SRR), controlled with PIN diodes, acts as the unit cell of MS layers, which are periodically placed in both X and Y direction. The total size of the antenna is 80cm. Physical rotation of Metasurface, accompanied by PIN diodes' configurations, lead to achieve compact single/multi bands reconfigurable antenna. The design concepts, supported by electromagnetic full wave simulation, are presented. The results confirm that the designed antenna can be reconfigured to switch to several single bands and to several multi bands as well.

articleTitle: Multi-octave linear-to-circular polarizers
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Linear-to-circular polarizers operating at mm-wave frequencies with multiple octaves of bandwidth are reported. First, a polarizer constructed from cascaded anisotropic dielectrics is discussed. This polarizer scales the design of achromatic waveplates from optical frequencies down to mm-wave frequencies. In addition, the polarizer is constructed from artificial dielectrics (metamaterials) rather than naturally occurring crystals, which would be too bulky at these lower frequencies. Next, a broadband polarizer utilizing a meanderline/metamaterial combination is reported. The polarizer significantly extends the bandwidth over previous microwave designs by optimizing the orientation of each metallic layer, as well as combining meanderline and metallic patch geometries into the design. Both polarizers operate at incident angles up to 60° from normal.

articleTitle: A smart beam-switching multi-antenna system for UAV
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 2.4 GHz five element circularly polarized patch antenna is designed and built for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) application. The antenna switches its beam automatically to maximize the received signal power while suppressing the interferences. A received signal power with much less variation over single patch has been achieved using the switching algorithm.

articleTitle: Internal pattern-switchable 1.0 wavelength loop antenna array for satellite smartphone applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This article presents a novel internal pattern-switchable high-gain antenna array design for satellite mobile phone applications. By designing two sets of two-element 1.0 wavelength folded loop antenna array at top and side edge of a handset ground respectively, four different directional and steerable fan-shape radiating beams can be formed successfully to cover the 360 degree parallel with and surrounding the handset ground. Peak antenna gains and radiation efficiencies of the four radiating beams are better than 4.5 dBi and 60 % in the desired frequency band. The proposed design could be one of promising pattern-switchable antenna solutions for the future smartphone devices integrated with satellite-link functions. The constructed prototype has been studied in this paper.

articleTitle: Design of an electrically small antenna using a broadside-coupled split ring resonator
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An electrically small planar antenna using a broadside-coupled split ring resonator (BC-SRR) with a simple structure is presented. Due to the capacitance between the two SRRs in the BC-SRR, the resonant frequency of the antenna is lowered without increasing the size of the antenna. The proposed antenna resonates at 2.45 GHz and 7.31 GHz. At 2.45 GHz, the dimension of the SRR in the proposed antenna is as small as 0.012λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>× 0.082λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the wavelength in vacuum. The radiation efficiency is 24% at 2.45 GHz.

articleTitle: Limitations of phased arrays for 5G wireless communications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we discuss the limitations of phased arrays for 5G massive MIMO systems. The multibeam radiation patterns produced by a full phased array, a phased array with fixed sub-arrays, and a phased array with segmented phased sub-arrays are compared via illustrative examples. In fact, conventional phased array can only improve the link gain or the coverage, but couldn't enhance the capacity. Besides, the requirement of a huge amount of phase shifters makes the phased array not an ideal candidate for 5G massive MIMO base stations. Instead, the digital multibeam antennas would be more appropriate which are able to overcome these shortcomings.

articleTitle: A 3D printed dual GSM band near isotropic on-package antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we propose an on-package dual band monopole antenna with near-isotropic radiation pattern for GSM mobile applications. The proposed antenna is well matched for both GSM 900 and 1800 bands and provides decent gain for both the bands (1.67 and 3.27 dBi at 900 MHz and 1800 MHz respectively). The antenna is printed with silver ink on a 3D printed polymer based package. The package houses the GSM electronics and the battery. By optimizing the antenna arms width and length, a near-isotropic radiation pattern is achieved. Unlike the published isotropic antennas which are either single band or large in size, the proposed antenna covers both GSM bands with required bandwidth and is only half wavelength long. The design is low cost and highly suitable for various GSM applications such as localization, in additional to conventional communication applications.

articleTitle: A microwave tomographic technique to enhance real-imaginary permittivity image quality
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Typical microwave tomographic techniques reconstruct the real part of the permittivity with much greater accuracy as compared to the imaginary part. In this paper, we propose a method to mitigate the imbalance between the reconstructed complex permittivity components. To do so, the cross-sectional complex permittivity is expressed as summation of some known permittivities weighted by their corresponding fractions. We reconstruct the unknown complex permittivity of the imaging domain by computing the fractions of the known permittivities. A modified Gauss-Newton algorithm formulated for this particular scenario, is employed. Simulation results show that while direct reconstructions of the complex permittivity sometimes fail to obtain balance between relative permittivity and conductivity images, the proposed method leads to excellent reconstruction for both permittivity components.

articleTitle: Waveguide fed microstrip antenna array using i-shaped slots at ka-band
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, slotted waveguide fed microstrip antenna array has been designed at Ka-band. It comprises of the slotted waveguide having I-shaped slots to feed the microstrip antenna array. This type of feeding technique has an advantage that it reduces the losses from the microstrip feed network and improves the power handling capacity. Each linear microstrip antenna array has 13 elements and is placed on top I-shaped slot on the waveguide. It gives a bandwidth (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> ≤ 10dB) from 35.90-36.18 GHz and gain of 28dB. It gives side lobe level of 17dB. Such an antenna can be used in high power millimeter wave applications.

articleTitle: Vector channel-sounder using fiber delay lines to separate the channels
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper demonstrates a technique for vector channel sounding using a single-input, single-output channel-sounder. The vector channels are separated by inserting different radio-over-fibre (RoF) signal delays into the antenna ports and then combining the antenna signals as a set of separated-in-time responses. The RoF delays must be large relative to the channel delay spreads. In the VNA/channel-sounder, the delayed channels can be easily separated with basic signal processing, ready for statistical analysis.

articleTitle: Wideband VLF and LF systems
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A systems approach using several technologies achieves wideband VLF and LF transmission. The technologies include adaptive equalization, solid state amplifiers which return reactive power to the DC power supply, a new antenna matching network, and high efficiency envelope modulation.

articleTitle: Systematic design of single-layer multi-stop-band frequency selective surfaces
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a methodology for the systematic design of single-layer multi-band frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) by mapping the desired frequency response to a canonical structure consisting of easily tuned loaded-dipole elements. Drawing inspiration from circuit and filter theory, the elements can be individually tuned in order to optimize features such as stop-band bandwidth and pass-band shape. The method under discussion is used to create and optimize an FSS for Wi-Fi applications; it has the potential to be embedded in building materials to block transmission of signals at the 2.4-GHz and 5.2GHz bands. The design is tuned to exhibit high selectivity and a completely symmetric pass-band. Validations are performed in Ansys HFSS.

articleTitle: An efficient FSS absorber for WLAN security
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An efficient FSS absorber is presented for 5 GHz WLAN security. The proposed design consists of two layers of conductive and resistive FSSs, both etched on Rogers RO 3210 with a separation of 2.8 mm. It ensures better angular stability, reduced distance between the layers making it low profile and improved absorption in the desired band compared to the data presented in recent research. Simulation results are presented for both TE and TM polarizations at normal and oblique incidence.

articleTitle: The low-profile end-fire antenna with circular polarization at S band
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This letter presents a low-profile and wideband planar helical antenna to generate end-fire radiation beams. The antenna consists of a small reflective plate, a dielectric support plate and several metal patches. The helix is formed using printed strips with straight-edge connections implemented by metal poles. The profile of the antenna is very low at 0.16λ0 of the center frequency. A broad frequency bandwidth from 2.2GHz to 2.7GHz (25%) for VSWR less than 2 is achieved simultaneously. And the AR bandwidth is from 2.1GHz to 2.7GHz. The direction coefficient of the end-fire antenna in the whole band is above 10dB.

articleTitle: Hexagonal symmetry metasurfaces for broadband antenna applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work a three layer metasurface with hexagonal symmetry is presented. This surface supports a TE-like mode confined to the surface and presents very low dispersion. This means that the effective refractive index of the surface is almost constant over a broad range of frequencies. Furthermore, the surface exhibits high isotropy. These two characteristics make the surface appealing for the manufacture of broadband lens antennas. In this paper we present both simulation and experimental data that demonstrate these properties.

articleTitle: Optimal element arrangement of folded reflectarray for high aperture efficiency
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, new element arrangement method is proposed to obtain the high aperture efficiency in folded reflectarray. To optimize the performance of antenna, several characteristics are considered, such as polarization efficiency and phase error. As a result, aperture efficiency of proposed antenna is 51.1% at 77GHz. Detail design considerations are presented.

articleTitle: Broadband omnidirectional antenna for GSM900, GSM1800, 3G, 4G and Wi-Fi applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a broadband omnidirectional antenna, consisting of three tapered monopoles is presented. The antenna has |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>| <; -10dB from 880MHz to 2.52GHz. The gain of the antenna is greater than 2dBi over the entire bandwidth. The measured H-plane radiation pattern is omnidirectional with less than 8dB variation over the entire bandwidth. The antenna covers GSM900, GSM1800, 3G, 4G and Wi-Fi bands.

articleTitle: A novel broadband aperture-coupled microstrip patch array antenna for AiP solutions
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel broadband and high gain aperture-coupled microstrip patch array antenna is developed for AiP solutions. The compact size of the whole AiP is only 10×8.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The array antenna structure consists of parallel and series feed networks. A 16-element aperture microstrip coupled patch array antenna achieves over 15% of the operating bandwidth from 57 to 70 GHz which covers global unlicensed band at around 60 GHz. The proposed antenna peak gain can achieve 15 dBi at 65 GHz and can be utilized for two basic AiP solutions, including vertical and horizontal configurations.

articleTitle: Design and study of an aperture coupled patch antenna array with hyperbolic lens in c-band
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper we proposed an aperture coupled patch antenna array with hyperbolic dielectric lens at 6.45GHz. The structure of the aperture coupled provides narrow bandwidth and a hyperbolic lens is used to focus the beam from the patch antenna in the forward direction resulting in higher realized gain. Comparing with the traditional patch antenna array without a hyperbolic lens, this proposed antenna achieves 2.3 dB higher gain from simulation with CST software.

articleTitle: Printed single-feed circularly polarized UHF reader antenna for RFID applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper an optimally designed corner trimmed microstrip UHF reader antenna fabricated using screen printing of silver ink on an FR4 substrate is presented. The reader antenna, 12×12 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> in size, is fed through a single microstip line with an SMA connector attached to the antenna board. The measured results demonstrate reflection coefficient better than −15 dB as well as 3dB-beamwidth greater than 60° over the 900 MHz–930 MHz frequency bandwidth. The measured axial ratio lower than 3 dB within the range of 910 MHz–920 MHz shows the antenna polarization is circular in this frequency range. The designed antenna is light, low-cost and easy to manufacture and therefore can be conveniently used as reader antenna in RFID retail monitoring applications.

articleTitle: Computational polarimetric localization with a radiating metasurface
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel computational technique is presented in this article for enabling the estimation of both the localization of radiating sources and their polarization states. To this end, a radiating metasurface is conceived to multiplex the polarization information received by the its aperture into a single frequency domain signal, allowing for a massive simplification of the architectures conventionally implemented.

articleTitle: Polarization Reconfigurable Antennas Using a Liquid Metal Switching Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes the use of a pressure-actuated liquid metal switching mechanism to alter the polarization characteristics of printed circuit antennas. The mechanism is applied to a truncated corner patch antenna and an annular slot antenna to provide switching between linear and circular polarization.

articleTitle: Effect of ground plane size on a rectangular microstrip patch antenna based on te modes supported by perfect magnetic conducting surface
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The effects of varying the size of the ground plane of a rectangular microstrip antenna, which can excite TE modes, are investigated in this paper. The magnetic conducting patch and ground planes replace the electric conducting patch and ground plane. The antenna is designed following the conventional design steps by applying duality theorem to it in order to excite the TE modes. An L-probe feed excites the patch antenna. Antenna characteristics such as impedance bandwidth and radiation beamwidths are investigated by varying the ground plane size.

articleTitle: A compact CPW-fed wideband antenna design for 5G/WLAN wireless application
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a small, coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed wideband antenna for 5G/WLAN application. The proposed antenna consists of a pair of symmetrical meandering C-shaped strips, a rectangular ring strip and a monopole radiator. The designed antenna has a compact size of 20 × 27.5mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(0.16λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> × 0.22λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>). The simulated results show that the proposed antenna has 10-dB impedance bandwidths of 3530 MHz (2.37-5.9 GHz) to cover all the 2.4/5.2/5.8-GHz WLAN bands and the 5G candidate bands (3-6 GHz). The antenna provides regular omnidirectional radiation patterns, relatively stable gain in the working bands.

articleTitle: Microwave imaging of dielectric objects using a combination of simulated annealing and multi-directional search
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present a microwave imaging system based on the simulated annealing algorithm and the multi-directional search algorithm to reconstruct the electrical properties of dielectric regions. The simulated annealing method has been applied as a global optimization method for the inverse-scattering problem and the multi-directional search algorithm has been utilized to enhance the performance of the imaging system. Powerful performance of this technique in accurately reconstructing two-dimensional images of the dielectric regions is demonstrated by numerical results.

articleTitle: Dual Orbital Angular Momentum Mode Antenna by Combination of Transmitarray and Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual orbital angular momentum (OAM) mode antenna with l=0 and l=4 mode wave is presented. The proposed antenna employs a transmitarray and a reflectarray and uses a dual-polarization conical horn as the feed. By using two orthogonal linear polarization waves as excitations, the antenna can generate a pencil beam and an OAM beam, respectively.

articleTitle: Broadband circularly polarized microstrip antenna for airborne x band cp-sar
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel design of broadband circularly polarized microstrip antenna as an element of airborne X-band circularly polarized synthetic aperture radar (CP-SAR) sensor. The antenna is designed in low weight, low cost, low profile of configuration, and will transmit and receive left-handed circular polarization (LHCP) or right handed circular polarization (RHCP). The proposed antenna is an element of airborne CP-SAR that will be implemented into arrays that consist eight array submodule. For broaden the bandwidth, prototype constructed by double-layers substrate that has low dielectric constant and dissipation factor. Proximity-coupled feed stripline feeding adopted to avoid complexity in feeding network configuration. Basic characteristics of antenna parameters such as return loss, axial-ratio, and radiation pattern investigated and presented.

articleTitle: Monopole and conformal PIFA for small cylindrical groundplane mounting
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper characterizes antenna elements for mounting on a cylinder which is too small to be treated as a planar groundplane. A benchmark candidate is an outward-pointing quarter wavelength monopole, and we also present a lower-profile printed antenna. The best printed-type candidate is a new design - a wrapped PIFA. The bandwidths are surprisingly high: 12% for the monopole and 30% for the PIFA. These new designs are suitable for navigational and communications antennas on small frames such as found on unmanned aerial vehicles, drones, and bicycles.

articleTitle: Wearable-free wireless fall detection system
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Falls among the elderly population are a major concern for public safety since they are the dominant cause of injuries and hospitalization. Nearly a quarter of these falls can result in serious injuries that require immediate medical attention; hence, an external, privacy-preserving and device-free system is required for fall detection. Herein, we investigate the use of radars to monitor human motion and detect falls. This approach has been implemented with the use of a low-cost UWB radio operating between 3GHz-10GHz. The resulting radar data is shown to successfully enable fall detection for a person in a furnished room. This study demonstrates the enormous potential using indoor radars for motion detection, activity recognition, home-security, and fall alert systems.

articleTitle: Frequency tuning through physical reconfiguration of a corrugated origami frequency selective surface
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Frequency tuning is investigated for a dipole-based frequency selective surface on a corrugated structure through origami folding. Three types of 1D folding patterns that alter the in-plane and out-of-plane element spacing at different rates are used to examine the frequency response in relation to spatial rearrangement. Folding decreases the in-plane spacing and leads to smaller Floquet periodicity lengths and a higher stop-band frequency. In some fold arrangements, folding increases the out-of-plane spacing and results in phase-shift and two distinct coupling modes.

articleTitle: An explicit MOT scheme for solving the TD-EFVIE on nonlinear and dispersive scatterers
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: An explicit marching-on-in-time (MOT) scheme for solving the time domain electric field volume integral equation (TD-EFVIE) on nonlinear and dispersive scatterers is described. The unknown electric field intensity, electric flux density, and polarization densities representing Kerr nonlinearity along with Lorentz dispersion relation, all of which are induced inside the scatterer upon excitation, are expanded using half and full Schaubert-Wilton-Glisson functions in space. The TD-EFVIE and the constitutive relations between polarization, field, and flux terms are cast in the form of a first-order ordinary differential equation. The resulting matrix system is integrated in time using a predictor-corrector scheme to obtain the time dependent unknown expansion coefficients. The resulting MOT scheme is explicit and accounts for nonlinearity by simple function evaluations.

articleTitle: 30–2000 MHz multi-band body wearable antenna (MBWA)
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A Multi-band Body Wearable Antenna (MBWA) has been designed to cover six communications bands: SINCGARS band (30 MHz-88 MHz), Air & Marine band (116 MHz-174 MHz), UHF band (225 MHz-450 MHz), UHF-Public Safety band (450 MHz-512 MHz), UHF SATCOM band (225 MHz-318 MHz) and Soldier Radio Waveform (1-2 GHz). The MBWA can also be remoted from the radio and the soldier to enhance communications range in heavily forested or triple canopy jungle environments. A breadboard model has been developed and preliminary tests at WEO had fairly good results, reaching TRL-4.

articleTitle: Efficient optimization method for a reconfigurable OTA chamber
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A reconfigurable over-the-air chamber (ROTAC) allows the synthesis of arbitrary propagation environments inside a reverberation chamber for wireless device testing by controlling the reflection of waves along the chamber walls with reconfigurable elements. This work proposes an efficient two-step algorithm for realizing desired channels by first optimizing a linearized ROTAC model and then using gradient ascent optimization to refine the reconfigurable reflector states. Representative results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for power angular spectrum synthesis.

articleTitle: A frequency-scanning substrate-integrated-waveguide meanderline antenna for radar applications at 60 GHz
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes the design and characterization of a frequency-scanning meanderline antenna for operation at 60 GHz. The design incorporates SIW techniques and slot radiating elements. The amplitude profile across the antenna aperture has been weighted to reduce sidelobe levels, which makes the design attractive for radar applications. Measured performance agrees with simulations, and the achieved beam profile and sidelobe levels are better than previously documented frequency-scanning designs at V and W bands.

articleTitle: A high gain patch antenna using near zero-index metamaterial coating
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a high gain patch antenna using a near-zero-index metamaterial (NZIM) coating is presented for operating at 4.35 GHz. The proposed NZIM unit-cell is investigated and analyzed by both theoretical and numerical methods. It is shown that the designed NZIM unit-cell has a near refraction index characteristic at 4.25-4.45 GHz, which overlaps with the operating bands of the reference antenna. By covering a single layer NZIM coating with 4×4 cells over a conventional microstrip antenna, a gain enhancement of 2.8 dBi is achieved in comparison with the original antenna.

articleTitle: Dual-band chiral metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We propose a novel dual-band chiral metasurface that offers arbitrary polarization control of electromagnetic waves. By cascading an array of multiple concentric rectangular rings and precisely rotating each array, we physically encode certain surface impedances at two different frequency bands and realize a dual-band tensor impedance metasurface. Such a meta-surface can be configured to perform general chiral operations. We demonstrate the versatility of the proposed structure through a design example of a dual-band circular polarization selective surface.

articleTitle: L band circularly polarized synthetic aperture radar onboard microsatellite using parabolic mesh antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Our laboratory develops L Band circularly polarized synthetic aperture radar (SAR) sensor for microsatellite (150kg class) using 3.6m diameter of gold coated parabolic mesh antenna. This presentation explains the specification, antenna deployment system, RF system, and characteristics of parabolic mesh antenna for the developed sensor. This sensor will be employed to monitor global land deformation in the future.

articleTitle: A technique to enhance the impedance response of probe-fed stacked patch antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A simple procedure to enhance the impedance bandwidth of a probe-fed stacked patch antenna is presented. In this technique, the excitation via is extended to be in direct contact with both patch radiators. As a consequence not only is the manufacturing of blind vias avoided, but the impedance bandwidth is significantly increased. In this paper we apply the technique to several probe-fed stacked patch configurations and demonstrate that the -10 dB reflection coefficient bandwidth can be increased twofold. We also highlight that the bandwidth of the resulting antenna is now gain-bandwidth limited rather than impedance-bandwidth limited, since the excitation via causes scalping in the radiation patterns at higher frequencies.

articleTitle: HF noise trends in coastal southern california
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Electromagnetic noise measurements in the high frequency (HF) band from 2–30 MHz over a seven-day period off the waters of Southern California are analyzed in this paper. This analysis updates the external HF noise levels necessary to compute HF link budgets and design shipboard HF receive systems.

articleTitle: Implicit space mapping with substrate segmentation for reliable antenna optimization
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A reliable technique for EM-driven design optimization of antenna structures using implicit space mapping (ISM) with substrate segmentation is proposed. In our approach, the coarse model for space mapping is obtained by reducing discretization level of EM analysis as well as by partitioning the antenna substrate and assigning individual dielectric permittivity values that serve as preassigned parameters of ISM. Our approach is demonstrated through optimization of a 5.5 GHz bandwidth-enhanced patch antenna.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable impedance ground plane for broadband antenna systems
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: We introduce a reconfigurable impedance ground plane for broadband antenna array systems. The reconfigurable antenna elements need an adjustment of the local reflection phase to operate over a broadband frequency range. The proposed ground plane is constructed based on high impedance surfaces with RF MOSFETs populated in the gaps between the patches. The transistors play the role of RF switches to manipulate the surface topology by turning on/off the switches. In this paper, we numerically demonstrate the novel tunable ground plane and simulation results to show the extreme tuning range from 2 to 17 GHz by using ideal transistor switches, while maintaining the artificial magnetic conductor properties of the high impedance surface.

articleTitle: Passive battery-free UHF RFID tag for athermic car windshields
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a passive RFID tag operating in the UHF (Ultra-High Frequency) band is specifically designed for athermic car windshields in highway toll application. The calculations from the characterization in the anechoic chamber show that the realized tag offers a read distance greater than 12 meters for the entire Universal UHF RFID frequency band 860-960MHz.

articleTitle: A low profile circular patch loaded monopole antenna embedded in a manhole cover
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a low profile circular patch loaded monopole antenna suitable for embedded use in a manhole cover. It consists of a center-fed circular patch and two shorting strips connecting the patch to the ground. The simulated and field test results show that the antenna embedded in a manhole cover has a good gain and omnidirectional radiation pattern on the ground surface. The antenna can be used for a wireless monitoring and control system of underground facilities such as water supply pipes, sewer pipes, gas pipes, etc.

articleTitle: Efficient simulation of electromagnetic telemetry using thin wire kernel and layered media Green's function
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: To simulate the EM telemetry system in deviated and horizontal drilling, the underground formation is assumed to be horizontally layered media, and the long, metal drill string acts as an antenna that may be treated as a thin wire excited by a gap voltage source located near the drill bit. The numerical model employs the electric field integral equation (EFIE) and the method of moments (MoM) to obtain a linear system for the axial current distribution on the drill string, which is subdivided into one-dimensional segments. By using the thin wire kernel, near-field interactions can be evaluated accurately and efficiently, while also reducing problem dimensionality and singularity order of the homogeneous medium contribution to the layered media Green's function (LMGF). Numerical results are presented to verify the fast and accurate performance of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Ground de-embedded source reconstruction using a planar array of H-field probes
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents an introduction to a new source reconstruction method SRM which tries to deal with a special measurement scenario involving a finite ground plane. In this particular scenario, an array of H-field probes is placed slightly on top of a finite rectangular ground plane as such the normal SRM techniques are not the best choice when it gets to source reconstruction. Our primary goal in this work is to improve the accuracy of near-field to far-field transformation via the reconstruction method. We verify our method by comparing the far-field radiation pattern calculated by this application to that of the typical plane wave spectrum method (PWS).

articleTitle: Performance analysis of next-generation passive optical network (XG — PON)
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we have simulated and evaluated a XG-PON architecture performance based on ITU-T recommendations. It's a promising technology for Triple play as well as for the quadruple play application. The upstream and downstream links was analyzed along with the possibilities of reachability extension and last-mile flattening were evaluated.

articleTitle: Improved design of balanced antipodal Vivaldi for MMW applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel balanced antipodal Vivaldi antenna (BAVA) featured with substrate cut-out (CUT), additional substrates (ADS) and mixed slot edge (MSE) is designed to operate from 10GHz to 40GHz. Without increasing the total dimensions, beam squint in E-plane which is considered to be the major defect of conventional BAVA is effectively negated by the asymmetric structure. Besides, the antenna has better than -10dB S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> and much lower side lobe level (SLL) over the entire operating band-width benefiting from MSE. And gain of the antenna is respectively elevated by substrate cut-out up to 15 dB at higher frequencies and by MSE to 10 dB at lower frequencies.

articleTitle: Dual slant polarized cavity backed massive MIMO panel array antenna with digital beamforming
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A 4 × 4 sub-array of cavity backed dual slant polarized printed dipoles is designed and fabricated from 4.9 GHz-6 GHz for massive MIMO panel array antenna applications. The radiating elements provide measured impedance matching below -10 dB and envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) below 0.1. A larger panel of 8 × 8 is developed from the 4 × 4 sub-array and the digital beamforming capability showing multiple beams are verified using the Keysight SystemVue simulation tool.

articleTitle: Array antenna with uniformly excited elements to realize an equivalent arbitrary field distribution: A key technology for mass-production antenna engineering
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A large array antenna is composed of a large number of radiating elements so that the cost should be reduced by mass-production. We propose a novel technology for mass-production adding to previously proposed ones. Each element is driven with uniform excitation to cut complicated operation. Instead, the element separation is adjusted in the proposed algorism. The validity of the theory is confirmed by simulation.

articleTitle: Circularly-polarized, unidirectional antennas for simultaneous transmit and receive (STAR) applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The operational principles of circularly-polarized (CP) antenna elements for use in wideband simultaneous transmit and receive (STAR) antenna arrays are presented and discussed in this paper. Based on these operating principle, two designs of CP STAR array elements are presented. Both designs use the same cancellation technique to achieve STAR operation but they use different radiating elements. They provide isolation levels of 38 dB and 48 dB, respectively. In these STAR element designs, antenna bandwidth is primarily determined by the bandwidth of the CP element. Prototypes of each device are designed and discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic scattering from a pec target over a random rough sea surface using hybrid KA-PO-PTD method
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, radar echo width (REW) of a 2-D PEC target with tow edges situated over a random rough sea surface is analyzed by a combination of hybrid Kirchhoff approximation, physical optics and physical theory of diffraction (KA-PO-PTD) methods. The results are compared with those of conventional method of Moments (MOM). The effect of the target-surface configuration and wind speed on the REW of the composite geometry is studied.

articleTitle: Closed form expressions for the realistic modeling of weakly directive antenna patterns
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper a set of analytical expressions useful to model the pattern of printed antennas in a behavioral manner is proposed. Despite their simplicity, the proposed functions are computationally simple and well suited for fitting antenna measurement, hence useful to be implemented when a fast response is required, as in early stage of feasibility study.

articleTitle: Phaser-based polarization-dispersive antenna and application to encrypted communication
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper introduces the concept of polarization-dispersive (PD) antenna. The antenna consists of a patch radiator orthogonally fed by a network composed of a power divider with a phaser-loaded arm and a transmission-line-loaded arm. The PD characteristic is realized by designing the phaser such that the phase difference at the two excitation points varies, across a specified frequency range, from -90° to +90° through 0°, corresponding to a meridional excursion from left-handed circular polarization (LHCP) to right-handed circular polarization (RHCP) via linear polarization (LP) in the Poincaré sphere. A proof-of-concept PD antenna design is demonstrated and applied to encrypt a communication link. A more sophisticated system will be presented at the conference, where, using simultaneously full Poincaré-sphere mapping and dispersion coding, will lead to much more robust encryption for high-speed communication.

articleTitle: A planar 8-port MIMO antenna for 2.4-GHz WLAN applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A planar 8-port MIMO antenna consisting of only 4 slot elements is proposed in this paper. The antenna has a symmetrical structure and is designed to operate from 2.40-2.48 GHz. Each of the 4 slot elements is serving as a common radiator for 2 input ports. A T-shaped defected ground structure (DGS) is cut in the middle of the slot element to increase isolation between the two input ports to more than 10 dB and reduce the Envelop-Correlation Coefficient (ECC) to below 0.1. The proposed antenna is studied using computer simulation and fabricated for measurement using the Satimo Starlab system.

articleTitle: A wideband high-efficiency polarization reconfigurable antenna for wireless communication
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A single-feed polarization reconfigurable magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna is presented in this paper. With the manipulation of the diode states, the proposed ME dipole can provide three states of polarization control (one linear polarization and two orthogonal circular polarizations). To improve the effective bandwidth, antenna efficiency and front-to-back ratio, which are critical for wireless communication system, several techniques including a new excitation method, a low-loss reconfigurable perturbation and a box-shaped reflector are developed or selected after careful examining. The antenna is numerically analyzed and then measured. The fabricated prototype features an effective bandwidth of 7.9%, antenna efficiency of 80-90% and back radiation level below -20dB.

articleTitle: A compact two-dimensional multibeam antenna fed by two-layer SIW butler matrix
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a compact two-dimensional multi-beam antenna fed by two-layer SIW Butler matrix is designed at 30 GHz. This multibeam antenna can generate four beams in two planes. The simulation results demonstrate that the beam directions are (30°, 35°), (115°, 20°), (-75°, 25°), and (-135°, 40°), respectively. The gains for each beam are almost 9 dBi. This multibeam antenna takes the advantages of low loss, cost effective, compact size and ease of integration, which can be applied in 5G communication systems.

articleTitle: Microwave power transmission for multi-targeting antenna using time-reversal technology
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Time-Reversal (TR) technology is used in a Microwave Power Transmission (MPT) system with multiple unknown-position targets. In the TR-MPT system, the Time-Reversal Mirror (TRM) array receives detecting signals emitted from the targets and re-emits the time-reversed one convoluted with high energy electromagnetic waves, and then the electromagnetic wave energies are focused on the targets. Three cases with different target positions are studied. Compared to the energies received by the targets in a conventional MPT system, more energy can be received by the targets in the TR-MPT system. The results show that the TR technology can be used to improve the performance of a multi-target MPT system.

articleTitle: The shape synthesis of unit elements for transmitarray antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The synthesis of transmitarray unit elements that are shape optimized to give specified properties is described. This is in contrast to the use of elements of specified prior shape whose size is varied to adjust the element behavior.

articleTitle: Wide-band circularly polarized dielectric resonator antenna array
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broad-band circularly polarized aperture coupled rectangular dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) array is presented. Sequential phase feeding technique is employed to increase the bandwidth of circular polarization without compromising the impedance bandwidth. The 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 2 × 2 DRA array is about 38% using sequential phase feeding technique. In addition, a broad-band matching bandwidth of 46% is accomplished. The achieved maximum gain is 10.5 dB of the DRA array. Moreover, the radiation patterns are symmetrical around the broadside direction with side-lobe levels below -14 dB. A compact array size of square wavelength area has been accomplished and verified using two different simulation tools for X-band applications.

articleTitle: A high gain printed antenna with parabolic metal grid reflector based on SIW technology
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A printed parabolic antenna is proposed in this paper. The antenna is loaded with a parabolic cylinder reflector which is composed of a series of metal-via arrays in order to improve the gain of H-plane horn antenna based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW). The final simulation results by CST Microwave Studio indicate that this antenna has the effect of high gain, the reflection coefficient of the antenna in 36.04-36.35GHz is lower than -10dB, the gain is 13.12dBi at 36.2GHz. This type of antenna solves the difficulty in integrating reflector antenna.

articleTitle: Wide bandwidth cavity-backed dual-polarized vivaldi array antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A dual-polarized two-element Vivaldi array antenna recessed inside a lossless metallic cavity is presented. A novel approach based on properly integrating the array with a flared cavity is used to achieve a resonance-free ultra-wideband antenna with high gain, good impedance match, and low side lobe levels (SLLs)<;-25dB over more than 4:1 bandwidth. Designed antenna is characterized experimentally and computationally and high-quality far-field performance is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Offset-fed dielectric reflectarray antenna designs
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, we present two offset-fed dielectric reflectarray designs. Both reflectarrays feature broadband designs realized by using dielectric blocks backed by a PEC plane. One of these arrays uses a phase compensating flat lens to reduce the maximum permittivity of the dielectric blocks covering the PEC. We compare the results of both reflectarrays and list their benefits as compared to traditional reflectarrays that use resonant elements for their designs, which render them narrowband.

articleTitle: Isolation enhancement between two closely spaced circular patches using dgs
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a new Defected Ground Structure (DGS) to enhance the isolation between two closely spaced circular patches for wireless applications. The antennas are placed on a Roger substrate with a relative permittivity of 3 and thickness of 1.52 mm. Four arcs are slotted on the ground underneath the substrate to eliminated the mutual current interacting between the elements. An enhancement of 26 dB has been achieved with a separation of 0.05 λo at 4.8 GHz. The total realized gain at the resonance frequency after the isolation is 5.2 dB. The array is suitable for applications where compact circular patches array is suitable.

articleTitle: Parametric analysis of double-split ring resonator as a reflectarray unit cell
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This work presents a parametric analysis of double split ring resonator (DSRR) for linear polarized X-band reflectarray antennas. We performed the parametric analysis on the unit cell of the reflectarray antenna, where we investigate the effects of the outer radius, ring width, ring gap, periodicity, and polarization on the resonance frequency and phase of reflected signal. Using the results of the parametric analysis, we designed two unit cells that operate at 8 and 12.5 GHz, respectively. The simulation results show that the designed unit cells provide 360° phase difference range by using element rotation technique. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study that investigates the performance of DSRR structures as linearly polarized reflectarray elements.

articleTitle: Broadband complex permittivity measurement of paraffin films at 26 GHz–1 THz using time domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, we report complex permittivity measurement of thick paraffin films at the frequency range of 26 GHz-1 THz. Paraffin is a low loss dielectric polymer that exhibits a 15% volumetric change through its solid-liquid phase change. Unique electrical and mechanical properties of paraffin makes it an attractive phase change material for the development of millimeter wave (mmW) and terahertz (THz) reconfigurable RF components such as variable capacitors and antennas. We employ a free-space measurement technique using time domain spectroscopy (TDS). Complex permittivity of paraffin is characterized over the frequency range of 26 GHz-1 THz by using Debye relaxation model to extrapolate the measurement data for lower frequencies. Measured relative permittivity of paraffin is 2.26 and loss tangent is measured to be 1.57 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> at 26 GHz and 0.006 at 1 THz.

articleTitle: Unequally spaced linear antenna array synthesis using multi-objective cauchy mutated cat swarm optimization
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The process of synthesis of antenna array involves the simultaneous optimization of the conflict parameters such as peak sidelobe level (PSLL) and first null beamwidth (FNBW). In this paper, the multi-objective form of the newly developed Cauchy mutated cat swarm optimization (CMCSO) is developed and proposed to trade-off the PSLL and FNBW. A Pareto-optimal front containing all the compromised solutions is developed using a multi-objective (MO) form of CMCSO, traditional cat swarm optimization (CSO) and particle swarm optimization (PSO). Targeted compromised solutions may be chosen from the optimal Pareto front based on the application at hand. Numerical illustrations show that MO-CMCSO yields superior results as compared to MO-CSO and MO-PSO.

articleTitle: Design of a Ku-band 1-bit reconfigurable transmitarray with 16×16 slot coupled elements
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The design and simulations of a Ku-band 1-bit reconfigurable transmitarray is presented. The proposed element consists of two orthogonal H-shaped slots and a coupling microstrip transmission line. By controlling the two PIN diodes integrated on the transmission line, opposite ends of the receiving H-shaped slot are excited, thus achieving 1-bit quantized phase with 180° phase difference. The simulated insertion loss at both phase states is 1.6 dB. A 16×16 transmitarray with aperture size of 128 mm is designed and analyzed. Full-wave simulation results show a satisfactory performance with gain of 18.8 dBi and aperture efficiency of 23.0% at 12 GHz.

articleTitle: Bandwidth-enhancement of digital communication systems employing narrowband antennas: A novel electromagnetic OFDM approach
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A new approach to antenna system design is proposed achieving significant bandwidth enhancement without modifying the antenna's physical layout. By deploying a complete electromagnetic link impulse response incorporating full Tx/Rx antenna effects, a novel electromagnetic OFDM (EM OFDM) scheme is developed to implement wideband digital communication systems employing narrowband antennas. An example of two wire-antenna BPSK system demonstrated about %100-bandwidth increase with probability of error performance significantly better than the typical (no EM OFDM) case.

articleTitle: A novel electromagnetic band gap structures for two-element MIMO antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a novel electromagnetic band gap (EBG) structure is proposed to reduce the mutual coupling between two element MIMO antenna. The proposed array antennas consist of two rectangular patch antennas and three EBG structure units inserted between them on the substrate. The proposed MIMO antenna is designed on FR4-epoxy substrate with a thickness of 1.1mm, permittivity is 4.4 and loss tangent is 0.02. In this design, rectangular patch antenna using coaxial feed mode and the distance between the two antennas is 15mm, it ensures that the distance between the two antennas of the MIMO antenna is close and the space utilization is high. The mutual coupling of antenna in 2.45GHz is -14.5dB without EBG structure which mutual coupling effect is obvious. By inserted three EBG units between the two patches, the mutual coupling of antennas in 2.45GHz is reduced to -28.5dB. Thus, the proposed antenna array isolation greatly improved by use of the EBG structure. The proposed MIMO antenna can be used in a wireless local area network communication system.

articleTitle: Switchable quadri-polarization slot antenna using a single feed port
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a switchable slot antenna with four polarization states excited by a single port is proposed. The slot radiator is coplanar with a coplanar waveguide, which is excited by a microstrip line on the other side of the substrate. To demonstrate polarization diversity and achieve impedance matching for each state, the PIN diodes were used as the switching elements to select the particular feeding structure and the associated matching network. Experimental results show that this antenna can exhibit right-handed and left-hand circular polarizations, vertical and horizontal (linear) polarizations with measured gains of 1.89 dBi, 2.51 dBi, 2.08 dBi, and 2.62 dBi, respectively.
