abstract: This paper presents compact integrated designs of substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) filter and dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) and integration of SIW filter with DRA arrays, for millimeter-wave applications. Synthesis and optimization methods using equivalent circuit models are presented. EM simulation results for the integrated designs with a center frequency of 35.5 GHz are shown for validation.

articleTitle: One meter deployable reflectarray antenna for earth science radars
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper describes the development of a 1-m deployable reflectarray antenna which is designed to fit in a 6U (10×20×30cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) class CubeSats. It operates at 35.75 GHz for the measurement of atmospheric processes over a short, evolutionary timescale. It deploys into a 98.6 cm × 82.1cm flat reflector. This antenna provides a gain of 48.0 dBi and an aperture efficiency of 44%. It consists of a cassegrain reflectarray using 14 deployable panels, one fixed panel and a telescoping feed and subreflector.

articleTitle: A low profile, wideband and high gain beam-steering antenna for 5G mobile communication
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A low profile, wideband and high gain Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) Transmission Line (TL) Butler Matrix (BM) beamforming network (BFN) for beamforming and beam-steering applications at 28 GHz (5G) is presented in this paper. Four distinct beams steering between -50° to 50° with sidelobe and return-loss level below -10 dB are generated by connecting the proposed BFN to microstrip antennas forming a phased array antenna. The simulated and measured results are shown and discussed.

articleTitle: A compact circularly-polarized square slot antenna with enhanced axial-ratio bandwidth using metasurface
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A low-profile single-fed, wideband, circularly-polarized slot antenna is proposed. The antenna comprises a square slot fed by a U-shaped microstrip line which provides a wide impedance bandwidth. Wideband circular polarization is obtained by incorporating a metasurface consisting of a 9 × 9 lattice of periodic metal plates. It is shown that this metasurface generates additional resonances, lowers the axial ratio (AR) of the radiating structure, and enhances the radiation pattern stability at higher frequencies. The overall size of the antenna is only 28 mm × 28 mm (0.3 λo × 0.3 λo). The proposed antenna shows an impedance bandwidth from 2.6 GHz to 9 GHz (110.3%) for |S11| > -10 dB, and axial ratio bandwidth from 3.5 GHz to 6.1 GHz (54.1%) for AR > 3 dB. The antenna has a stable radiation pattern and a gain of greater than 3 dBi over the entire frequency band.

articleTitle: An ultrawideband tightly coupled antipodal Vivaldi antenna array for UHF-Ku band applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Designing a tightly coupled antipodal Vivaldi antenna (TC-AVA) array is proposed in this paper. With increased capacitive coupling effects of the overlapped end portions of adjacent flare-arms of AVA elements, the bandwidth of the TC-AVA array is effectively broadened by decreasing the lowest frequency about 69.5% compared with the single isolated element. The simulated results show that the proposed TC-AVA array operates over 0.51-18GHz band (35.3:1 bandwidth) for VSWR<;3.5 and possesses stable radiation patterns and nearly constant group delay in most frequencies. It is an excellent candidate for UHF-Ku band ultra-fast data-links and direction finding systems.

articleTitle: High efficiency rectifier for RF energy harvesting in the GSM band
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, a miniature RECtifying antENNA (rectenna) operating in the GSM band is designed and realized. The RF micro-generator consists of a simple rectifier circuit combined with a dipole antenna. The miniaturization of the circuit lies in avoiding the adaptation input filter and in optimizing the transmission lines by the gradient method search. The designed circuit is based on a Schenkel voltage doubler rectifier and Schottky diodes HSMS 2850 of AVAGO and is optimized through electromagnetic simulation software, Agilent ADS 2014 environment. Experimental results show an RF-DC conversion efficiency up to 40% with an output DC voltage of 1.8 V at 10 dBm of input power. A Wireless Power Transmission (WPT) experience demonstrates an average voltage of 22 mV over a distance of 3 m.

articleTitle: Circularly-polarized horn antennas for terahertz communication using differential-mode dispersion in hexagonal waveguides
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this work, we present a class of circularly polarized (CP) horns that are scalable to sub-mm-wave and terahertz bands. The presented design utilizes a hexagonal waveguide, that is hollow and can be easily fabricated in these bands, as opposed to traditionally used waveguide partitions. We demonstrate the proposed design using a WR-8 (90-140 GHz) horn showing 18 dBi gain with 37% 3dB axial-ratio (AR) bandwidth. Design-optimization, fabrication steps and measurement results are presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Design of broadband dual-polarized oval-shaped base station antennas for mobile systems
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper proposes a new design of wideband oval-shaped antenna with ±4° dipoles suitable for the base station of mobile communication systems. The designed antennas cover bands of 700-960 MHz (the lower band antenna) and 1700-2700 MHz (the upper band antenna) for cellular 2G/3G/LTE technologies. The design enjoys the advantages of stable directivity and beamwidth within frequency bands and a simple feeding structure with a compact size and low profile. The oval-shaped structure makes the antenna smaller in size than other polygon shapes. The antenna in the lower band has a beamwidth of 85.4°± 1.3° and directivity of 7.2±0.13 dBi with the reflection coefficient ≤ -17 dB and the isolation between the ports ≥ 19 dB while the antenna in the upper band has a beamwidth of 84.15°±3.9° and directivity of 6.94±0.38 dBi with the reflection coefficient ≤ -10.5 dB and the isolation between the ports ≥ 20.5dB. High cross polarization discrimination ratios were also achieved within the desired frequency bands.

articleTitle: Ultra-low profile tri-polarized antenna for WLAN/MIMO application
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a novel tri-orthogonal polarization antenna operating at 2.4 GHz with good prospective for WLAN and MIMO systems. The design is implemented by integrating dual polarized cross-slot antenna and zeroth-order resonant (ZOR) antenna. The total height of the antenna is 0.762 mm corresponding to 0.01λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> (where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> is the guide wavelength at 2.4 GHz). Linear horizontal dual-polarization and vertical polarization radiation patterns are obtained by using cross-polarized slot antennas and ZOR array antenna respectively. The broadside gain provided by the slot radiation is 5.3 dBi while the azimuthal average gain of the ZOR antenna is about 1.2 dBi.

articleTitle: Gain enhancement of suspended miniaturized antenna on high-loss paper substrate
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A configuration of antenna using flexible substrate for RF energy harvesting system working at GSM frequency 1800 MHz is presented. The suspended structure is used to surpass the high loss of the substrate. By taking advantage of the flexible properties, the process of miniaturization is achieved through folding the substrate into sections. The antenna prototypes were fabricated and measured. With the compact size of 0.36 λ × 0.33 λ × 0.03 λ, the measured gain is 5.3 dB, about 10 dB gain increase compared to conventional structure.

articleTitle: Broadband differentially-fed circularly polarized antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broadband differentially-fed circularly polarized (DFCP) antenna and a low-profile broadband DFCP antenna are proposed in this paper. Both antennas are made up of folded off-center-fed dipoles and are differentially-fed by two coaxial cables through a microstrip stub. It is shown that the DFCP antenna achieves a bandwidth of 44% (1.76-2.75 GHz) for differential reflection coefficient <;-15 dB and axial ratio (AR) <;3 dB. Due to the introduction of a broadband artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) surface, the overall antenna height of the low-profile broadband DFCP antenna is 0.125λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22GHz</sub> (where λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22GHz</sub> is the wavelength in free space at the frequency 2.2 GHz). Experimental results show that the low-profile DFCP antenna has a bandwidth of 54% (1.47-2.56 GHz) for differential reflection coefficient <;-15 dB and a bandwidth of 46.6% (1.68-2.75 GHz) for AR <;3 dB.

articleTitle: Broadband monostatic simultaneous transmit and receive reflector antenna system
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A broadband reflector antenna with monostatic simultaneous transmit and receive (STAR) capability is introduced. The proposed antenna operates over 4-8GHz with VSWR <; 2, gain > 21dBic (with a maximum gain of 28dBic @ 8GHz), and high isolation. A dual-polarized coaxial cavity antenna is designed and used as reflector feed. The monostatic STAR capability is achieved by the use of a simple beamformer network and circulators arranged to cancel any signal leakage from TX to RX paths leading to hypothetically infinite system isolation. Practically, the proposed system achieves isolation > 30dB limited by the imperfections of the used COTS components.

articleTitle: A low-cost mechanical beam scanning waveguide slot antenna array
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A low-cost mechanical beam scanning waveguide slot antenna array is introduced in this paper. A novel phase shifter using a circular arc mechanical structure is presented, which can achieve continuous phase shifter by changing the distance from the exciting locations to radiating antenna. An 8×8 elements array is simulated with perfect performances, verifying the design.

articleTitle: From optimization of near-field WPT systems to far-field antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A semidefinite relaxation-based optimization framework developed for near-field wireless power transfer systems is adopted for far-field applications. As shown via simulation results, the framework can be used to maximize gain by using optimal reactive loading as well as to iteratively optimize the geometry for self-resonant maximal-gain array antennas.

articleTitle: A dual-band notched ultra wideband microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A kind of dual-band notched ultra wideband microstrip antenna is presented in this paper. The reflectioncoefficient has goodnotched characteristics at rejection band of 3.3GHz~3.7GHz and 5.15GHz~5.85GHz by etching a complementary split ring in semicircular radiating patch. The stop bands cover WIMAX and WLAN frequency band. The designed antenna operates from 2.8GHzto12GHz. The gain is 2.3dB~6.3dB in operating band, while the gain is less than 0dB in rejection band. And the antenna shows good omnidirectional radiation patterns in H-plane in the working band.

articleTitle: A spiral antenna for amplitude-only direction finding
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A two-arm Archimedean spiral antenna which covers 1GHz to 23GHz is discussed. We describe the practical implementation of the antenna, report on the feed structure and show a simulation comparison study with a equiangular spiral regarding direction finding performance in an amplitude-only system.

articleTitle: Accuracy investigation of SFCW radar in human vital signs detection for subject's relative position
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the effects of different subject orientations, and multiple subjects in human vital sign detection using stepped frequency continuous wave (SFCW) radar are analyzed. The accuracy performance is validated with an electromagnetic scattering human ribcage model. Both of simulation and measurement results are demonstrated in this work.

articleTitle: Spatio-temporal modulated doppler cloak restores invisibility of moving cloaked objects
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this contribution, we report our results on the possibility of restoring the invisibility of cloaked objects in relativistic motion by using a spatio-temporal (ST-) modulated cover wrapped around or just in front of the object. It consists of an artificial dielectric whose refractive-index is modulated as a periodic function in both space and time, leading to a periodic profile of the refractive index that moves with a certain velocity. The periodicity of the spatial modulation and the modulation frequency are properly chosen in order to frequency modulate the propagating signal in the cover. We show that by properly choosing the modulation scheme and frequency of the ST-modulated cover, it is possible achieving a full compensation the Doppler frequency shift, restoring the operation frequency of the cloak and, thus, the invisibility of the object.

articleTitle: Antenna probes for power reception from deep tissues for wearable microwave thermometry
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The goal of the research presented in this paper is a design procedure for wearable antenna probes for monitoring internal body temperature using microwave radiometry. Receiving thermal black-body radiation from internal tissue layers is challenging as the human skin dominates the received power due to its high conductivity and permittivity. Therefore, a new design method is needed for probes that receive thermal power preferentially from deep tissue layers, while minimizing the contribution of surface tissues. The design method starts from reciprocity in the near-field, allowing simulations of volume loss power density to be used to predict black-body radiation. Several probes with superstrates are designed in order to maximize the volume loss power density in a specific buried layer. The experiments are performed in the 1.4-GHz quiet band, and temperature tracking is demonstrated and compared to thermocouple direct measurements on a skin-fat-muscle phantom.

articleTitle: A low-profile frequency reconfigurable metasurface patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper present a frequency reconfigurable antenna with metasurface. This antenna consisted of two substrates with the thickness of 1mm. Metasurface with tunable capacitors is placed on the top layer, while the microstrip feeding line and the ground plane are printed below the metasurface. The working frequencies of the proposed antenna are controlled by a single DC voltage applied on the varactors. By altering the capacity of the varactors, the working frequency of the proposed antenna can be shifted from 2.43 GHz to 3.31 GHz. Furthermore, the antenna maintains broadside radiation and has more than 5 dBi gain in all the operating bands.

articleTitle: Silicon micromachined high-contrast artificial dielectrics for millimeter-wave transformation optics antennas
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Transformation optics methods and gradient index electromagnetic structures rely upon spatially varied arbitrary permittivity. This, along with recent interest in millimeter-wave lens-based antennas demands high spatial resolution dielectric variation. Perforated media have been used to fabricate gradient index structures from microwaves to THz but are often limited in contrast. We show that by employing regular polygon unit-cells (hexagon, square, and triangle) on matched lattices we can realize very high contrast permittivity ranging from 0.1-1.0 of the background permittivity. Silicon micromachining (Bosch process) is performed on high resistivity Silicon wafers to achieve a minimum permittivity of 1.25 (10% of Silicon) in the WR28 waveguide band, specifically targeting the proposed 39GHz 5G communications band. The method is valid into the THz band.

articleTitle: Applications of magneto-dielectric materials in wearable antenna design
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper is focusing on suggesting realizing antennas using flexible Magneto-Dielectric (MD) materials for wearable applications. For proof of concept, different monopole antenna configurations are studied and their performances evaluated at 2.45 GHz. Monopole based MD antenna integrated a ground plane at a distance of 4 mm away from the antenna has showed a comparable performance to the monopole integrated flexible Artificial Magnetic Conductor (AMC) structure and a superior performance compared to the monopole based dielectric antenna. In addition, a study on the structural deformation of the proposed monopole configurations in terms of antenna bending in two perpendicular planes is presented. Results demonstrated the effectiveness of using flexible MD materials to stabilize antenna performance within the industrial, scientific, and medical ISM-2.45 GHz band.

articleTitle: A planar transmitting array system with a single tuning capacitor for uniform power transfer coverage
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents a new transmitting array system of magnetically-coupled resonance for uniform spatial wireless power transfer coverage. Unlike a conventional array system in which each resonant coil element has its own respective resonant tuning capacitor, the proposed array system consists of four identical resonant coil elements with only one common tuning capacitor. Four resonant coils are connected in two planar spiral patterns of number `8' to ensure right magnetic couplings with improved performances. The prototype is fabricated and tested. Both simulations and measurements show that the proposed array system can produce (i) easier tuning and higher power transfer efficiency and (ii) a more uniform transfer efficiency distribution in the intended wireless power cover region than the conventional array. The proposed array can be considered as a good candidate for developments of practical wireless power transfer systems for applications such as charging mobile devices.

articleTitle: Overview of human vital signs detection using radar techniques
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, we present an overview on the use of different radar types for vital signs detection. Our results using step frequency continuous wave radar for detecting heart rate and respiration rate and associated detection errors relative to reference measurements will be discussed in detail.

articleTitle: Rapid statistical analysis and tolerance-aware design of antennas by response feature surrogates
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: Fast statistical analysis of antenna structures using response features is addressed. Our approach exploits response surface approximations of suitably selected characteristic points of the antenna response. Taking advantage of close-to-linear dependence of the feature point coordinates on antenna geometry parameters allows for accurate yet cheap yield estimation. Extension of the technique for tolerance-aware design is also discussed. The approach is demonstrated using a dual-band patch antenna.

articleTitle: Design of UAV and ground station antennas for communications link budget improvement
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of two antennas aiming the improvement of the link budget between an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) and the ground station. The performance of the antennas is simulated using CST software tool and the simulation results are found to be in good agreement with the measurements. The UAV antenna presents 6 dBi of gain with an omni-directional coverage. The ground station antenna is a directional antenna based on a stacked configuration allowing an increase of the bandwidth while achieving a gain of 13.5 dBi. Both antennas operate at 1.335 GHz and a range of 50 Km is predicted when included in the communication system.

articleTitle: CPW ring wearable antenna on leather material for BAN applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: In this paper, the design, simulation and fabrication of a ring wearable antenna is presented for body-area-network (BAN) applications. A leather flexible textile material is used as substrate material. The dielectric constant ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> = 1.79, and loss tangent tanδ = 0.042 of the leather substrate are measured by using two different methods. This is a broad-band CPW-fed monopole antenna which is designed to operate over a frequency band between 1.5-6.5 GHz. This antenna is studied in both free-space and on-body environments. This antenna is fabricated using folded cupper and measured by Agilent 8719ES VNA.

articleTitle: Printed circularly polarized open loop antenna array for millimeter-wave applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A circularly polarized antenna element composed of two open loops is proposed. The concept of sequential rotation is demonstrated using the proposed element, which helps to broaden the axial ratio bandwidth to 16.4%. This antenna element can be used for wireless communications at 60 GHz.

articleTitle: High performance CRLH waveguide leaky-wave antenna with optimized sidelobe level
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A Ka-band high performance composite right/left-handed (CRLH) leaky-wave antenna (LWA) is designed and reported in this paper. This LWA is based on an air-filled CRLH waveguide with double ridge corrugations (DRCs). Meandering long slot is cut on the smooth broadwall of the CRLH waveguide to realize a tapered excitation distribution. The antenna synthesis method for this CRLH LWA is studied intensively. The designed CRLH LWA is simulated with the optimized sidelobe levels below -20 dB achieved for the radiation patterns in the operating band, which demonstrates the effectiveness of the antenna synthesis method for high performance CRLH LWAs.

articleTitle: Isoflux phased array design for cubesats
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: The optimization and design process for an isoflux phased array for Cubesats in low earth orbit (LEO) is presented. A genetic algorithm is used to create a multi-ring concentric circular phased array that creates a near-isoflux power pattern on the earth surface. At high operating frequencies, the array is small enough to fit on the 1U face of a Cubesat. Simple microstrip patch antennas are used for the array design for proof of concept, with full wave simulation demonstrating the array performance.

articleTitle: Wiener-Hopf formulation of the scattering by a stepped wedge
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: This paper presents the formulation and the procedure to get the solution of the scattering problem constituted by a PEC wedge connected to a PEC step structure. We formulate the problem in terms of generalized Wiener-Hopf equations (GWHEs) in spectral domain whose solution is obtained through Fredholm factorization with the help of circuital representations of the angular region and layered region.

articleTitle: Segmented helical antenna with reconfigurable polarization
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A novel polarization reconfigurable segmented helical antenna is explored. The antenna has two stable states, right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) state and left-hand polarization (LHCP) state. The sense of polarization of this antenna can be switched easily by mechanical rotation. The proposed antenna is analyzed using simulations and measurements.

articleTitle: Rectangular and circular arrays with independently controlled beamwidth and sidelobe level
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting
abstract: A simple method for the synthesis of rectangular and circular antenna arrays with independently specified beamwidth and sidelobe level is presented. It makes use of the Taylor one-parameter design method, and thus the resulting arrays have decaying sidelobes. Knowing that the array factor of the rectangular array is the product of the array factors of two linear arrays, the rectangular array is obtained by separately designing the two constituent linear arrays, each with the desired beamwidth and sidelobe level. On the other hand, an existing method can make the transformation between a a circular array and a virtual linear array. After relating the beamwidth of the circular array to that of the virtual linear array, this transformation method is used to synthesize a circular array with the wanted beamwidth and sidelobe level. Examples are given to validate the presented method for the two array types.
